A small pool of sauce surrounds the base of the chicken. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A single portion, balanced and appealing.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan.
Add sliced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add irregularly sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the pan. Turn to coat with sauce.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Kombucha-Brined Chicken with Broccoli Stem Pesto Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, set on a light reclaimed wood surface. The plate features a mindful, uncluttered composition. At the center, a mound of pasta, lightly coated in a vibrant green broccoli stem pesto, is interspersed with roasted zucchini half-moons, red bell pepper chunks, and halved cherry tomatoes, showcasing earthy tones of green, red, and orange. Beside the pasta, two thick, golden-brown chunks of kombucha-brined chicken are placed, revealing their tender, moist texture. A delicate, creamy white mozzarella sauce is drizzled artfully over the chicken and pasta, adding a subtle visual contrast. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh, dark green basil leaves, providing a natural pop of color. The overall presentation emphasizes natural textures and colors. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring soft, natural lighting, with a hint of an undyed linen napkin and a subtle green plant in the distance, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare chicken brine: Combine kombucha, salt, peppercorns, and rosemary in a bowl. Submerge chicken breasts in brine. Cover and refrigerate for 4-6 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Remove chicken from brine; pat dry thoroughly. Discard brine.

Sear chicken: Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to oven. Roast 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.

Prepare broccoli stem pesto: Peel tough outer layer from broccoli stems. Cut stems into 2 cm pieces. Blanch stem pieces in boiling water for 3 minutes. Drain and cool immediately in ice water. Drain well.
In a food processor, combine blanched broccoli stems, garlic, sunflower seeds, basil, nutritional yeast, and 50 ml olive oil. Process until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Roast vegetables: Cut zucchini into 1.5 cm half-moons. Cut bell pepper into 2 cm chunks. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss vegetables with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 15-20 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

Make mozzarella cream: Tear fresh mozzarella into small pieces. In a small saucepan over low heat, combine mozzarella and vegetable broth (or milk). Stir until mozzarella melts into a smooth, light cream. Season lightly with salt.
Assemble dish: In a large bowl, toss cooked pasta with broccoli stem pesto. Add roasted vegetables and gently combine. If too thick, add a tablespoon or two of reserved pasta water.
Slice chicken breasts into thick chunks. Do not fan out.
Plate pasta and vegetables. Arrange chicken chunks alongside. Drizzle mozzarella cream over chicken and pasta. Garnish with a few fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Boeuf Provençal aux Haricots Rouges et Pastis
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Boeuf Provençal aux Haricots Rouges et Pastis is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, positioned slightly off-center on a simple, light-toned wooden table. The rich, dark reddish-brown stew fills the bowl, leaving a clean white rim. Large, irregular chunks of slow-braised beef, tender and dark, are nestled among plump, dark red kidney beans. Softened pieces of diced onions, 1.5 cm thick carrot rounds, and 1.5 cm celery pieces are visible, coated in the glossy, aromatic sauce. The sauce has a moderate viscosity, clinging to the ingredients without being overly thick. A generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top, providing a vibrant color contrast. The setting is a modern bistro, with a clean white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the bowl. Simple, elegant silver cutlery rests on the table. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and deep colors. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere without distracting from the food. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a well-proportioned, inviting single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for soaking up the rich sauce.
Accompany with simple boiled potatoes or rice.

ingredients.name: Canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Carefully add Pastis. Let it simmer briefly for 1 minute.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Add drained and rinsed kidney beans. Simmer for another 10 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beer-Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty beer-braised chicken is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown seared chicken thigh, cooked to tender perfection, sits prominently amidst chunky, soft root vegetables – thick rounds of orange carrots and substantial cubes of off-white potatoes – all bathed in a rich, glossy, dark brown braising liquid. The sauce has a natural sheen, clinging to the ingredients. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a simple, functional garnish. The plating is casual, with components naturally overlapping and touching, evoking a comforting, home-cooked feel. A simple, everyday fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a relaxed family dinner atmosphere with minimal, natural background elements, such as a water glass or a simple bread basket, out of focus.

ingredients.name: Sweet wine (e.g., Marsala or Late Harvest)
Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into thick rounds

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Russet)
ingredients.quantity: 400 g, peeled and cut into large cubes

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Dredge chicken lightly in flour. Shake off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add chopped onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in dark beer, sweet wine, and dark rum. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in chicken stock. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in liquid. If not, add a little more stock.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 45 minutes.
Add potato cubes to the pot. Stir gently.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Potatoes should be fork-tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Beef and Broccoli Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of creamy garlic parmesan beef and broccoli pasta is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The fettuccine pasta forms the base, richly coated in a thick, velvety cream sauce. Scattered throughout are browned, bite-sized chunks of seared beef, showcasing their savory crust. Vibrant green broccoli florets are interspersed, retaining a slight crispness. A generous dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, melting slightly into the warm pasta. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a pop of color. The dish is arranged naturally, with components touching and overlapping, appearing as if just served from a family pot. The entire plate is visible, placed on a well-used dark wooden dining table. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate, and a casually folded cloth napkin is nearby. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Cut beef into 2.5cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside. Ensure beef reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Add broccoli florets to the pasta water during the last 3 minutes of cooking. Drain pasta and broccoli, reserving 100ml of pasta water.
Melt butter in the same large pan over medium heat. Add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Add cooked beef, pasta, and broccoli to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure beef is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Cheesy Macaroni Bake and Cucumber-Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single, inviting portion rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. A golden-brown, braised chicken thigh, with its skin crisped from searing, anchors the dish. Beside it, a generous scoop of creamy, golden-topped macaroni bake, its surface bubbly with melted cheese and a hint of browned crust, holds its shape. A hard-boiled egg half, its yolk a pale yellow, is nestled atop the macaroni bake. A vibrant side of diced red tomatoes and green cucumber, lightly dressed and glistening, provides a fresh counterpoint. Fresh green parsley is sprinkled over the salad. The elements are arranged organically, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin and standard European flatware are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the textures and colors of the dish, set against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: medium potatoes, cut into 2 cm wedges

instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.

Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Deglaze with beer, scraping up any browned bits. Add chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return chicken thighs to the pot. Bring to a simmer, then cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 170°C. Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and is very tender.

While chicken braises, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with 30 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and rosemary (if using). Spread in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown and tender.

Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside. In a medium saucepan, melt 50g butter over medium heat. Whisk in 50g flour to form a roux. Cook for 1-2 minutes. Gradually whisk in 500 ml milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar cheese and Dijon mustard until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Combine cooked macaroni with cheese sauce. Transfer to a medium oven-safe baking dish.
Place macaroni bake in the oven with the chicken (adjust oven rack if needed). Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until top is golden brown and bubbly.
In a medium bowl, combine diced cucumber and diced tomatoes. Drizzle with 30 ml extra virgin olive oil and 15 ml red wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.

Remove chicken from braising liquid. Discard thyme and bay leaf. Remove macaroni bake from oven. Place one braised chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of cheesy macaroni bake alongside. Add a serving of fresh cucumber-tomato salad. Garnish the macaroni bake with a hard-boiled egg half or quarter and sprinkle fresh parsley over the salad.
notes: For extra flavor, reduce the braising liquid after removing chicken to create a rich sauce.
Adjust cheese type in the macaroni bake to your preference; Gruyere or Fontina also work well.

recipes.recipe_name: Murgh Kari
recipes.visual_description: The Murgh Kari is presented in a deep, white ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, creamy orange-red sauce. Tender chicken chunks (3-4 cm) are generously coated in the vibrant sauce, with no fanning of meat. A swirl of fresh cream lightly streaks the surface, adding visual depth. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, freshly chopped coriander leaves, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl is placed on a simple, light wooden table surface. Beside the bowl, a piece of golden-brown naan bread is artfully folded, and a small, white side bowl holds fluffy basmati rice. A simple, dark grey cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the curry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fresh basmati rice.
Serve with warm naan bread or roti for scooping.
Accompany with a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or pickled onions.
instructions: Combine chicken chunks, yogurt, 10g ginger-garlic paste, 2g turmeric, 2g red chili powder, 5g coriander powder, 2g cumin powder, and salt in a bowl. Mix well. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or karahi over medium heat. Add finely diced onions. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add remaining 10g ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Reduce heat to low. Add remaining 3g turmeric, 3g red chili powder, 5g coriander powder, and 3g cumin powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes. Increase heat to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates from the mixture, about 8-10 minutes.
Add marinated chicken to the pot. Stir to coat. Cook for 5 minutes until chicken changes color.
Add 100 ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in garam masala and heavy cream. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Taste and adjust salt as needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander leaves.
traditional_techniques: Bhunao (Sautéing spices and aromatics until oil separates)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apple-Onion Relish and Roasted Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared pork chops, roasted rosemary potatoes, and apple-onion relish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pork chops are golden-brown with a seared crust, sliced into thick, moist medallions or presented as whole, substantial pieces. Roasted potato wedges are deep golden, with slightly crispy edges and a tender interior, piled neatly beside the pork. The apple-onion relish features caramelized onions and tender apple pieces, interspersed with vibrant diced tomatoes, creating a rich, slightly saucy texture. A fresh sprig of rosemary garnishes the dish, adding a touch of green. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table surface with a cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under natural, even lighting, suggesting a modern bistro ambiance with a subtly blurred background.
instructions: PREHEAT oven to 200°C.

WASH potatoes. CUT into 2.5 cm wedges or chunks. TOSS with 30ml olive oil, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. ROAST for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and tender. FLIP halfway through.
PAT pork chops dry with paper towels. SEASON generously with salt and pepper.
HEAT remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

SEAR pork chops for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. TRANSFER skillet to preheated oven. ROAST for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. REMOVE pork from skillet. REST on a cutting board, loosely tented with foil.
WHILE pork rests, ADD butter to the same skillet over medium heat. ADD sliced onion. SAUTÉ for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
CORE apples. CUT into 1.5 cm dice. ADD diced apples to the skillet. COOK for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
MINCE garlic. ADD minced garlic to the skillet. COOK for 1 minute until fragrant.
POUR in apple cider vinegar. DEGLAZE the pan, scraping up any browned bits. ADD chicken broth and chopped thyme. SIMMER for 3-5 minutes, allowing sauce to reduce slightly.
DICE tomatoes into 1 cm pieces. STIR diced tomatoes into the apple-onion mixture. COOK for 1-2 minutes until just heated through. SEASON relish with salt and pepper to taste.
SLICE rested pork chops into thick medallions, or serve whole if preferred. ARRANGE pork, roasted potatoes, and apple-onion relish on individual plates. GARNISH with a fresh rosemary sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow bomba rice, infused with saffron, is mounded slightly in the center, appearing moist and flavorful, not dry. Scattered throughout the rice are vibrant orange diced carrots and bright green peas. Nestled naturally within and on top of the rice are golden-brown, tender chunks of boneless chicken thigh, showcasing their seared exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and freshness. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, casual restaurant-style background that remains unobtrusive.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and carrots to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add bomba rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Potatoes with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of golden-brown potatoes and deeply caramelized onions fills a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The 2 cm cubed potatoes are tender inside with a slightly crisp exterior, showcasing a rich, reddish-orange hue from the smoked paprika. Dark, tender, thinly sliced onion strands are scattered throughout the rustic mound. A vibrant green sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. The dish sits on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. A small ceramic tapas bowl with aioli is placed beside the plate. A clean, folded cotton napkin rests to the left. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures. The background is a subtly blurred casual restaurant scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a side of aioli or a red pepper relish.
Pair with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Maris Piper or Yukon Gold)
Smoked Paprika (Pimentón de la Vera, sweet)

instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Thinly slice onions. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat.
Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Stir occasionally.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly. Do not burn.
Add cubed potatoes to the pan. Stir to coat potatoes with onion and paprika mixture.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes. Potatoes should be tender.
Uncover. Increase heat to medium-high. Cook until most liquid evaporates and potatoes are slightly crisp on edges.
Season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
traditional_techniques: Pimentón de la Vera (traditional smoked paprika use)

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef Ragu with Fermented Tomato Passata and Fresh Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Braised Beef Ragu with Fresh Tagliatelle is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic bowl. Long strands of al dente tagliatelle are generously coated in a rich, dark reddish-brown ragu, loosely piled in the center. Tender, pull-apart chunks of slow-braised beef are prominently visible within the pasta, showcasing their deep, caramelized edges. The sauce has a glossy texture, clinging beautifully to the pasta. A delicate sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft, natural light illuminating the dish, highlighting its rustic elegance. A simple, silver fork is placed beside the bowl. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread for dipping in the ragu.
A sprinkle of grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese is traditional.

ingredients.name: Sweet red wine (e.g., Marsala or Port)
Beef broth (homemade from bones if possible)

instructions: Pat beef chuck dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with sweet red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add fermented tomato passata, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Alternatively, transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F).
Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef into large chunks using two forks. Discard herb sprigs and bay leaf.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir to combine. Simmer sauce for another 15-20 minutes to thicken slightly.
Cook fresh tagliatelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to achieve desired consistency. Toss to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainable cooking. Beef bones or trimmings can be used to make homemade broth, reducing food waste.

Fermented tomato passata adds a unique depth of flavor and utilizes preservation techniques. If not available, regular passata can be used, but the fermented version enhances complexity and eco-consciousness.
Consider dehydrating any leftover tomato skins or pulp (from making your own passata or fermentation) to create a 'tomato dust' for garnish, further minimizing waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Potato & Rice Cakes with Lemon-Garlic Aioli
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents as a single serving of two golden-brown, pan-fried potato and rice cakes, each a thick, round patty. They are stacked slightly askew on a shallow, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Beneath the cakes lies a bed of creamy, pale white rice, its soft texture visible. A generous dollop of pale yellow lemon-garlic aioli rests beside the cakes, its smooth surface contrasting with the textured cakes and rice. A few vibrant green chive batons are scattered artfully over the aioli and cakes for a fresh pop of color. The plate is positioned on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly placed nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's textures and inviting warmth. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Prepare fermented potatoes: Wash and peel potatoes. Dice into 2 cm cubes. Dissolve 15g sea salt and 5g sugar in 1 liter filtered water to make brine. Place potato cubes in a clean jar. Pour brine over potatoes, ensuring full submersion. Seal jar loosely to allow gas release. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Bubbles indicate active fermentation. Drain potatoes when fermented.

Make lemon-garlic aioli: Peel and finely mince 2 cloves of garlic. Grate zest from the whole lemon. Squeeze 30ml lemon juice. In a bowl, whisk egg yolk with minced garlic, lemon zest, 15ml lemon juice, 2g sea salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Slowly drizzle in vegetable oil while continuously whisking until a thick emulsion forms. Adjust seasoning.

Cook creamy garlic rice: Peel and finely mince remaining 2 cloves of garlic. In a saucepan, combine brown rice, chicken stock, milk, and minced garlic. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30-35 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare potato cakes: Mash fermented potatoes thoroughly. Mix with 100g of the cooked creamy rice. Form mixture into 8 round, thick cakes, about 2 cm thick. Ensure they are firm.
Cook potato cakes: Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Carefully place potato cakes in the skillet. Pan-fry for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.

Plate the dish: Spoon creamy garlic rice onto each plate as a base. Arrange two pan-fried potato cakes on top of the rice. Dollop a generous amount of lemon-garlic aioli beside the cakes. Finely chop chives into small batons. Garnish the dish with chive batons. Serve immediately.
notes: Fermentation time for potatoes may vary based on ambient temperature. Taste test after 3 days; they should be tangy.
Ensure all lemon zest is used in the aioli for maximum flavor and zero-waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Avocado and Creamy Tuna Salad
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, hearty salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, indicative of home use. The salad is casually scooped onto a bed of crisp, green romaine lettuce leaves. The components are naturally mixed, showing flaked tuna, creamy avocado diced into 1 cm cubes, chopped egg pieces of 1 cm, and flecks of finely diced red onion and dill. The salad mound is generous but not overflowing, leaving some negative space on the plate's edge. Dominant colors are the pale pinkish-white of tuna, light green of avocado, yellow and white of egg, bright green of dill and lettuce, and hints of red from the onion. The salad has a soft, creamy texture from the mayonnaise and avocado, contrasted with the slight crunch of celery and the crispness of the lettuce bed. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded cotton kitchen towel in a neutral color is casually placed nearby. Lighting is warm and soft, as if from a kitchen window or overhead light, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. Everyday stainless steel forks are placed beside the plate. A hint of a blurred, lived-in kitchen background is visible.

ingredients.name: Lettuce leaves (e.g., romaine or butter lettuce)

instructions: Drain tuna well. Flake into a large bowl.
Peel and pit avocados. Dice into 1 cm cubes. Add to the bowl with tuna.
Peel hard-boiled eggs. Chop into 1 cm pieces. Add to the bowl.
Finely dice celery and red onion. Add to the bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and chopped dill.
Pour the dressing over the tuna mixture. Gently fold until all ingredients are coated.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately on fresh lettuce leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Cheesy Sauerkraut Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Cheesy Sauerkraut Gratin is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pork loin, cut into two thick, juicy medallions with a golden-brown crust, is placed slightly off-center. Beside the pork, a generous scoop of the bubbling, golden-brown cheesy sauerkraut gratin sits, its creamy texture visible. A rich, glossy, deep red-brown tomato-Worcestershire reduction is artfully drizzled over the pork and partially around the gratin. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the inviting textures and warm colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crisp green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
For the Gratin: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens. Remove from heat.
Stir in shredded cheddar cheese and diced American cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Gently fold in drained sauerkraut into the cheese sauce.
Transfer sauerkraut mixture to a 20x20 cm baking dish. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and golden brown on top.
For the Pork Loin: While gratin bakes, pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 70°C.
Remove pork from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing into thick medallions.
For the Tomato-Worcestershire Reduction: Drain excess fat from the skillet, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Add tomato paste to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute, stirring.

Deglaze with beef or vegetable broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce reduces and thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
notes: For best results, rinse sauerkraut well to reduce acidity.
Ensure pork loin rests adequately for maximum juiciness.
The gratin can be prepared ahead of time and reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto al Manzo Brasato e Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy, free-flowing Risotto al Manzo Brasato e Pomodoro is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a warm orange-red from the tomatoes, is studded with tender, irregular chunks of dark brown braised beef. The rice grains are plump and distinct, coated in a luscious, fluid sauce that pools slightly at the base of the bowl. A scattering of bright green, whole basil leaves provides a vibrant contrast, along with a light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese. The dish is centered on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded off-white linen napkin and classic silver flatware (fork and spoon) are placed to the side. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and inviting warmth. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual, inviting restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a 'primo piatto' or main course.
Offer extra grated Parmesan at the table.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for soaking up sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Season beef cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pot, scraping up browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and 500ml hot beef broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Once beef is tender, remove from pot. Shred or break into smaller chunks. Keep warm.
Strain braising liquid. Discard solids. Reserve liquid.
In a separate large, wide pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium heat.
Add Arborio rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges become translucent.
Add 100ml of the reserved braising liquid. Stir until absorbed.
Begin adding hot beef broth (and remaining braising liquid) one ladleful at a time, stirring continuously. Wait until liquid is almost absorbed before adding the next ladle.
Continue adding liquid and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute to emulsify (mantecare).
Gently fold in the shredded beef.
Serve immediately.
notes: The quality of San Marzano tomatoes significantly impacts flavor.
Stirring the risotto constantly is crucial for creamy texture.
Ensure beef broth is hot when adding to risotto to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Chicken with Fermented Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown confit chicken thigh, its skin slightly crisped, rests on a handcrafted, natural ceramic plate in an earthy tone. Beside it, a mound of fluffy brown rice is subtly flecked with finely minced fermented garlic, offering a delicate contrast. Adjacent to the rice, a vibrant pile of quick-pickled seasonal greens, such as thinly sliced kale or chard, provides a pop of fresh green and a hint of tang. The chicken is presented as a whole, succulent piece. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. A few sprigs of fresh chives or parsley are scattered over the dish for a touch of natural color. The setting features a light, textured wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural overhead lighting, creating an eco-conscious and inviting presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with reserved confit fat for dipping crusty bread
Compost all organic waste
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Place chicken in a deep oven-safe pot. Add chicken fat, bay leaves, thyme, and peppercorns. Ensure chicken is submerged.
Bake at 150°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until very tender. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Carefully remove chicken from fat. Strain fat and reserve for future use.
While chicken confits, rinse brown rice. Combine rice and 400 ml water in a pot. Bring to boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 40-45 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, 125 ml water, sugar, and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat.
Wash and chop seasonal greens into bite-sized pieces. Place in a heat-proof bowl. Pour hot pickling liquid over greens. Let stand 15 minutes, then drain.
Once rice is cooked, fluff with a fork. Stir in minced fermented garlic.
To serve, place a confit chicken thigh on a ceramic plate. Spoon a portion of fermented garlic rice beside it. Arrange a pile of quick-pickled greens next to the rice.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.
notes: Save chicken bones for stock
Compost vegetable scraps
Store excess confit fat for future cooking

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Chorizo Paella
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Chicken and Chorizo Paella is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, vibrant golden-yellow from saffron, forms a cohesive base with visible, distinct grains. Interspersed are tender, browned 3 cm chicken chunks and rich red 1 cm chorizo rounds. Diced red bell pepper and finely diced onion pieces add color and texture. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, and a bright yellow lemon wedge rests at the plate's edge. The presentation is organized but natural. The background features a rustic wooden table, with simple, elegant flatware and a small ceramic bowl for discarded lemon rind, all under soft, natural lighting, creating an authentic Spanish bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, offering extra lemon wedges for squeezing.
Traditionally enjoyed communally from a large paella pan, but individual portions are common in restaurant settings.
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine or sangria.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: 0.5 g, steeped in 60 ml hot water

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add chorizo to the pan. Cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice in the tomato mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Pour in hot chicken stock and saffron water. Stir gently once.
Bring to a simmer. Distribute ingredients evenly. Do not stir further.
Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is al dente.
Reduce heat to low. Continue cooking for 5-7 minutes, listening for a crackling sound to form the socarrat.
Remove from heat. Arrange cooked chorizo on top of the paella.
Cover pan with foil or a lid. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Pear and Cocoa Black Bean Soup
recipes.visual_description: The Savory Pear and Cocoa Black Bean Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, velvety dark brown color. The soup has a smooth yet slightly textured consistency, indicating a partial blend of the black beans and pears. A small dollop of pale white crema or plain yogurt sits elegantly off-center on the soup's surface, creating a visual contrast. A scattering of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh cilantro leaves is placed beside the crema, adding a pop of color. Toasted pepitas are sprinkled sparingly over the soup, providing a subtle textural element and a warm, earthy tone. The bowl is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a heavy, dark-toned wooden spoon. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the soup's depth and the freshness of the garnishes. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, focusing entirely on the plated dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping
Offer a side of pickled jalapeños

ingredients.name: Pears
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, ripe, peeled, cored, and roughly chopped

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped pears, black beans, and cocoa nibs. Pour in vegetable broth.
Bring soup to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup. Blend until desired consistency, leaving some texture if preferred.
In a small bowl, whisk whole wheat flour with 60 ml cold water to form a slurry.
Return soup to medium heat. Slowly whisk in the flour slurry. Stir constantly until soup thickens, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in honey. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro, a dollop of crema or yogurt, and toasted pepitas.
notes: This soup offers a unique balance of savory, sweet, and smoky notes.
The cocoa nibs provide a deep, earthy bitterness that complements the sweetness of the pear and honey.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet and savory elements common in mole-inspired dishes

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Cranberry Chili
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty chili fills a rustic ceramic bowl. The chili is thick, rich, and deep reddish-brown, with visible small, irregular chunks of browned ground beef, diced tomatoes, and kidney beans. Plump, dark red dried cranberries are scattered throughout, adding color and tartness. A generous mound of bright yellow, freshly shredded cheddar cheese melts slightly over the hot chili, creating a creamy contrast. A few fresh green cilantro leaves are casually sprinkled on top for a pop of color. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table, beside a simple, slightly mismatched ceramic plate and a casual cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, evoking a cozy family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cornbread or saltine crackers.
Offer hot sauce on the side for added heat.
instructions: Dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Brown, breaking it into small, irregular chunks. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in chili powder, ground cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes, drained and rinsed kidney beans, beef broth, and dried cranberries.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook for at least 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Cook longer for deeper flavor.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Grate the cheddar cheese. Serve hot, topped with shredded cheddar and fresh cilantro.
notes: For best flavor, let the chili simmer for at least an hour.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Penne alla Vodka
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Penne alla Vodka is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The penne pasta is coated evenly in a creamy, vibrant orange-red sauce, showcasing its smooth texture. Each short, ridged tube of penne is distinct. A sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests atop the pasta. Several fresh green basil leaves, some whole, some torn, are scattered over the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The pasta is arranged organically in the bowl, creating a slight mound in the center with moderate negative space around the edges. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the bowl. Natural, even light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the sauce's sheen. A fork is placed to the right of the bowl, ready for dining. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra grated Parmesan cheese
Offer a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in vodka. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Mix well.
Add cooked penne pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Stir in chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (for the onion and garlic base)

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Beer Rice Pot
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty chicken and beer rice is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, with its skin slightly crisp, rests atop a mound of rich, amber-hued rice. The rice is moist, not dry, and flecked with soft, diced orange carrots and translucent, diced onions. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a vibrant contrast. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, as if served directly from the pot to the plate. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, accompanied by a standard fork and knife and a casually folded linen napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors, set against a softly blurred background hinting at a cozy, lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in long-grain rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to lightly toast the rice.
Pour in dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add chicken broth and bay leaf. Bring back to a simmer.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture, ensuring they are partially submerged.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5-10 minutes.
Discard bay leaf. Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
This dish is designed for homely, comforting appeal, perfect for family meals.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pasta & Gnocchi with Fermented Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta and gnocchi is arranged organically on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Roasted carrot chunks provide warm orange accents. Vibrant green broccoli florets and julienned stems add freshness. The dish is unified by the golden-hued fermented carrot and bell pepper relish, lightly coating pasta and gnocchi. Small, irregular pieces of crispy, rendered ham are sprinkled sparingly. The natural palette includes creams, greens, oranges, and browns. Textures are soft gnocchi, al dente pasta, tender-crisp broccoli, charred roasted carrots, and crispy ham. Ingredients are casually tossed, creating a natural heap, leaving ample white space. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wooden surface. An undyed linen napkin is draped beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green foliage.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel carrots. Cut into 2cm chunks. Toss with 10ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook gnocchi according to package directions until they float. Remove with a slotted spoon.
In the same pot, cook pasta until al dente. Reserve 100ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, dice ham into small pieces. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced ham. Cook until crispy. Remove ham with a slotted spoon. Leave rendered fat in the pan.

Cut broccoli head into small florets. Julienne the broccoli stem. Add remaining 20ml olive oil to the skillet with ham fat. Add broccoli florets and julienned broccoli stem. Sauté 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Mince garlic. Add to the skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cooked gnocchi, pasta, roasted carrots, and fermented relish to the skillet. Stir gently to combine.
Add reserved pasta water or vegetable broth. Simmer 2-3 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Stir in crispy ham. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Stuffed Bell Peppers with Brown Rice and Lentils
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty stuffed bell peppers rests on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. One or two vibrant red and yellow bell pepper halves, slightly softened and gently charred at the edges from baking, are generously overfilled with a rich, savory brown rice and lentil mixture. The filling showcases the natural, earthy tones of brown rice, the subtle green of cooked lentils, and flecks of diced onion and bright red tomato. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is casual and natural, reflecting home-style plating with components touching. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a relaxed family dining area. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. The overall impression is one of comforting, expertly prepared home cooking, served simply and invitingly.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions until tender. Drain any excess water.
Rinse lentils. Boil lentils in 250 ml of vegetable broth until tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
Cut bell peppers in half lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Arrange pepper halves cut-side up in a baking dish.
Dice the yellow onion into small cubes. Mince garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, cooked brown rice, and cooked lentils. Mix well.
Season the filling with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.
Spoon the rice and lentil mixture evenly into each bell pepper half.
Pour the remaining 250 ml of vegetable broth into the bottom of the baking dish around the peppers.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until peppers are tender and the filling is heated through.
Garnish with remaining fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Blue Cheese Sauce and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, creamy blue cheese sauce, pale off-white with visible blue cheese flecks, is generously spooned over the chicken. Around the base of the chicken, an artful, natural arrangement of roasted, tender-crisp 2cm rustic carrot chunks and celery pieces, alongside earthy brown quartered cremini mushrooms, creates a vibrant, balanced composition. The colors are natural and appealing: golden chicken, orange carrots, pale green celery, deep brown mushrooms, and the creamy white sauce. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley adds a final pop of color. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard polished flatware, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting presentation in a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut carrots and celery into 2cm rustic pieces. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.

While vegetables roast, quarter the cremini mushrooms. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from skillet and set aside.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. In the same skillet, add butter and melt over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and rest on a cutting board.

In the same skillet, add minced garlic and minced chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and crumbled blue cheese. Simmer gently, stirring constantly, until cheese is melted and sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.

To serve, place a roasted chicken breast on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of blue cheese sauce over the chicken. Arrange roasted carrots, celery, and sautéed mushrooms artfully around the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Fermented Garlic Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of braised chicken thigh rests centrally on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The chicken, deep golden-brown from searing and braising, is presented as a whole, un-sliced piece, showcasing its tender texture. It is nestled amongst a rich, glossy ragout of mixed mushrooms and diced vegetables. The mushrooms, in varying earthy tones of brown and grey, retain their rustic shapes. The sauce is a deep, inviting brown, clinging to the chicken and vegetables. A light scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley or celery leaves provides a pop of natural color and freshness. The plate sits on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a soft beige tone is casually folded to one side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the natural colors and textures of the dish. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green foliage from a distant plant. The overall composition is simple, unforced, and highlights the dish's inherent beauty and sustainable ethos.

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster)
ingredients.quantity: 400g, cleaned, larger ones halved or quartered

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley or celery leaves, chopped

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add chopped fermented garlic and mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Return chicken to the pot, skin-side up. Add chicken broth, thyme, and rosemary. Liquid should come halfway up the chicken.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pot. Set aside. Cover loosely with foil to keep warm.
Place pot back on stovetop over medium-high heat. Reduce sauce for 8-10 minutes until slightly thickened. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Discard herb sprigs. Serve chicken with mushroom ragout. Garnish with fresh parsley or celery leaves.
notes: To minimize waste, use chicken bones and vegetable scraps (carrot peels, celery ends, onion skins) to make homemade chicken broth for this recipe.

Fermented garlic can be prepared by submerging peeled garlic cloves in a 2% brine solution (20g salt per 1 liter water) and allowing it to ferment at room temperature for 1-2 weeks. This enhances flavor and preserves the garlic.
Source seasonal and local mushrooms for best flavor and reduced environmental impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken & Mushroom Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A generous square portion of Savory Chicken & Mushroom Bread Pudding sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pudding has a rich, golden-brown crust on top, showing slightly crisp edges and visible pieces of deeply caramelized mushrooms and golden-seared chicken chunks peeking through. The interior, revealed by the clean cut, is moist and tender, showcasing soft bread cubes bound by a creamy, savory custard, interspersed with vibrant green specks of fresh herbs and melted Gruyere cheese. A light scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual, professional restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish with butter.
Cube stale sourdough bread into 2-3 cm pieces. Set aside.
Dice yellow onion. Mince garlic. Slice cremini mushrooms thinly.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breast. Sear chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a plate. Cool slightly. Shred or cut chicken into 2 cm chunks. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

Add 30 g butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and brown. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, chicken stock, salt, and pepper until well combined.

Add cubed bread, shredded chicken, sautéed mushroom mixture, shredded Gruyere, chopped thyme, and half of the chopped parsley to the egg mixture. Gently fold until bread is evenly coated and ingredients are distributed.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish. Press gently to ensure all bread is submerged in liquid.
Bake 35-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Cut into 4 equal portions. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb Roasted Chicken with Lemon Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, perfectly roasted bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh positioned slightly off-center. The chicken skin is a rich, glossy golden-brown, with visible crisp texture. Adjacent to the chicken, a generous portion of golden-hued potato wedges are arranged organically, some displaying crispy edges and others a tender interior. Interspersed among the chicken and potatoes are a few roasted lemon wedges, their edges slightly caramelized. A light sheen of pan juices glazes the bottom of the plate, adding moisture and depth. The dish is garnished simply with fresh green parsley leaves, scattered lightly over the chicken and potatoes, providing a vibrant color contrast. The overall presentation is inviting and rustic yet refined, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the food's natural colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side salad of cucumber, tomato, and red onion dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm wedges
lemons, 1 zested and juiced, 1 cut into wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine 30ml olive oil, lemon zest, minced garlic, chopped fresh rosemary, chopped fresh oregano, smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon salt, and black pepper.
Add chicken thighs to the bowl. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 20 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
In another large bowl, toss potato wedges with remaining 30ml olive oil, dried oregano, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and the juice of one lemon.
Arrange chicken thighs in a single layer on a large baking tray or roasting pan.
Scatter potato wedges around the chicken. Add lemon wedges to the pan.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Pour chicken stock into the pan. Stir potatoes gently.
Continue roasting for another 25-35 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, internal temperature reaches 75°C, and potatoes are tender and browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sausage and Shrimp Pasta with Creamy Paprika Sauce and Apple-Blue Cheese Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Sausage and Shrimp Pasta is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Rigatoni pasta, coated in a creamy, vibrant orange-red paprika tomato sauce, forms the base. Seared sausage chunks, approximately 2-3cm, and whole pink shrimp rest naturally atop the pasta. Bright green chopped fresh dill sprinkles the dish. Beside the pasta, a small cluster of golden-brown roasted potato cubes, 2cm, are neatly arranged. A modest portion of the crisp apple-blue cheese salad, with diced apple and cucumber amidst mixed greens and blue cheese crumbles, is presented in a small white ramekin. The plate sits on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware complete the presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato cubes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden brown.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, heat 10ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. If using bulk sausage, break it into 2-3cm chunks. If using links, slice into 2-3cm thick pieces. Add sausage to the skillet. Sear until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove sausage from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 5ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.

Stir in smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Stir in cream cheese until fully melted and sauce is smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.

In the same skillet, increase heat to medium-high. Add shrimp. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and cooked through. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove shrimp and set aside.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat. Stir in half of the chopped fresh dill and the cooked sausage chunks.

For the salad, whisk together white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens, diced apple, and diced cucumber. Just before serving, add crumbled blue cheese and toss with dressing.
Serve pasta with sauce, sausage, and shrimp. Garnish with remaining fresh dill. Serve roasted potato cubes and the apple-blue cheese salad alongside.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Corn Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests on a bed of vibrant yellow corn gratin with diced red bell pepper. The gratin features a bubbling, golden-brown crust of melted cheddar and Monterey Jack cheese. A light sprinkle of fresh green cilantro adorns the chicken and gratin, providing a fresh contrast. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly seared exterior. The dish is arranged on a round white porcelain plate on a simple wooden table surface. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. The chicken is whole, bell pepper and onion are diced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm tortillas
Serve with a side of black beans
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer chicken to a plate. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion and red bell pepper. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in corn kernels, chicken broth, heavy cream, and hot sauce. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Stir in 150g of shredded cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Nestle seared chicken breasts into the corn mixture in the skillet.
Top chicken and corn with remaining 50g shredded cheese.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature and cheese is bubbly and golden.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: This dish can be prepared ahead of time and baked just before serving.
Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Pork and Potato Stew
recipes.special_requests: mediterranean cuisine, without oven, without broth and wine, made with multicooker
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty Mediterranean Pork and Potato Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly uneven, natural glaze. Thick chunks of seared pork, approximately 3-4 cm cubes, are nestled among tender 3 cm potato chunks. The rich, ruddy red tomato base, infused with dried oregano and thyme, coats the ingredients. Dark, briny Kalamata olives are scattered throughout, adding visual contrast. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a final pop of color. The stew has a comforting, slightly rustic texture. It is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, off-white linen napkin and a plain metal spoon beside the bowl. Natural, warm lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3-4 cm cubes.
Peel potatoes and cut into 3 cm chunks.
Chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in the multicooker on 'Sauté' mode.
Sear pork cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork from the multicooker.
Add chopped onion to the multicooker. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return pork to the multicooker. Add chopped tomatoes, pitted Kalamata olives, dried oregano, dried thyme, and water.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Close the multicooker lid. Set to 'Pressure Cook' or 'Stew' mode for 25 minutes.
Once cooking is complete, perform a quick pressure release.
Open the lid. Add potato chunks to the multicooker. Stir gently to combine.
Close the lid. Set to 'Pressure Cook' or 'Stew' mode for another 10-12 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Perform a quick pressure release. Open the lid.
Stir the stew. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Ham, Potato, and Mushroom Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single rectangular portion of golden-brown, bubbly gratin sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin's surface is caramelized and rich, revealing hints of melted cheese and a creamy interior. Thinly sliced potatoes form distinct layers, interspersed with savory chunks of pan-seared ham, earthy sliced mushrooms, and diced ripe tomatoes. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the top for a vibrant green accent. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware placed alongside. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors. The background is a subtly blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Accompany with crusty baguette slices.
