Surrounding the chicken are vibrantly colored roasted elements: plump, burst cherry tomatoes in shades of red, dark purple-black Kalamata olives, and translucent yellow roasted lemon slices. A delicate drizzle of the savory pan sauce subtly pools around the ingredients. A fresh sprig of rosemary or thyme rests beside the chicken, adding a touch of green and aromatic appeal. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, all under natural, even lighting to enhance the dish's natural colors and textures. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of couscous or orzo pasta.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.

Add cherry tomatoes, pitted Kalamata olives, lemon slices, smashed garlic cloves, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs to the skillet around the chicken. Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over vegetables.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove skillet from oven. Transfer chicken and vegetables to a platter. Tent with foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Pour chicken broth into skillet. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly reduces.
Serve chicken with roasted vegetables and pan sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken skin is very dry before searing to achieve maximum crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Spicy Tomato and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown, braised chicken thigh rests centrally on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, left whole, showcases its tender texture and a rich, deep red tomato sauce generously coats it. Visible within the rustic sauce are soft, vibrant red tomato chunks, translucent slices of garlic, and delicate slivers of red chili, offering subtle flecks of green from fresh basil leaves scattered atop. The dish maintains moderate negative space, presented in an organic, flowing arrangement. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve over creamy polenta
Serve with a side of simple pasta
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large braising pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add thinly sliced garlic and finely sliced chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the pan bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove lid for the last 10 minutes to allow sauce to thicken slightly, if desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom, Fruit, and Gherkin Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, displaying a vibrant mix of colors and textures. Tender, golden-brown sautéed mushroom chunks are combined with crisp diced green apple, sunny yellow diced pineapple, soft orange diced peach, and deep red halved grapes. Thinly sliced red onion adds sharp contrast. Quartered cherry tomatoes provide red bursts, and sliced gherkin rounds offer a pale green and white element. A light, glossy lime-dill dressing coats all ingredients. Components are arranged organically, with moderate negative space. Fresh dill sprigs garnish the top. The setting includes a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh, modern bistro presentation.
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add quartered mushrooms. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool.

Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, soy sauce, Dijon mustard, and chopped fresh dill. Slowly drizzle in 4 tbsp olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or a pinch of sugar if desired.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled sautéed mushrooms, thinly sliced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, diced apple, diced pineapple, diced peach, halved red grapes, and sliced gherkins.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to ensure all components are evenly coated.
Divide the salad among four plates. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Onion & Apple Tatin with Beer Caramel
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of inverted Tatin rests centrally on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate. The Tatin is a golden-brown disc, approximately 10 cm in diameter, showcasing deeply caramelized, tender onion rings and soft apple wedges. The pastry base, a whole wheat shortcrust, is a light golden hue, crisp yet yielding. A glossy, deep amber beer caramel glaze coats the Tatin's surface, reflecting the soft natural light. Scattered artfully beside the Tatin are a few pieces of transparent, amber-hued candied apple peels and small, vibrant green candied pickled jalapeno slices, offering a textural contrast and subtle color pop. The plate has ample negative space, emphasizing the dish's minimalistic elegance. It is presented on a light reclaimed wood surface with an undyed linen napkin and subtle green foliage in the background, reinforcing the sustainable theme.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Onions: Thinly slice 2 large sweet onions. In a clean jar, combine 200ml water, 5g sea salt, and 10ml apple cider vinegar. Add onion slices, ensuring they are fully submerged. Cover loosely and ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly tangy. Drain well before use.

Make Shortcrust Pastry: In a bowl, combine 150g whole wheat flour and 75g diced cold vegan butter. Rub butter into flour until crumbly. Add 30-45ml cold water, a tablespoon at a time, mixing until dough forms. Knead briefly. Form into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Prepare Candied Garnish: Peel 2 apples, reserving peels. Thinly slice 2-3 pickled jalapeno chilies. In a small saucepan, combine 100ml water, 20ml maple syrup, and 1 whole chipotle chile. Bring to a simmer. Add apple peels and jalapeno slices. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender and translucent. Remove chipotle. Drain peels and jalapenos, spreading on parchment paper to dry slightly.

Caramelize Onions & Apples: Preheat oven to 180°C. In an oven-safe, non-stick pan (approx. 20cm diameter), melt 20g vegan butter over medium-low heat. Add drained fermented onions. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very soft. Add 30g brown sugar and 30ml maple syrup. Cook 5 more minutes until syrupy. Remove from heat.
Assemble Tatin: Slice 2 apples into 1cm thick wedges. Arrange apple wedges decoratively over the caramelized onions in the pan.
Add Beer Glaze: Pour 150ml dark beer into the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add Pastry: Roll out chilled pastry into a circle slightly larger than the pan. Place pastry over the apples and onions, tucking edges down around the fruit.
Bake Tatin: Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and crisp.
Serve: Carefully invert the Tatin onto a serving plate. Allow to cool slightly. Garnish with the prepared candied apple peels and candied pickled jalapeno slices. Serve warm.
notes: Use sweet onions like Vidalia or Walla Walla for best caramelization.
A brown ale or porter works well for the beer caramel.
The fermentation time for onions can vary; taste after 2 days for desired tang.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Tomato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of hearty beef and tomato stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim. The stew is rich and thick, showcasing large, tender chunks of braised beef, diced potatoes, and round slices of carrots. The beef is dark brown from searing, contrasting with the vibrant red-orange of the tomato-based sauce. The potatoes are soft and slightly starchy, while the carrots retain a gentle bite. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a fresh counterpoint. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. Next to it, a simple cloth napkin is casually placed, along with a sturdy metal spoon. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3 cm cubes
Potatoes, medium, peeled, cut into 2 cm chunks
Carrots, medium, peeled, cut into 1.5 cm thick rounds

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Toss beef with flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add potato chunks and carrot rounds. Stir well.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef and vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra flavor, deglaze the pot with a splash of red wine after searing the beef and before adding onions.
This stew freezes well. Store in airtight containers for up to 3 months.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Biryani is presented in a wide, white porcelain bowl on a rustic wooden table. The long-grain basmati rice shows distinct white and saffron-stained yellow grains. Three large, bone-in chicken chunks and two golden-crusted potato halves are arranged within the rice mound. Diced orange carrots provide bright accents. The dish is topped with a generous scatter of dark, crispy caramelized onion strands and whole toasted golden cashews. A sprig of fresh cilantro sits on top. The background includes a clean cotton napkin and a small terracotta bowl of yogurt raita. Natural side lighting emphasizes the steam rising and the fluffy texture of the rice. The composition is balanced with clean margins.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chilled cucumber raita
Accompany with spicy lime pickle
Eat using the fingers of the right hand for traditional experience

ingredients.name: Saffron threads soaked in 30ml warm milk

instructions: Marinate chicken chunks with yogurt, ginger, garlic, turmeric, and salt for 60 minutes.
Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 30 minutes.
Boil 2 liters of salted water. Add rice. Cook until 70% tender. Drain and set aside.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot. Fry cashews until golden. Remove and set aside.
Fry onions in the same ghee until deep brown. Remove half for garnish.
Add potatoes and carrots to the pot. Sear for 5 minutes until browned.
Add dried chilis and marinated chicken. Cook over medium heat until chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and garam masala. Cook for 5 minutes.
Spread par-boiled rice evenly over the chicken and vegetable base.
Drizzle saffron milk over the rice. Top with reserved fried onions.
Cover pot with a tight lid. Cook on very low heat for 20 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently before serving. Garnish with toasted cashews.
notes: Use aged basmati rice for better grain separation
Ensure the pot lid is airtight to trap steam during the final stage

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of pan-seared chicken breast rests centrally on a round, rustic ceramic plate. The chicken, golden-brown with a slightly crusted exterior, is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. It is generously draped with a thick, creamy mushroom sauce. The sauce is rich with browned, irregularly sliced cremini mushrooms and finely diced onions. A vibrant sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh parsley adds a natural green contrast. The components touch and overlap naturally, creating an inviting, home-style appearance. The dish is set on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple ceramic side plate and a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere. Colors are natural: golden chicken, earthy brown mushrooms, creamy white sauce, and green parsley.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side. Cook until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet.
Add diced onion. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Return cooked chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Heat through for 1-2 minutes until chicken is warmed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Mole Poblano con Arroz Rojo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally featuring two bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, deeply coated in a rich, velvety mole poblano sauce. The chicken, cooked to tender perfection, exhibits a dark, glossy, reddish-brown hue from the mole. A generous mound of vibrant, reddish-orange Arroz Rojo, fluffy and perfectly cooked, sits beside the chicken, speckled with finely diced onion. The plate is garnished simply yet authentically: a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds over the mole, a fresh lime wedge, and a small cluster of finely chopped white onion. A cotton napkin is placed to the side on a simple wooden table. Natural, even lighting highlights the food’s textures and colors. A traditional Mexican ceramic bowl for accompaniments completes the modern bistro setting. The composition is balanced, showcasing a refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Lime wedges
Finely chopped white onion
Toasted sesame seeds

ingredients.name: Chicken broth
ingredients.quantity: 1.5 litres (1 litre for mole, 500 ml for rice)

instructions: Prepare chiles: Remove stems and seeds from ancho, mulato, and pasilla chiles. Lightly toast chiles on a dry comal or pan until fragrant. Rehydrate in hot water for 20 minutes.
Toast nuts, seeds, and spices: In a dry pan, toast sesame seeds, almonds, peanuts, cinnamon stick, whole cloves, star anise, coriander seeds, and cumin. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Heat 15 ml lard/oil in a pan. Sauté 1 medium chopped onion, 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 medium tomatoes, and 2 medium tomatillos until softened. Add dried thyme and Mexican oregano.

Blend mole ingredients: Drain rehydrated chiles. Combine chiles, toasted nuts, seeds, spices, sautéed aromatics, stale bread/tortilla, and 250 ml chicken broth in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing solids.

Cook mole sauce: Heat 30 ml lard/oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour in the strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 15-20 minutes until it darkens and thickens significantly.

Add chocolate and broth: Stir in dark chocolate until melted. Gradually add remaining 750 ml chicken broth, stirring until smooth. Season with salt and optional sugar. Simmer mole gently for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook chicken: Season chicken thighs with salt. Heat 15 ml lard/oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Flip and sear other side.
Finish chicken in mole: Add seared chicken to the simmering mole sauce. Ensure chicken is submerged. Simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Prepare arroz rojo: Heat 15 ml oil in a medium saucepan. Sauté 1/2 small diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves until fragrant. Add 300 g rinsed long-grain rice. Sauté until lightly toasted.
Add tomato and broth to rice: Stir in 200 ml tomato puree. Add 500 ml chicken broth. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 18 minutes. Let rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
traditional_techniques: Fritura de Mole (Frying the Mole Paste)

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Green Bean Salad with Honey Mustard Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant and textural medley. Tender sliced potatoes form the base, topped with bright green bean pieces, crisp 1cm diced cucumber, finely 0.5cm diced carrots, and julienned kohlrabi. Halved cherry tomatoes add pops of red, while chopped hard-boiled egg pieces contribute creamy yellow. A creamy honey-mustard vinaigrette lightly coats all components. Freshly chopped parsley, toasted sunflower seeds, and chia seeds are scattered over the top, adding a rustic garnish and crunch. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting, creating an inviting bistro ambiance.
instructions: Scrub potatoes. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain. Let cool slightly. Slice into 1.5cm thick rounds or quarters.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain. Plunge into ice water. Drain well. Cut into 2cm pieces.
Dice cucumber into 1cm cubes. Finely dice carrot into 0.5cm cubes. Peel kohlrabi and julienne.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Chop hard-boiled eggs. Chop fresh parsley.
Lightly toast sunflower seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes. Set aside.
For the dressing, whisk together minced garlic, Dijon mustard, honey, red wine vinegar, mayonnaise, salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika in a small bowl. Slowly whisk in olive oil until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine sliced potatoes, green bean pieces, diced cucumber, diced carrot, julienned kohlrabi, halved cherry tomatoes, and chopped hard-boiled eggs.
Pour dressing over the salad. Gently toss to coat all ingredients. Stir in chopped parsley, toasted sunflower seeds, and chia seeds.
Serve immediately or chill for 30 minutes for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in an authentic shallow ceramic tagine base on a rustic wooden table. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are positioned centrally, featuring golden-brown rendered skin coated in a thick, vibrant yellow saffron and turmeric sauce. The sauce contains visible softened diced onions. Scattered around the chicken are bright green whole cracked olives and thin yellow strips of preserved lemon peel. A cinnamon stick rests to the side of the meat. The dish is garnished with a generous amount of roughly chopped emerald-green cilantro and parsley. A side bowl of fluffy steamed couscous and a clean white cotton napkin are placed nearby. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the glossy texture of the braising liquid.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm khobz or crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a side of steamed couscous
Serve with a traditional Moroccan mint tea

ingredients.name: Preserved lemon, peel only, sliced into strips

instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Turn chicken and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot.
Sauté onions for 8 minutes until translucent and soft.
Stir in garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, and saffron.
Cook spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot with the cinnamon stick.
Pour in chicken stock until chicken is half-submerged.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 35 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add preserved lemon strips and olives.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in cilantro and parsley before serving.
notes: Rinse preserved lemons under cold water to remove excess salt before slicing.
Use a diffuser if cooking in a clay tagine on a gas stove to prevent cracking.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Garlic Shrimp Scampi with Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Lemon Garlic Shrimp Scampi with Linguine is presented on a round, white porcelain dinner plate. The linguine is neatly twirled into a moderate, elegant mound at the center. Around the base and nestled atop the pasta are several plump, pan-seared shrimp, cooked to a vibrant pink-orange hue, showcasing their natural curvature. A light, glossy lemon-garlic sauce coats the pasta and shrimp, reflecting the ambient light. Bright green flecks of finely chopped fresh parsley are scattered generously over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A small wedge of fresh lemon rests on the side of the plate. The composition is clean and balanced, with appropriate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a crisp green salad.
instructions: Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add shrimp to skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Cook 1-2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd. Remove shrimp from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add lemon juice and reserved pasta water to skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add cooked linguine to skillet. Toss to coat pasta in sauce. Return shrimp to skillet.
Add chopped parsley. Toss gently to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken and Bean Chili
recipes.visual_description: A hearty serving of Beer-Braised Chicken and Bean Chili fills a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The chili is deep reddish-brown, thick with tender shredded chicken, soft kidney beans, and diced tomatoes. Bright orange shredded sharp cheddar cheese melts generously over the top. A dollop of cool white sour cream is placed off-center. Fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro garnishes the dish. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin lies beside it. In the background, blurred, a few golden-brown cornbread wedges sit on a small rustic board. Natural, even lighting illuminates the comforting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cornbread.
Offer additional shredded cheddar, sour cream, and chopped green onions as toppings.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and minced jalapeno (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in dark beer and Worcestershire sauce. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Return seared chicken thighs to the pot.
Bring chili to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and easily shreddable.
Remove chicken from pot. Shred chicken using two forks. Return shredded chicken to the pot.
Add rinsed and drained kidney beans to the chili. Stir well.
Simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes, allowing chili to thicken. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Confit White Bean Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Garlic Confit White Bean Soup is presented in a clean, wide white porcelain bowl. The soup, a smooth, pale beige, has a luxurious, velvety texture, with a few whole, tender white beans visible. A generous drizzle of golden-green garlic confit oil swirls on the surface, creating an inviting sheen. It is garnished simply with a light scattering of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese and a delicate, vibrant green sprig of fresh rosemary, placed artfully near the rim. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a slice of rustic, crusty bread. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's comforting warmth and refined simplicity. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting, maintaining focus on the elegantly presented dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Prepare garlic confit: Peel garlic cloves. Place in small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Cook over very low heat until garlic is tender and golden, about 25-30 minutes. Do not brown.
Remove garlic from oil. Reserve oil for later use.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery into small, uniform pieces.
Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of the reserved garlic confit oil.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add reserved garlic confit cloves, rinsed and drained white beans, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Remove half of the soup from the pot. Blend until smooth using an immersion blender or standard blender. Return blended soup to the pot.
Add fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs to the soup. Simmer for 5 more minutes.
Remove herb sprigs. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Drizzle with a little more garlic confit oil. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and a small fresh herb sprig.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Gratin Dauphinois
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of golden-brown Poulet Gratin Dauphinois occupies the center, showcasing a rich, bubbly, caramelized Gruyère crust. The top layer of potatoes is slightly crisp, revealing soft, creamy potato slices beneath. Peeking from within the gratin are tender, roasted chicken thigh chunks, their surfaces lightly browned from searing, contrasting with the creamy white potatoes. The potatoes are uniformly thin, forming neat, overlapping layers. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green thyme leaves garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. The gratin is served warm, with steam subtly rising. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing the gratin to be the focal point. The table setting features a simple wooden surface, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its comforting textures and warm tones.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette to cut through the richness.
Accompany with crusty baguette slices for dipping into the creamy sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice potatoes thinly, about 2-3 mm thick. Use a mandoline for even slices.
Rub chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and a little thyme. Sear chicken in a hot pan with cooking oil until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Set aside.
Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in cream and milk. Add a pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer. Remove from heat.
Add sliced potatoes to the cream mixture. Stir to coat thoroughly.
Arrange a layer of potatoes in a large gratin dish (approx. 20x30 cm).
Place seared chicken thighs over the potato layer.
Cover chicken with remaining potatoes, ensuring even distribution.
Pour remaining cream mixture over potatoes.
Sprinkle grated Gruyère evenly over the top.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly. Insert a knife to check potato tenderness. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C.
Let gratin rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: For best results, use a mandoline to slice potatoes uniformly.
Adjust baking time based on gratin dish depth and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Orange-Thyme Reduction and Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared beef medallions with orange-thyme reduction and tagliatelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown, thick-cut beef medallions, seared to a perfect crust with tender interiors, are placed beside a neat nest of al dente tagliatelle. A glossy, amber-orange reduction sauce is artfully drizzled over the beef and partially over the pasta. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley, adding a vibrant green contrast. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. A grey cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate, with standard metal fork and knife. Natural, even overhead lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors against a subtly blurred casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pat beef dry. Cut into 3-4 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add tagliatelle and cook according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef medallions 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Internal temperature for well-done beef is 70°C (160°F).
Remove beef from pan. Set aside on a cutting board to rest, covered loosely.
Finely dice shallots and mince garlic. Add to the same pan. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened.
Deglaze pan with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Zest one orange into the pan. Juice both oranges and add 120 ml of juice to the pan. Add beef broth and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce sauce by one-third until slightly thickened. Remove thyme sprigs.
Stir in butter until melted and sauce is glossy. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Drain pasta. Toss lightly with a spoonful of the orange reduction sauce.
Portion pasta onto plates. Arrange beef medallions beside or on top of the pasta. Drizzle remaining sauce over beef and pasta.
Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Beef & Potato Soup with Fermented Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Sustainable Beef & Potato Soup presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed finish, resting on a light reclaimed wood table. The rich, deep brown soup fills the bowl, showcasing tender, slow-cooked beef chunks (2-3 cm cubes) and soft, creamy potato cubes (2 cm). Specks of vibrant red from the fermented tomato puree and dark green from fresh herbs are visible. The soup's surface has a slight sheen, reflecting its savory depth. Garnishes include a few golden-brown, rustic potato peel crisps, scattered artfully, alongside a small sprig of fresh parsley or dill, adding a touch of natural green. The arrangement is clean and minimalist, allowing the inherent textures and colors of the ingredients to shine. The background is uncluttered, featuring soft natural lighting and a hint of green foliage from a nearby plant, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed next to the bowl, completing the understated, organic presentation.

ingredients.name: Zero-waste vegetable broth (made from onion skins and vegetable scraps)

instructions: Cut beef chuck into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Reserve potato peels. Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Dice onions. Reserve onion skins for broth if not already made.
Prepare zero-waste vegetable broth: Combine onion skins and vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, celery ends) with 1 litre of water. Simmer for 30 minutes. Strain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in fermented tomato puree. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in dark beer. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add zero-waste vegetable broth, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add potato cubes to the pot. Continue simmering for 20-25 minutes, until potatoes are tender.

While soup simmers, make potato peel crisps: Toss reserved potato peels with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes, until crispy and golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs from soup. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with potato peel crisps and fresh parsley or dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Squash & Lentil Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic, wholesome stew fills a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The stew, a harmonious blend of soft, tender brown lentils and firm, golden-orange squash cubes, has a fluid, natural consistency. The squash pieces are distinct 2 cm cubes, some showing the slight textural change from fermentation. A scattering of dark green chopped parsley or cilantro provides a fresh pop of color. The stew is crowned with irregular, golden-brown crispy squash skin pieces and plump, toasted squash seeds, adding textural contrast. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood or stone surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its organic textures and warm colors against a clean, minimalist background with subtle natural elements.
instructions: Wash squash. Carefully peel skin and set aside. Halve squash, scoop out seeds and stringy bits; set seeds aside. Cut squash flesh into 2 cm cubes.
For fermentation brine, combine 500 ml filtered water and 10 g sea salt in a clean jar. Stir until salt dissolves. Add 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar.

Place half of the squash cubes into the jar. Ensure squash is fully submerged by placing a fermentation weight or small plate on top. Seal loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, burping daily. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate once fermented.

Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Toss reserved squash skin with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Toss reserved squash seeds with 1 tablespoon olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a separate part of the baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until skin is crispy and seeds are golden brown and crunchy. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Rinse lentils. In a medium pot, combine lentils with 600 ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender. Drain excess water if any.

In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Add the remaining unfermented squash cubes to the pot. Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until squash is tender.

Stir in the cooked lentils and the fermented squash cubes, including a spoonful or two of the brine for extra tang. Simmer for another 5 minutes to heat through. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Ladle the hot stew into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with crispy squash skin, roasted squash seeds, and fresh chopped parsley or cilantro.
notes: This recipe utilizes fermentation to enhance flavor and preserve seasonal squash.
All parts of the squash are used, minimizing waste.
Vegetable broth can be made from saved kitchen scraps.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Cherry Reduction and Herb Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Beef Medallions with Cherry Reduction and Herb Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A neat mound of fluffy, herb-flecked basmati rice occupies one side of the plate. Two thick, seared beef medallions, boasting a deep golden-brown crust and a tender, pink interior, are positioned beside the rice. A rich, glossy, dark ruby-red cherry reduction sauce is generously spooned over the beef and pools elegantly around its base. The vibrant green of fresh parsley and thyme is visible in the rice and as a delicate garnish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed green beans or roasted asparagus.
Offer a crisp green salad with a light vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Dry red wine (e.g., Merlot or Pinot Noir)

instructions: Pat beef dry. Cut beef into 4 equal thick medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef medallions 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove beef from skillet. Place on a cutting board. Tent with foil. Let rest 10 minutes.
While beef rests, prepare cherry reduction. Add diced shallot to the same skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add cherries, beef broth, and balsamic vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Cook 8-10 minutes until sauce thickens. Stir occasionally.
Remove from heat. Stir in 15g butter. Season cherry reduction with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cook rice: Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Combine rice with 480 ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes, covered. Fluff with a fork.
Chop fresh parsley and remaining thyme leaves. Stir into the cooked rice.
Slice beef medallions if desired, or serve whole. Do not fan slices.
To plate, spoon a portion of herb rice onto each plate. Place 1-2 beef medallions beside the rice.
Spoon cherry reduction generously over the beef. Garnish with a few fresh cherry halves or a small thyme sprig.
notes: Adjust beef cooking time for desired doneness. Use a meat thermometer for accuracy (e.g., 55-60°C for medium-rare).
For a richer sauce, substitute a portion of the beef broth with more red wine.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Red Bean Stuffed Peppers
recipes.special_requests: without chicken broth, with Red beans
recipes.visual_description: Four halved, roasted bell peppers are generously filled with a robust, savory mixture of ground chicken, diced red onion, tomatoes, and red beans. The chicken is cooked to a rich brown, contrasting with the vibrant red of the tomatoes and beans. Each pepper is crowned with a thick layer of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese, exhibiting a golden-brown crust in places. The bell peppers retain their shape, slightly softened from baking, with a deep green hue. The dish is presented on a rustic, everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections, set on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually placed cloth napkin and simple flatware complete the homely, inviting scene under cozy kitchen lighting. Portions are ample and comforting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of sour cream or Greek yogurt.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
Offer cornbread or a simple green salad on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced red onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground chicken to the skillet. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Drain any excess fat from the skillet.
Stir in diced tomatoes, rinsed red beans, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Evenly spoon the chicken and bean mixture into the bell pepper halves.
Sprinkle shredded cheese generously over each stuffed pepper.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is bubbly and lightly golden.
notes: Ensure ground chicken is fully cooked to 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For extra flavor, you can roast the bell peppers briefly before stuffing them.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage & Fermented Carrot Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. A generous portion of vibrant, finely shredded and julienned vegetables forms a natural mound. Colors are a fresh palette of pale green from cabbage, bright orange from carrots, subtle red from onion, and flecks of dark green dill. Textures are crisp from fresh vegetables, complemented by slightly softened, tangy fermented elements. The dressing lightly coats all ingredients, creating a cohesive, glossy appearance. The arrangement is organic and unforced, allowing each component to be distinctly visible. A few stray dill sprigs are scattered for natural garnish. The setting includes an undyed linen napkin in beige. Soft natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's freshness and simple beauty. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural plant life.
instructions: FOR FERMENTED CARROTS AND CABBAGE (PREPARE 3-7 DAYS AHEAD):
Clean and julienne 150g carrots. Finely shred 150g green cabbage.
Pack carrots and cabbage tightly into a clean glass jar.
Dissolve 6g sea salt in 300ml non-chlorinated water to create brine.
Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring full submersion. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily.
Ferment at room temperature for 3-7 days, until tangy.
Refrigerate once desired tanginess is reached.
FOR SALAD ASSEMBLY:
Drain 200g of prepared fermented carrots and cabbage. Reserve 15ml of the brine.
In a large bowl, combine drained fermented vegetables, fresh shredded cabbage, fresh julienned carrots, thinly sliced red onion, and chopped dill.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, olive oil, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, reserved fermentation brine, salt, and black pepper.
Pour dressing over the vegetable mixture.
Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Unagi Don (Grilled Eel Rice Bowl)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Unagi Donburi is presented in a classic deep ceramic donburi bowl, showcasing a generous fillet of glazed, grilled eel resting atop a bed of perfectly steamed, fluffy white Japanese short-grain rice. The eel, dark golden-brown with slight char marks from grilling, is cut into thick, substantial pieces, its glistening surface reflecting the sweet-savory unagi sauce. A light sprinkling of bright green finely sliced spring onions and a dusting of sansho pepper flakes adorn the eel. The white rice fills the bowl, providing a clean contrast. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, accompanied by a pair of dark wooden chopsticks resting beside it. Warm, natural lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. A simple, slightly imperfect ceramic side plate with a small mound of gari (pickled ginger) is placed next to the donburi, completing the authentic Japanese home meal setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup.
Offer pickled ginger (gari) as an accompaniment.
Serve with a cup of hot green tea.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. Drain.
Combine rinsed rice and 500 ml water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.

While rice cooks, prepare unagi sauce. In a small saucepan, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sugar dissolves and sauce slightly thickens, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Preheat oven broiler to medium-high. Line a baking tray with foil.
Place unagi fillets, skin-side down, on the prepared baking tray. Brush generously with unagi sauce.
Broil eel for 3-5 minutes, or until heated through and sauce is caramelized. Watch closely to prevent burning.
Divide cooked rice among four donburi bowls.
Place one unagi fillet on top of the rice in each bowl. Drizzle with remaining unagi sauce.
Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced green onions and a sprinkle of sansho pepper. Serve immediately.
notes: Most Asian supermarkets sell pre-grilled and seasoned unagi fillets, which greatly simplifies preparation.
Adjust the amount of sugar in the sauce to your preferred sweetness level.
Ensure eel is heated to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) if not pre-cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken Cutlets with Creamy Potato Salad and Tangy Coleslaw
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crispy Chicken Cutlets with Creamy Potato Salad and Tangy Coleslaw is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown, crusted chicken cutlet, roughly oval-shaped, is placed slightly off-center. Its exterior is visibly crisp with a textured panko coating. A generous scoop of creamy, chunky potato salad, showing diced potatoes, finely diced red onion, and fresh dill, is nestled beside the chicken. Opposite the potato salad, a vibrant mound of tangy coleslaw is arranged, featuring finely shredded green cabbage and julienned carrots. A few thinly sliced cucumber rounds are arranged beside the coleslaw for a fresh element. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. Fresh parsley sprigs garnish the chicken, and a sprinkle of chopped chives brightens the potato salad. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin positioned beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over the chicken.
Offer a small dish of pickles or pickled vegetables on the side.
instructions: Prepare Potato Salad: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Let cool completely.

While potatoes cool, finely dice half the red onion. Thinly slice 50g of cucumber. In a large bowl, combine cooled potatoes, diced red onion, sliced cucumber, and half the chopped dill and parsley. Season with salt and pepper.

For potato salad dressing, whisk together 150 ml mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, 15 ml apple cider vinegar, and 5g sugar. Pour over potato mixture. Gently fold to combine. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Prepare Coleslaw: Finely shred green cabbage. Julienne carrots. In a separate large bowl, combine shredded cabbage and julienned carrots.

For coleslaw dressing, whisk together remaining 100 ml mayonnaise, remaining 15 ml apple cider vinegar, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Pour over cabbage and carrot mixture. Toss to coat. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Prepare Chicken Cutlets: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound evenly to a thickness of about 1.5 cm. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Set up a breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and panko breadcrumbs in a third. Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, allowing excess to drip off. Coat thoroughly with panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.

Heat 2 cm of vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. When oil reaches 175°C (350°F), carefully place 2-3 cutlets in the skillet, ensuring not to overcrowd. Fry for 4-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Transfer cooked chicken cutlets to a wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain excess oil. Repeat with remaining cutlets.

To serve, place one crispy chicken cutlet on each plate. Scoop a generous portion of creamy potato salad next to the chicken. Place a mound of tangy coleslaw on the opposite side. Garnish chicken with fresh parsley sprigs and potato salad with chopped chives. Thinly slice the remaining cucumber into rounds and arrange a few slices beside the coleslaw.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Onion and Chickpea Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Red Onion and Chickpea Salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. Thinly sliced red onions, diced crisp cucumber, halved juicy cherry tomatoes, and plump, golden chickpeas are artfully tossed. Dark, briny Kalamata olive halves provide contrast, interspersed among the fresh green chopped parsley and mint. A light, glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette coats each component, enhancing their natural sheen. The arrangement is organic and inviting, allowing each ingredient's distinct shape and color to be visible. The plate is not overcrowded, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty artisan bread for scooping.
instructions: Thinly slice red onions. Dice cucumber into small cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes. Halve pitted Kalamata olives. Chop fresh parsley and mint.
Rinse and drain canned chickpeas.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.
In a large salad bowl, combine sliced red onions, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, halved Kalamata olives, rinsed chickpeas, chopped parsley, and chopped mint.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all components evenly.
Serve immediately or chill for 15 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccolini
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccolini is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The orecchiette pasta is tender, tossed with crumbles of browned Italian sausage and vibrant green broccolini florets and thinly sliced stems. The dish has a natural, slightly rustic arrangement, with the pasta forming a loose mound. Flecks of red chili flakes and thinly sliced garlic are visible throughout. A generous dusting of freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese covers the top. The texture is a mix of tender pasta, crumbly sausage, and al dente broccolini. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty loaf of Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a medium-bodied red wine like Chianti.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage, breaking it apart. Cook until browned and cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Remove sausage, leaving rendered fat.

Trim broccolini. Cut florets into 3 cm pieces. Thinly slice stems. Add broccolini to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Thinly slice garlic. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Cook orecchiette in boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add cooked pasta and sausage back to the skillet with broccolini mixture. Add 150 ml reserved pasta water. Toss well.
Stir in remaining 30 ml olive oil and half of the freshly grated Pecorino Romano. Continue tossing, adding more pasta water gradually as needed, until a creamy sauce forms and pasta is well coated.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili flakes to desired spice level.
Broccolini can be substituted with broccoli rabe if preferred.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, golden-brown Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake is presented in a well-loved, rustic ceramic baking dish, slightly off-center on a warm, worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features tender, cubed chicken breast chunks and soft potato cubes, generously coated in a creamy, savory sauce, with vibrant green peas interspersed throughout. A thick, bubbly layer of golden-brown melted cheddar cheese forms a crisp crust over the top. The sauce peeks through in places, showing its rich, creamy texture. The overall appearance is hearty and inviting, with natural, modest portions. The setting is a homely family kitchen, bathed in warm, soft light from an overhead fixture. A simple, everyday ceramic plate with minor imperfections is placed nearby, ready for serving. A casually folded cloth napkin and basic flatware rest beside the dish. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere with a natural, unpretentious feel, emphasizing the dish as the centerpiece of a satisfying home-cooked meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a pot of salted cold water. Bring to a boil. Cook 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain thoroughly.
Dice chicken breasts into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat an oven-safe baking dish or large skillet over medium heat. Melt butter. Add diced chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from dish.
Add chopped onion to the same dish. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Remove dish from heat.
Stir mayonnaise into the sauce until well combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add seared chicken, drained potatoes, and frozen peas to the dish. Pour the creamy sauce over. Stir gently to coat all ingredients.
Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbly and the cheese topping is golden brown. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Noodles with Corn
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom noodles is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dish features tender 2 cm cubes of golden-brown chicken, thinly sliced brown mushrooms, and bright yellow corn kernels, all coated in a rich, velvety off-white cream sauce. The egg noodles are well integrated, showing their distinct strands. A layer of melted, bubbly, golden-brown shredded cheddar cheese forms a crust over the top, with some edges slightly caramelized. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and flowing, filling the plate without overcrowding, allowing for moderate negative space around the edges. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, typical of a modern bistro setting. A silver fork is placed to the right of the plate, and a folded white cotton napkin is positioned beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the food while suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 2.5 liter baking dish.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Stir constantly for 1 minute to cook the flour.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth, then milk. Stir continuously until sauce thickens and is smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir in cooked noodles and drained corn. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Kohlrabi and Red Lentil Salad with Honey-Mustard Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in earthy beige. The natural, unforced arrangement highlights each ingredient. Reddish-brown cooked red lentils form a base. Interspersed are precisely diced 1cm cubes of pale green fresh kohlrabi, bright green cucumber, and halved crimson cherry tomatoes. Thinly sliced orange carrot rounds and translucent quick-pickled kohlrabi half-moons add varied textures. Golden sunflower seeds and black chia seeds are scattered for contrast. Fresh green basil and parsley leaves are folded throughout. The salad is lightly coated in a glossy, pale yellow honey-mustard vinaigrette. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige sits beside it. Soft natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing ingredient beauty against a minimalist background with subtle green foliage.
instructions: Prepare Pickled Kohlrabi: Peel one kohlrabi. Slice thinly into rounds or half-moons. In a small pot, combine 200ml water, 30ml apple cider vinegar, 10g sugar, and 3g salt. Bring to a boil. Pour hot brine over kohlrabi slices in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Cook Red Lentils: Rinse lentils under cold water. Combine lentils with 450ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until tender. Drain any excess water. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Let cool.

Prepare Fresh Vegetables: Peel and dice the remaining kohlrabi into 1cm cubes. Dice cucumber into 1cm cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice carrot into rounds or half-moons. Chop basil and parsley leaves coarsely.

Make Honey-Mustard Vinaigrette: Mince garlic cloves. In a small bowl, whisk together minced garlic, honey, Dijon mustard, 30ml apple cider vinegar, 60ml olive oil, 2g salt, and 2g black pepper until emulsified.

Assemble Salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled red lentils, fresh diced kohlrabi, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced carrot. Drain and add the quick-pickled kohlrabi. Add sunflower seeds and chia seeds. Pour vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to combine. Fold in chopped basil and parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty chicken and potato stew is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features two golden-brown chicken thighs, cooked until tender, nestled among substantial chunks of soft, pale yellow potatoes. Diced red tomatoes and translucent onion pieces are visible within the rich, savory, reddish-brown broth. The surface of the stew is lightly speckled with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley. The chicken skin is slightly crinkled, showing its slow-cooked texture. The broth has a natural, slightly viscous consistency, clinging to the ingredients. The bowl is placed slightly off-center on a simple, slightly worn, off-white ceramic plate. A simple fork and spoon rest beside the bowl. Warm, soft kitchen light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and colors of the home-cooked meal.
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip. Sear other side 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add chopped onions to pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Add potato chunks to pot. Return chicken to pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in liquid.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer 30-40 minutes.
Cook until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Gratin with Gruyère
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Gratin served in a clean white porcelain bowl. The base features thinly sliced 3mm potato rounds, layered and baked in a creamy, nutmeg-infused sauce. The surface has a bubbly, golden-brown crust of melted Gruyère cheese with caramelized edges. Two whole, pan-seared chicken thighs with crispy, deep-brown skin sit centrally atop the gratin. Fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the dish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a white linen napkin, and a silver fork. Natural lighting highlights the contrast between the creamy sauce and the roasted chicken skin. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty French baguette to soak up the cream sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed in a sharp dijon vinaigrette
Pair with a glass of chilled Chardonnay or a light Pinot Noir
instructions: Peel and slice potatoes into 3mm rounds.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Whisk heavy cream, chicken stock, garlic, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Arrange half the potato slices in a greased ceramic baking dish.
Sprinkle 75g of Gruyère over the potatoes.
Layer the remaining potatoes on top.
Pour the cream mixture evenly over the potatoes.
Place the whole chicken thighs on top of the potato layers.
Bake at 190°C for 45 minutes.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over the dish.
Broil for 3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.
notes: Using a mandoline ensures even potato slices for consistent cooking.
Dry the chicken skin thoroughly before searing to ensure maximum crispiness.
Check the thickest part of the chicken thigh to confirm it reaches 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato Chicken & Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of the "Fermented Tomato Chicken & Rice Bowl" is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a warm cream tone, showcasing the dish's natural beauty and sustainable ethos. The base is a generous bed of fluffy, earthy brown rice. Arranged artfully atop the rice are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, interspersed with vibrant red bell pepper squares, tender green bean pieces, and earthy quartered mushrooms. A rich, rust-colored quick tangy tomato sauce lightly coats the chicken and vegetables, creating a cohesive, inviting visual. Bright yellow quick-pickled corn kernels are scattered across the top, providing a pop of color and texture. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of emerald green chopped fresh parsley and golden-crisp, thinly fried onion slivers, adding visual depth and a textural crunch. The presentation is minimalistic, allowing the natural colors and textures of each ingredient to shine. The bowl rests on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin and a single wooden spoon, all illuminated by soft, natural overhead light. The background is clean and slightly blurred, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Prepare Quick Tangy Tomato Sauce: Roughly chop 400 g ripe tomatoes. Blend with 15 ml apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and a tiny pinch of sugar until smooth. Set aside.
Prepare Quick Pickled Corn: In a small bowl, combine 200 g corn kernels with 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 5 g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Stir well. Let sit for at least 30 minutes.

Cook Rice: Rinse 300 g brown rice. Combine rice with 600 ml vegetable stock and a pinch of salt in a pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare Crispy Onions: Thinly slice half the onion. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry onion slices until deeply golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel. Season with a pinch of salt. Reserve the oil.

Cook Chicken: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil (or reserved onion oil) in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.

Sauté Vegetables: Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion and bell pepper squares (2 cm). Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, quartered mushrooms, and green beans (3 cm pieces). Sauté for another 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and beans are tender-crisp.

Combine Sauce and Chilies: Stir the prepared tomato sauce and thinly sliced chilies into the vegetables. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer. Return cooked chicken to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes to heat through and coat with sauce.

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among four serving bowls. Top each with the chicken and vegetable mixture. Drain and scatter quick pickled corn over each bowl. Garnish generously with crispy onions and chopped fresh parsley or coriander.
notes: For true fermentation, prepare the tomato sauce 3-5 days in advance using traditional lacto-fermentation methods (salt brine).
Save all vegetable trimmings and chicken bones for making flavorful stock, reducing food waste.
The quick-pickled corn adds a bright, tangy element that mimics a fermented flavor without the wait.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Chicken and Tomato Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is free-flowing and spread naturally. Its vibrant orange-red hue contrasts with golden-brown seared chicken chunks, interspersed throughout. Halved, bright red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color and texture. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top, providing a pale yellow accent. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered as garnish, offering a pop of green. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware are placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Offer crusty ciabatta bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 15 g, chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add a ladleful of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
After 10 minutes, add halved cherry tomatoes to the risotto. Continue cooking and stirring.
When rice is al dente (creamy but with a slight bite), remove from heat.
Stir in cooked chicken, grated Parmesan cheese, and butter. Stir vigorously for 1 minute for mantecatura (creamy finish).
Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: Risotto requires constant stirring for optimal creaminess.
Ensure broth is hot for continuous cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cherry & Orange Beef with Root Vegetable Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. A smooth, creamy pool of earthy-toned root vegetable puree, made from roasted carrots, parsnips, and potatoes, occupies one side of the plate. Its natural, unforced shape creates a soft foundation. Adjacent to the puree, thick, substantial chunks of seared beef are placed, showcasing a rich brown crust and a hint of the reddish-pink interior. The beef is not sliced thin or fanned, but presented as robust, natural pieces. A scattering of a few deep red, whole fermented cherry halves provides a vibrant contrast and textural interest. A small, fresh sprig of thyme or rosemary rests delicately on the beef or beside it, adding a touch of green and natural elegance. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the elements, emphasizing the pure beauty and natural textures of each ingredient. The plate rests on a light bamboo or stone surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, with a clean, unobtrusive background featuring subtle plant elements.

ingredients.name: Beef Top Sirloin or Flank Steak

instructions: Prepare fermented marinade: Pit cherries. Zest the orange, then juice it. Crush 3 garlic cloves. Combine pitted cherries, orange zest, orange juice, crushed garlic, and 5g sea salt in a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Check for sourness.
Strain the fermented mixture. Reserve the liquid for marinating the beef. Keep the fermented cherry solids.
Trim beef. Place beef in a shallow dish. Pour fermented liquid over beef. Marinate in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash carrots, parsnips, and potatoes thoroughly. Peel all vegetables; reserve all peels and ends.
Cut peeled carrots, parsnips, and potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet for 25-30 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.

While vegetables roast, combine reserved peels and ends with 500 ml water in a saucepan. Add 3 whole garlic cloves and fresh thyme/rosemary. Simmer for 20 minutes to create a scrap broth. Strain broth; discard solids.
Remove beef from marinade. Pat dry thoroughly. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Sear beef for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached. Cook to an internal temperature of 63°C for medium-rare. Let beef rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes.

Combine roasted vegetables with 200 ml vegetable broth and 100 ml of the scrap broth in a blender. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add more scrap broth if needed for desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested beef into thick chunks. Do not fan out slices.

Plate: Spoon a generous pool of root vegetable puree onto one side of each plate. Arrange beef chunks alongside the puree. Garnish with a few pieces of the reserved fermented cherry solids and a small sprig of fresh herb.
notes: Fermentation time for cherries may vary based on ambient temperature. Taste for desired sourness. The longer it ferments, the more acidic it becomes.
Ensure beef is patted very dry before searing for optimal crust development.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Pork and Rice Stuffed Conchiglie
