instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan.
Add sliced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add irregularly sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the pan. Turn to coat with sauce.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mozzarella Baked Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Chicken and Mozzarella Baked Rigatoni is presented in a clean, round white porcelain bowl, showcasing a hearty, rustic Italian dish. Golden-brown rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, interspersed with tender, seared chicken chunks and melted, stretching white mozzarella. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, providing a bright color contrast. The baked rigatoni exhibits a slightly crispy, golden-brown cheese crust on top. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. It rests on a simple wooden table surface, beside a folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Finely dice onion and mince garlic. Add onion to the same skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour crushed tomatoes into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to the sauce. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Add cooked rigatoni to the skillet with the chicken and sauce. Stir to combine.
Tear fresh mozzarella into small pieces. Roughly chop half of the fresh basil.
Fold in mozzarella pieces and chopped basil into the pasta mixture.
Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the top. Bake for 20-25 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Cook pasta only until al dente as it will continue to cook in the oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Cerdo
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, orange-hued rice known as Arroz con Cerdo, served on a clean white porcelain plate. Large, golden-brown seared pork chunks are distributed throughout the fluffy medium-grain rice. Visible pieces of translucent diced onions, minced garlic, green olives, and small capers add textural variety. The rice is garnished with fresh, bright green chopped cilantro. A side of thick-cut fried sweet plantains rests beside the rice. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table and a neutral cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the moist texture of the meat and individual grains. The entire plate is visible, showing a balanced restaurant portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fried sweet plantains (amarillos)
Accompany with thick slices of fresh avocado
Serve with a side of crispy tostones
instructions: Season pork chunks with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork chunks on all sides until golden. Remove pork from pot.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until translucent.
Stir in tomato sauce, sazón, green olives, and capers.
Return pork to the pot. Add rice and stir to coat grains.
Pour in water. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a caldero for the most authentic rice texture.
Do not stir the rice while simmering to allow a crust (pegao) to form at the bottom.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Tagliatelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente tagliatelle is loosely coiled in the center, coated in a rich, creamy, pale orange sauce. Seared golden-brown chicken breast medallions are arranged naturally on top and around the pasta, showcasing their tender interior. Vibrant green wilted spinach leaves and reddish-brown sliced sun-dried tomato strips are interspersed throughout the pasta, adding color and texture. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh chopped parsley and a generous dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. It sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish against a softly blurred, casual restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the creamy sauce
Offer extra freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 80 g, grated, plus more for serving

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into thick medallions or chunks.
While chicken cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add tagliatelle. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
In the same pan, add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Sauté diced shallot 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced sun-dried tomatoes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add spinach; cook until wilted.
Return chicken to the pan. Add cooked tagliatelle and reserved pasta water. Toss to combine.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce thickens slightly. Squeeze in lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil or parsley and extra Parmesan.
notes: Use good quality, oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes for best flavor.
Ensure chicken is cooked through but remains moist.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Sausage Baked Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Sausage Baked Pasta is presented in a clean, white, shallow porcelain bowl. The top layer of pasta and cheese is golden-brown and slightly bubbling from baking, indicating a crisp texture. Beneath, the creamy, rich sauce coats tender penne pasta. Visible throughout are well-defined 2 cm cubes of pan-seared chicken and 1 cm thick slices of browned Italian sausage. Sautéed mushroom slices are interspersed, adding an earthy tone. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley and bright yellow lemon zest, with a subtle drizzle of red hot sauce providing a hint of spice. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Green salad on the side
Crusty bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cook pasta: Boil penne in salted water until al dente. Drain.
Cook sausage: In a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven, brown crumbled sausage over medium-high heat. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage.
Cook chicken: Add olive oil to the same skillet. Cut chicken into 2 cm cubes. Cook until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken.
Sauté vegetables: Slice mushrooms 0.5 cm thick. Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Mince garlic. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Make cheese sauce: Melt butter in the skillet. Stir in flour to form a roux. Cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk and chicken broth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens.

Combine: Grate cheddar cheese. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Stir in 30 ml hot sauce, lemon juice, cooked sausage, cooked chicken, and cooked pasta. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake: Transfer mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet. Bake 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and golden-brown on top.
Serve: Chop fresh parsley. Zest lemon. Garnish with fresh parsley and lemon zest. Serve with extra hot sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Tagliatelle al Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. A generous portion of golden-yellow tagliatelle pasta forms a soft, organic nest in the bowl's base. On top of the pasta rests a tender, whole seared chicken thigh, its surface a rich, deep golden-brown. The chicken is generously draped with a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce, studded with small diced onion pieces and hints of green herbs. Some sauce pools invitingly at the bottom of the bowl. Freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano is scattered over the chicken and pasta, alongside a few vibrant green basil leaves, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is clean and balanced, with appropriate negative space. A folded white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant setting, bathed in natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread (pane) to absorb the rich sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
Offer a simple side salad of mixed greens with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in sauce.
Cover pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is very tender.
While chicken braises, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100ml pasta water.
Remove bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme stems from the sauce. Adjust seasoning as needed.
If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water to thin. If too thin, simmer uncovered for a few minutes.
Serve chicken thighs over a bed of tagliatelle. Spoon ample sauce over chicken and pasta.
Garnish with freshly grated or shaved Parmigiano Reggiano and fresh basil or parsley.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality canned San Marzano tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Moo Palo (Thai Braised Pork Belly)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Moo Palo is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Rich, dark brown braising liquid surrounds several glistening, tender 5cm chunks of pork belly and a whole hard-boiled egg, halved to reveal its creamy yolk. The pork skin is soft and gelatinous, while the meat is fall-apart tender. The surface of the dish is garnished with vibrant green fresh coriander leaves and thinly sliced spring onions, providing a fresh contrast to the deep tones of the pork and sauce. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a traditional Thai spoon and fork. A small, simple ceramic dish containing chili vinegar sits beside the main bowl. A folded cotton napkin is placed neatly. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors. The background suggests a modern bistro with a casual atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Pork Belly
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg (skin on, boneless, cut into 5cm chunks)

instructions: Prepare pork belly: Wash, pat dry. Cut into 5cm chunks.
Make paste: In a mortar and pestle, pound garlic, coriander root, and white peppercorns into a coarse paste.
Sear pork: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork belly chunks on all sides until golden brown. Remove pork.
Caramelize sugar: In the same pot, add palm sugar. Cook until melted and caramelized, stirring constantly.
Sauté aromatics: Add the paste from step 2 to the pot. Sauté until fragrant.
Combine: Return seared pork to the pot. Add star anise, cinnamon stick, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, and fish sauce. Stir to coat pork.
Braise: Pour in water or stock to cover the pork. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is very tender.
Add eggs: Add peeled hard-boiled eggs during the last 30 minutes of braising.
Adjust seasoning: Taste and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce or fish sauce if needed. The sauce should be savory with a hint of sweetness.
Serve: Ladle pork belly and eggs with ample sauce into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and sliced spring onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Beef and Mushroom Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of Creamy Beef and Mushroom Rice is presented on an off-white, round ceramic plate, centrally placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features tender, browned 2-3 cm beef chunks nestled within creamy, rich rice. Sliced, earthy-toned mushrooms are generously mixed throughout, contributing a soft texture and deep color. The rice has a slight sheen from the cream and melted cheddar, showing its comforting consistency. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green coriander adds a vibrant contrast on top. The plate is modestly filled, allowing for some negative space. Adjacent to the plate, a simple metal fork and spoon rest on a casually placed, folded beige cloth napkin. Warm, natural lighting from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the food's inviting appearance.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Toss beef with flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches until seared on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add butter to the pot. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 7-10 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add rice. Stir for 1 minute to coat rice.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in cream and grated cheddar. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Herbed Cottage Cheese and Crispy Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Baked Rigatoni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rigatoni tubes are coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce, showcasing pockets of creamy white herbed cottage cheese nestled within. A golden-brown, crispy topping of panko breadcrumbs covers the top layer, providing textural contrast. Small green flecks of fresh basil and parsley are visible throughout the dish and on the breadcrumb crust. The pasta is arranged organically, allowing for some negative space on the plate. The entire plate is visible. A simple wooden table surface provides the backdrop, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and traditional silver fork positioned beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's comforting appeal in a modern bistro setting. In the soft-focused background, a classic ceramic baking dish with more baked rigatoni hints at the communal nature of the meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh green salad with vinaigrette.
Accompany with warm garlic bread or crusty Italian bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook rigatoni pasta in salted boiling water. Cook until al dente, about 2 minutes less than package directions. Drain pasta. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt, pepper, and sugar if desired.
In a separate bowl, combine cottage cheese, half of the grated Parmesan, half of the fresh basil, and half of the fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
In a large baking dish (approximately 23x33 cm), spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the bottom.
Add half of the cooked rigatoni over the sauce. Top with dollops of the cottage cheese mixture.
Spoon half of the remaining tomato sauce over the pasta and cottage cheese.
Repeat layers: remaining rigatoni, remaining cottage cheese, and remaining tomato sauce.
In a small bowl, combine panko breadcrumbs with remaining grated Parmesan, remaining fresh basil, and remaining fresh parsley. Drizzle with a little olive oil. Mix to coat.
Sprinkle the seasoned breadcrumbs evenly over the top of the pasta bake.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the sauce is bubbly and the breadcrumbs are golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Dijon Chicken and Mushroom Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Dijon Chicken and Mushroom Pilaf is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally mounded. The dish features succulent, golden-brown seared chicken chunks, diced to 2.5 cm cubes, nestled within a creamy, pale yellow pilaf. Thickly sliced, earthy brown mushrooms and finely diced onions are visibly integrated. The pilaf combines fluffy basmati rice grains with tender orzo pasta, creating a rich texture. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled generously over the top for a vibrant color contrast. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures, with a soft, blurred restaurant-style background.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes in batches until golden brown on all sides. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken and set aside.
Slice brown mushrooms thickly. Finely dice yellow onion. Mince garlic cloves.

Add more olive oil if needed to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms and cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add orzo pasta to the skillet. Toast for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden.
Stir in basmati rice. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice and orzo are tender.
Stir in Dijon mustard and heavy cream. Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Gently fold to combine all ingredients.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the pilaf with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuna Tostadas with Black Bean Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A crisp, golden-brown corn tostada forms the base, its irregular edges hinting at handmade authenticity. Mounded atop is a generous portion of creamy tuna mixture, showcasing finely diced crimson red bell pepper and pale red onion against the flaked tuna. Alongside, a vibrant black bean salsa bursts with color: glistening black beans, sunny yellow corn kernels, and emerald green bell pepper pieces. The salsa is loose and fresh, not overly uniform. A single fresh lime wedge rests beside the tostada, ready to be squeezed. The dish is presented on a simple, matte white ceramic plate, allowing the food's natural colors to pop. A sprig of bright green cilantro garnishes the tuna, adding a final touch of freshness. The setting is a clean wooden table with a folded cotton napkin nearby, under soft, even lighting, conveying a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Offer a selection of bottled hot sauces on the side.
Serve with a cold agua fresca or horchata.
Enjoy with hands, breaking off pieces of tostada.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Prepare Tuna Mixture: In a medium bowl, combine drained tuna, mayonnaise, finely diced red onion, finely diced red bell pepper, chopped cilantro, lime juice, salt, and black pepper. Mix gently until well combined. Cover and refrigerate.

Prepare Black Bean Salsa: In a separate bowl, combine rinsed black beans, corn kernels, finely diced green bell pepper, finely diced red onion, minced jalapeño, chopped cilantro, lime juice, olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine.

Prepare Tostadas: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or shallow pot to 175°C. Fry each corn tortilla for 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Use tongs to carefully remove. Place fried tortillas on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Season lightly with salt.
Assemble Tostadas: For each serving, place two crispy tostadas on a plate. Spoon a generous portion of the tuna mixture onto each tostada.
Serve: Spoon a portion of black bean salsa alongside the tostadas. Garnish with a fresh cilantro sprig and a lime wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic Mushroom Sauce, Roasted Rosemary Potatoes, and Blistered Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Seared Beef Medallions is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. Two to three thick, round beef medallions, each with a deep golden-brown crust and a visible tender, pink interior, are stacked slightly off-center. A rich, glossy, dark brown garlic mushroom sauce is generously spooned over the beef and pools around it on the plate. To the side, a neat mound of golden-brown roasted rosemary potato wedges, showing slight crispness on their edges, contrasts with the darker beef. Vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets, some with lightly charred edges, and bright red, burst cherry tomatoes are artfully arranged to balance the plate's composition. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring standard flatware beside the plate and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a minimal, casual restaurant background visible.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with 30 ml olive oil, 2 smashed garlic cloves, 1 sprig chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.

On a separate baking tray, toss broccoli florets and cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for the last 15-20 minutes with the potatoes, until broccoli is tender-crisp and tomatoes are blistered.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place beef medallions in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Transfer beef to a plate, tent with foil, and let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.

Pour in red wine (if using) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let wine reduce by half. Add beef broth and remaining chopped rosemary. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Arrange 2-3 beef medallions on each clean white porcelain dinner plate. Spoon generous amounts of garlic mushroom sauce over and around the beef. Arrange roasted potato wedges and blistered broccoli and tomatoes neatly beside the beef. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Запеченная Куриная Грудинка с Картофелем и Лимонным Соусом
recipes.special_requests: надо все сформировать на русском языке. Калорий на порцию в 250 грам не должно быть больше 250
recipes.visual_description: Блюдо подается на круглой белой фарфоровой тарелке в стиле современного бистро. В центре тарелки расположена целая, сочная, золотисто-коричневая запеченная куриная грудинка. Рядом с курицей аккуратно выложены несколько крупных золотистых долек картофеля с легкой хрустящей корочкой. Блюдо полито блестящим, слегка прозрачным лимонным соусом, который подчеркивает естественный цвет курицы и картофеля. Сверху обильно посыпано свежей рубленой петрушкой, добавляющей яркие зеленые акценты. Общая композиция сбалансирована, с умеренным негативным пространством. Стол из светлого дерева, рядом с тарелкой лежит хлопковая салфетка и стандартные столовые приборы. Освещение естественное, равномерное, подчеркивающее свежесть ингредиентов.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Подавать сразу после приготовления.

ingredients.name: Куриная грудинка (филе без кожи и костей)

instructions: Разогрейте духовку до 200°C.

Картофель очистите, нарежьте крупными дольками или брусочками. В большой миске смешайте картофель с 0.5 столовой ложки оливкового масла, солью, перцем, измельченными 2 зубчиками чеснока, веточками розмарина и тимьяна.
Выложите картофель в один слой на противень. Запекайте 25-30 минут до золотистой корочки и мягкости.
Куриную грудинку обсушите. Посолите, поперчите с обеих сторон.
В большой сковороде разогрейте оставшиеся 0.5 столовой ложки оливкового масла на среднем огне.
Обжарьте куриную грудинку по 4-5 минут с каждой стороны до золотистой корочки. Доведите до внутренней температуры 75°C. Переложите на тарелку, накройте фольгой, дайте отдохнуть 5 минут.
В ту же сковороду добавьте измельченный 1 зубчик чеснока. Обжаривайте 30 секунд.
Влейте куриный бульон и сок половины лимона. Доведите до кипения, варите 2-3 минуты, пока соус слегка не загустеет. Попробуйте, при необходимости посолите и поперчите.
На каждую тарелку выложите куриную грудинку и порцию запеченного картофеля. Полейте лимонным соусом.
Украсьте свежей петрушкой.
notes: Внутренняя температура куриной грудинки должна достигать 75°C для безопасного употребления.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle and Roasted Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic mound of wide pappardelle pasta, richly coated in a deep red-brown braised beef ragu, is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The ragu features tender, shredded beef chunks, visibly moist and glistening, intertwined with the broad pasta ribbons. Scattered artfully around and atop the pasta are vibrant orange, thick-cut roasted carrot wedges, their edges subtly caramelized, adding a pop of color and varied texture. A delicate dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese lightly covers the dish, hinting at its savory depth. A small fresh green sprig of parsley provides a final verdant accent. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, presented with a refined yet approachable restaurant style, embodying authentic Italian comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the rich ragu.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese or Pecorino Romano at the table.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as Chianti or Barolo.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5cm chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pot. Dice 2 carrots, the onion, and celery to create a soffritto. Add to pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Mince garlic. Add to soffritto. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary sprigs, and bay leaf. Stir to combine.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C.
Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Ensure beef internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While ragu braises, prepare roasted carrots. Cut remaining 2 carrots into thick chunks or wedges. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Place carrot wedges on a baking sheet. Roast in a separate oven or after removing ragu at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Remove ragu from oven. Discard rosemary sprigs and bay leaf. Use a fork to break up the tender beef into smaller, shredded pieces within the sauce. Stir well. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 125ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Add drained pappardelle directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency.

Plate a generous portion of ragu-coated pappardelle. Arrange roasted carrot chunks around and on top of the pasta. Grate fresh Parmesan cheese generously over the dish. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: The ragu can be made a day in advance; flavors deepen overnight. Reheat gently before serving.
For an even richer sauce, add a splash of balsamic vinegar or a pinch of sugar to balance the acidity of the tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Sausage Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, golden-brown Creamy Chicken and Sausage Macaroni Bake is presented in a white, oval ceramic baking dish on a well-used wooden dining table. The surface of the bake features a crisp, golden-brown breadcrumb topping, contrasting with the creamy, bubbling macaroni and cheese visible underneath. Irregular chunks of cooked chicken and savory Italian sausage are nestled throughout the rich, yellow-orange cheese sauce, interspersed with small, tender cubes of vibrant red bell pepper, bright orange carrot, and translucent onion. The macaroni itself is plump and coated in the thick, glossy sauce. A single, generous portion is scooped onto a simple, off-white ceramic plate. A metal fork rests beside the plate. The background shows a warm, cozy kitchen atmosphere with soft, overhead lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Often accompanied by crusty bread for dipping.
Traditionally enjoyed as a family meal, served directly from the baking dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 2-liter baking dish.
Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain.
Dice chicken into 2 cm cubes. Chop onion, bell pepper, and carrot into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate.
Add ground Italian sausage to the same pan. Cook, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Drain excess fat. Transfer sausage to the plate with chicken.
Add butter to the pan. Once melted, add chopped onion, bell pepper, and carrot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cheese and Dijon mustard until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine cooked macaroni, chicken, sausage, and vegetables with the cheese sauce in a large bowl. Mix well.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Pulse bread slices in a food processor to make coarse breadcrumbs. Sprinkle over the macaroni mixture.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbling and breadcrumbs are golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra flavor, add a pinch of smoked paprika or a dash of hot sauce to the cheese sauce.
Leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Savory Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of One-Pan Savory Chicken and Rice rests on a simple, cream-colored ceramic plate. Golden-brown, seared chicken chunks are nestled among fluffy, tender white rice. Bright yellow corn kernels and translucent diced onion are visibly mixed throughout the rice. The chicken pieces show a distinct sear, while the rice appears moist and well-cooked. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds a pop of color and freshness on top. The dish is presented on a well-worn wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and standard metal fork and knife. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a homely, comforting atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a modest, satisfying portion.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides, about 4-5 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to lightly toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in frozen corn kernels. Return the seared chicken chunks to the skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the skillet tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: This dish is perfect for a weeknight family meal. Adjust seasonings to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mozzarella, Tomato-Apple Relish, and Ginger Yogurt Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken boasts a golden-brown sear, its surface glistening, topped with melted, slightly bubbly white mozzarella cheese. Beside the chicken, a vibrant, colorful mound of freshly diced red tomatoes, pale green apple cubes, and finely chopped green herbs creates a lively tomato-apple relish. A creamy, off-white ginger yogurt sauce is artfully drizzled over the chicken and around the plate, adding an elegant touch. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and 1 cm of grated ginger.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Place mozzarella slices on top of each chicken breast. Return to oven for 2-3 minutes, until mozzarella is melted and bubbly.

Make tomato-apple relish: In a bowl, combine diced tomatoes, diced apple, finely diced shallot, and 1 minced garlic clove. Add 1 tbsp olive oil, half of the lemon juice, salt, pepper, and chopped fresh herbs. Mix well. Add a pinch of sugar if desired.
Make ginger yogurt sauce: In a small bowl, combine Greek yogurt, remaining grated ginger (2 cm), remaining lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Stir until smooth.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before plating.

Plate dish: Place one chicken breast on each white porcelain plate. Spoon a generous portion of tomato-apple relish beside the chicken. Drizzle ginger yogurt sauce over and around the chicken. Garnish with a fresh herb sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Sausage with Honey Mustard Glazed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crisped and glistening, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, two plump, pan-seared bratwurst sausages display a rich, caramelized exterior. A generous mound of roasted potato wedges, tender inside with slightly charred, golden edges, is arranged neatly alongside. The potatoes are coated in a subtle, glossy honey-mustard glaze, catching the light. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is scattered over the potatoes and chicken, adding a pop of color and freshness. A small, separate mound of fluffy white basmati rice completes the individual portion, providing a neutral base. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded grey cotton napkin and standard silverware beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and warm tones, evoking a hearty, comforting meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sauerkraut or pickled cucumbers for traditional German accompaniment.
A cold pilsner or a crisp white wine like Riesling pairs well.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm thick wedges. No need to peel.
In a large bowl, combine mustard, honey, 15ml olive oil, garlic powder, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper. Mix well to create the glaze.
Add potato wedges to the bowl with glaze. Toss until evenly coated.
Season chicken thighs with remaining 3g salt and 1g black pepper. Rub remaining 15ml olive oil over chicken skin.
Arrange chicken thighs and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 25 minutes. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F) when cooked.

While chicken and potatoes roast, cook rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Combine rice with 400ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
After 25 minutes, remove baking sheet from oven. Add bratwurst sausages to the baking sheet with chicken and potatoes.
Return to oven. Roast for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through, sausages are browned, and potatoes are tender and golden. Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer.
Remove from oven. Garnish chicken, sausages, and potatoes with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve chicken, sausages, and potatoes with a side of fluffy rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents seared boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into generous 5cm chunks, coated in a rich, creamy sauce. The golden-brown chicken pieces are nestled amongst vibrant green wilted spinach and ruby-red sun-dried tomato halves. The sauce, a harmonious blend of cream and Parmesan, gently clings to all components, showcasing a velvety texture. Garnished with fresh chopped Italian parsley, the dish offers a delightful contrast of colors and textures. It is served in a clean, white porcelain dinner plate on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting, rustic elegance. A single portion is thoughtfully arranged with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve alongside a simple green salad.
Serve over pasta, such as tagliatelle or penne.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut each thigh into 2-3 large chunks (approx. 5cm pieces). Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sliced sun-dried tomatoes to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in heavy cream and dried oregano. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until spinach is wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Return cooked chicken pieces to the pan. Toss to coat them in the creamy sauce. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Potato Gnocchi and Sage Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous individual portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Potato Gnocchi and Sage Butter Sauce is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gnocchi, small and pillowy with visible fork ridges, are piled organically in the center, coated in a glistening, golden-brown sage butter sauce. Scattered among the gnocchi are vibrant green, crispy sage leaves and thin, golden slices of garlic. Nestled beside the gnocchi are two to three thick, tender medallions of pan-seared chicken, showing a beautiful golden-brown crust. A dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese lightly covers the dish. The color palette is warm and inviting. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing textures and colors, evoking a refined casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served immediately, with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
A glass of light-bodied red wine like Barbera or a crisp white wine like Pinot Grigio.

ingredients.name: Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
ingredients.quantity: 50 g, freshly grated, plus more for garnish

instructions: Wash potatoes. Boil potatoes in their skins until very tender, about 30-40 minutes. Drain. Peel potatoes while still warm. Pass potatoes through a potato ricer onto a clean work surface. Spread out to cool slightly.
Create a well in the center of the riced potatoes. Add flour, egg, and salt to the well. Gently mix with a fork, then knead briefly until a soft, cohesive dough forms. Do not over-knead.

Divide dough into 4-6 portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, about 2 cm thick. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Roll each piece lightly over the tines of a fork or a gnocchi board to create ridges. Place shaped gnocchi on a lightly floured tray.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes. Slice chicken into 2 cm thick medallions.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi in batches. Cook until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Let them cook for another 30 seconds after floating. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain well.

While gnocchi cooks, melt butter in the same frying pan (or a clean one) over medium heat. Add sage leaves and sliced garlic. Cook until butter is golden brown and fragrant, and sage is crispy, about 3-4 minutes. Do not burn.
Add cooked gnocchi to the sage butter sauce. Add chicken broth. Toss gently to coat. Add grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. Toss until cheese melts and sauce emulsifies slightly.
Divide gnocchi and sauce among 4 plates. Arrange sliced chicken medallions beside or on top of the gnocchi. Garnish with additional fresh sage leaves and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Ricotta Frittata
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown frittata wedge rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The frittata is thick, with a slightly puffed, inviting top crust. Its interior reveals vibrant green wilted spinach and creamy white ricotta pockets, interspersed within the fluffy, custardy yellow egg. The frittata edge shows a delicate browning from the pan. A light sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adorns the top. Beside the frittata, a small, vibrant mound of fresh arugula leaves is lightly dressed, accompanied by a few halved bright red cherry tomatoes. The scene is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unfocused background of a modern bistro setting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced, approachable single portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread on the side.
A small bowl of extra grated Parmesan cheese can be provided.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Heat olive oil in a 25 cm oven-safe, non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add spinach in batches. Cook until wilted. Squeeze out excess liquid from spinach.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, ricotta, grated Parmesan, salt, and pepper.
Stir cooked onion, garlic, and spinach into the egg mixture.
Pour mixture back into the hot pan. Spread evenly.
Cook on stovetop for 3-5 minutes until edges set.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake 15-20 minutes until golden brown and set.
Insert a knife into the center; it should come out clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool 5 minutes before slicing into wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken and butternut squash pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The penne pasta is al dente, lightly coated in a savory, light golden sauce. Golden-brown roasted chicken pieces are interspersed with vibrant orange butternut squash cubes and softened, slightly charred red onion wedges. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a pop of color and freshness. Grated Parmesan cheese dusts the top. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors in a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm pieces. Season with salt, pepper, and 2g oregano.
Peel butternut squash. Dice into 2 cm cubes. Slice red onion into thin wedges.
Toss squash and onion with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt, pepper, and remaining oregano.
Spread chicken, squash, and onion on a large baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Cook chicken to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Vegetables should be tender and slightly caramelized.
While roasting, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Mince garlic. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic to skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in roasted chicken, squash, and onion.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the pasta. Grate Parmesan cheese.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Baked Salmon & Chicken with Creamy Shrimp Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Mediterranean dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of creamy, free-flowing Arborio rice, infused with vibrant green peas and tender pink shrimp, forms the base. Centered on the rice are a golden-brown baked chicken chunk and a flaky, perfectly cooked salmon fillet, showcasing its natural pink hue and crispy skin. Around the proteins, artfully arranged, are golden-roasted potato wedges, bright red and yellow bell pepper strips, and burst cherry tomatoes, their colors providing a warm contrast. A small, vibrant mound of fresh mixed salad greens sits to the side. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, natural even lighting, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space to highlight the food's natural textures and colors. All elements are clearly visible, showcasing refined knife work and professional presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash potatoes. Cut into thick wedges. Cut bell peppers into strips. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Toss potatoes, bell peppers, and cherry tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Bake vegetables for 20 minutes.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 thick chunks each. Season chicken and salmon fillets with salt and pepper.
After 20 minutes, add chicken chunks and salmon fillets to the baking tray with vegetables. Drizzle chicken and salmon with remaining 30ml olive oil.
Return tray to oven. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature and salmon is cooked through.
While baking, prepare the creamy shrimp rice. Heat a large saucepan over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil.
Sauté diced onion until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the saucepan. Stir for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in 100ml chicken broth. Stir until absorbed. Continue adding broth 100ml at a time, stirring frequently until absorbed before adding more. This will take about 15-20 minutes.
When half the broth is absorbed, add shrimp and green peas to the rice. Continue adding broth.
Once rice is almost al dente, stir in milk and shredded mozzarella. Cook until cheese melts and rice is creamy and free-flowing. It should not be dry.
Season creamy shrimp rice with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy shrimp rice onto each plate. Arrange baked chicken chunks and salmon fillets on top or alongside the rice.
Add a portion of roasted potatoes, bell peppers, and cherry tomatoes next to the main components.
Serve with a small side of fresh salad greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Clásico
recipes.visual_description: The Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous single portion. Golden-orange, moist medium-grain rice forms the base, studded with vibrant, uniformly diced red and yellow bell peppers, bright orange diced carrots, and soft, creamy diced butternut squash. Large, succulent chunks of seared chicken are nestled throughout the rice, displaying a rich, caramelized exterior. A scattering of bright green peas adds pops of color. The dish is garnished with freshly chopped green cilantro, providing a contrasting verdant hue. The composition is organic and flowing, not overly structured, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin, and a traditional, simple fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh citrus squeeze.
Traditionally accompanied by warm, crusty bread.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion, red and yellow bell peppers, carrot, and butternut squash to the pan. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, and bay leaf. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the pan. Stir 2 minutes to coat rice in aromatics.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking, if using.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Discard bay leaf.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
For best results, use a heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven to prevent sticking.
Avoid over-stirring the rice to prevent it from becoming gummy.
traditional_techniques: Sofrito preparation for the aromatic base

recipes.recipe_name: Kung Pao Chicken Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of glossy Kung Pao Chicken Noodles is artfully presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown egg noodles form a loose, inviting mound, generously coated in a rich, dark amber sauce. Scattered amongst the noodles are succulent 2cm cubes of stir-fried chicken, alongside vibrant julienne-cut carrots and deep red whole dried Sichuan chilies. A sprinkle of toasted peanuts provides a textural contrast, while thinly sliced bright green spring onion tops add a fresh garnish. The dish exhibits a harmonious blend of colors – deep browns, fiery reds, bright oranges, and verdant greens. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks is placed neatly beside the plate, with a small, plain white ceramic rice bowl nearby, hinting at an authentic Asian dining experience. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with chopsticks.
Can be accompanied by a light clear soup.
Often enjoyed with a side of steamed rice, though noodles are the main carb here.

ingredients.name: Egg noodles or wide wheat noodles
Spring onions
ingredients.quantity: 3 stalks, white parts sliced, green parts thinly sliced for garnish

instructions: Marinate chicken: Combine chicken cubes with 15 ml Shaoxing wine, 15 ml light soy sauce, and 15 g cornstarch. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Prepare sauce: In a bowl, whisk together 45 ml light soy sauce, 15 ml dark soy sauce, 15 ml Shaoxing wine, 30 ml Chinkiang vinegar, 15 g sugar, 5 g cornstarch, and 100 ml chicken stock. Set aside.
Cook noodles: Boil noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat wok: Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Stir-fry aromatics and spices: Add dried Sichuan chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant and slightly darkened. Remove chilies and peppercorns from wok; set aside.

Cook chicken: Add remaining 30 ml vegetable oil to wok. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok; set aside.
Sauté vegetables: Add minced ginger, minced garlic, and sliced white parts of spring onions to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add carrots: Add julienned carrots. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until crisp-tender.
Combine: Pour the prepared sauce into the wok. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Finish dish: Return cooked chicken, dried chilies, and Sichuan peppercorns to the wok. Add cooked noodles. Toss everything together to coat evenly with the sauce.
Serve: Stir in sesame oil. Transfer to serving plates. Garnish with roasted peanuts and thinly sliced green spring onion tops. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust dried chili and Sichuan peppercorn quantity for desired heat level.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
traditional_techniques: Wok Hei (achieving 'breath of the wok' through high heat stir-frying)
Velveting chicken (marinating with cornstarch for tender texture)
Mala flavor profile (numbing and spicy from Sichuan peppercorns and chilies)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown with a subtle reddish hue from cayenne, sits center on a modest, cream-colored ceramic plate. Its skin is visibly crispy. Surrounding the chicken are generous, rustic chunks of roasted potato, their exteriors golden and slightly blistered, revealing fluffy interiors. Some potato pieces show flecks of dried oregano. The components are arranged naturally, touching slightly, filling the plate without overcrowding. A few scattered green specks of fresh parsley provide a hint of freshness. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table under warm kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The overall impression is one of hearty, unpretentious comfort food, ready for a family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into rustic 3-4 cm chunks.
In a large bowl, combine minced garlic, hot sauce, oregano, cayenne pepper, olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Add chicken thighs and potato chunks to the bowl. Toss well to coat all pieces evenly.
Arrange chicken and potatoes in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken is done when internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Roasted Mediterranean Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, skin side up, is positioned slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon features a crisp, golden-brown skin and flaky, pink flesh. Around the salmon, artfully arranged but not rigidly, are roasted baby potato halves, vibrant green broccoli florets, softened red onion wedges, and burst cherry tomatoes, interspersed with dark, glossy Kalamata olives. Each vegetable exhibits a slight char and tender texture. A light drizzle of the lemon-basil pan sauce cascades over the salmon and vegetables. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered as a final garnish. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping in the pan sauce and vegetable juices.
A small glass of the dry white wine used in the sauce can complement the meal.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half for juice, half for wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
On a large baking sheet, combine potatoes, broccoli florets, red onion wedges, cherry tomatoes, and pitted Kalamata olives.
Drizzle vegetables with 45ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Stir halfway through.
While vegetables roast, pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season salmon generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip salmon. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Cook for 6-8 minutes, or until salmon reaches an internal temperature of 63°C.
Remove salmon from skillet. Set aside.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce wine by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in butter and juice from half a lemon until sauce is emulsified.
Stir in fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: This dish balances fresh, high-quality ingredients with refined cooking techniques for a sophisticated yet approachable main course.
The pan sauce adds depth and moisture, elevating the simple roasted components.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Chicken and Potato Goulash
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Hungarian Chicken and Potato Goulash is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl, showcasing a single generous portion. The stew features tender, golden-brown chicken chunks (4cm cubes) nestled among soft potato cubes (3cm cubes), diced red and green bell peppers, and softened onion. The sauce is a vibrant reddish-orange, glossy, and slightly thickened. A generous dollop of bright white sour cream sits centrally on top, melting gently. Fresh, finely chopped parsley adds a burst of green. The goulash has a comforting, rustic texture with visible ingredients. The bowl rests on a simple, light wooden surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, emphasizing its warmth. The background suggests a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Accompanied by a side of pickled vegetables (e.g., pickled cucumbers or peppers).
Traditionally enjoyed with a glass of dry red wine.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Add chicken to the pot. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Do not brown.
Add minced garlic, sweet paprika, hot paprika (if using), and crushed caraway seeds. Stir constantly for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn the paprika.
Deglaze the pot with a splash of chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits.
Add diced bell peppers and diced tomatoes to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add remaining chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add cubed potatoes. Stir well.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and potatoes are cooked through. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle goulash into bowls. Garnish with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped parsley.
traditional_techniques: Paprika Sautéing: Carefully blooming paprika in fat to release its flavors and color without burning.
Low and Slow Simmering: Allowing the ingredients to tenderize and flavors to meld over extended gentle heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Paprika Stew
recipes.visual_description: A robust, rustic Chicken and Potato Paprika Stew is presented in a deep, white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The stew boasts a rich, reddish-brown hue from the paprika and tomatoes. Tender, chunky chicken pieces (approximately 3-4 cm) are nestled amongst 2 cm cubed waxy potatoes, softened 1 cm wide bell pepper strips, and finely chopped onions. The sauce is thick and glossy, coating all ingredients. A generous dollop of bright white sour cream sits atop the stew, contrasting beautifully with a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley. Traditional flatware rests beside the bowl on a clean white cotton napkin. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting with natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and texture. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing a professional yet approachable presentation. A side of crusty bread or pickled cucumber could be subtly placed to enhance the cultural context.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
Offer additional sour cream at the table.
Serve alongside a simple green salad or pickled cucumbers.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely chop onions. Mince garlic. Slice bell peppers into 1 cm wide strips. Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add sliced bell peppers and minced garlic. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in Hungarian sweet paprika. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly. Do not let paprika burn.
Return pot to heat. Pour in chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Add diced tomatoes and Dijon mustard. Stir well.
Return seared chicken and cubed potatoes to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. If stew is too thick, add a little more broth. If too thin, simmer uncovered for a few minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot in individual bowls, garnished with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Using good quality Hungarian sweet paprika is crucial for authentic flavor and color.
Browning the chicken adds depth of flavor to the stew.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Beet and Lentil Patties with Beet Green Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly cooked Fermented Beet and Lentil Patty rests centrally on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate. The patty, a deep earthy red-brown, exhibits a crisp, golden-brown crust from pan-searing. Its circular form is clean and defined. Beside the patty, a vibrant, smooth mound of dark green beet green puree provides a striking color contrast. The plate features ample negative space, highlighting the dish's minimalistic elegance. The setting is an eco-conscious light bamboo table surface. A natural beige undyed linen napkin is folded simply to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the left, casting gentle shadows and enhancing the textures of the patty and the sheen of the puree. The background is clean and unobtrusive, allowing the dish to be the sole focus.

ingredients.name: Fermented red beets, grated and squeezed dry
Beet greens, washed and finely chopped

instructions: Prepare flax egg: Combine ground flaxseed meal and 45 ml water. Let sit 5 minutes to thicken.
In a large bowl, combine cooked lentils, grated fermented beets, finely diced red onion, minced garlic, chopped dill, and chopped parsley.
Add flax egg, 2.5 ml olive oil, 5 g salt, and 2 g pepper to the mixture. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Divide mixture into 4 equal portions. Form each portion into a firm, round patty, about 2 cm thick.
Blanch beet greens in boiling water for 1 minute. Immediately transfer to ice water to cool. Squeeze out excess water.
In a small saucepan, heat 5 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add blanched beet greens. Sauté 2 minutes.
Transfer sautéed beet greens to a blender. Add 10 ml lemon juice and 5 ml olive oil. Blend until smooth puree forms. Add a splash of water if needed for consistency. Season with a pinch of salt.
Heat remaining 20 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Carefully place patties in hot pan. Cook 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through.
Serve hot patties immediately with a generous dollop of beet green puree.
notes: To make fermented beets: Slice 2 medium beets thinly. Place in a clean jar. Add 1 teaspoon salt per 250 ml non-chlorinated water. Pour brine over beets to cover. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, burping daily, until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
This recipe utilizes beet greens, reducing food waste and adding nutritional value.
Lentils provide a complete plant-based protein source.
The dish is naturally low in calories and rich in fiber.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Pilaf is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pilaf forms a natural mound in the center, allowing the individual grains of rice to be visible. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among the fluffy, yellow-tinted basmati rice. Visible specks of vibrant red diced bell pepper and green chopped parsley are interspersed throughout the rice. The chicken exhibits a slightly crisp exterior, contrasting with its tender interior. The rice is light and separate, with a soft texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley covers the top. One or two vibrant yellow lemon wedges are placed neatly beside the pilaf. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded, light-colored cotton napkin to the side. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The background is slightly blurred, focusing attention on the dish while hinting at a casual restaurant environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain Greek yogurt.
Accompany with warm pita bread.
Serve with a simple cucumber and tomato salad.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Drain well.
Pat chicken chunks dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced red bell pepper, cumin, coriander, paprika, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the drained rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat rice with spices and oil.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly.
Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid during simmering.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Stir in half of the fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Pasta with Paprika and Basil
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of al dente rigatoni pasta, coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce, forms the base. Nestled among the pasta are several golden-brown, seared chicken thigh chunks, showing well-cooked exteriors. The vibrant red-orange tomato sauce, flecked with finely diced onion and dark red paprika, coats the pasta. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered throughout for color and freshness. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese melts slightly. The plating is inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space. The scene features a simple light wooden table surface, a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin, and classic flatware. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the dish, suggesting an approachable, yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, black pepper, and 5g paprika.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest chicken, then cut into thick chunks.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and remaining 10g paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Stir most of the chopped fresh basil into the tomato sauce.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust paprika quantity to taste; smoked paprika adds a deeper, more robust flavor.
Chicken thighs stay moister than breasts for this slow simmer.
Reserving pasta water helps achieve the perfect sauce consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Sausage Ragu with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A modest, homely portion of Hearty Beef and Sausage Ragu with Rigatoni is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The rigatoni is coated generously with the rich, deep red ragu, featuring tender, dark brown beef chunks and crumbled browned sausage. Finely diced vegetables from the slow-cooked soffritto are visible within the thick sauce. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley rests on top, adding a touch of color. The dish is casually placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table, alongside a simple cloth napkin and standard flatware. Warm, natural lighting from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the comfort food appeal. The overall impression is one of a satisfying, unpretentious family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Grated Parmigiano Reggiano
Crusty Italian bread

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, boneless, cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Add beef chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add crumbled sausage to the pot. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat if needed. Remove sausage and set aside with beef.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto base.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Return beef and sausage to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring the ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 2-3 hours, or until beef is very tender and sauce has thickened. Stir occasionally.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to combine.
