Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and optional grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot & Lentil Salad with Quick-Pickled Red Onions
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Carrot & Lentil Salad is presented on a handcrafted, natural-toned ceramic plate, set against a light reclaimed wood table. Soft, natural lighting highlights the dish. Diced roasted carrots, tender green lentils, and quick-pickled red onion slivers form the colorful base. Scattered among them are diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and a few small, irregularly shredded pieces of chicken. The ingredients are artistically distributed, ensuring each component is visible, lightly coated in a glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette. Textures vary from crisp cucumber to tender lentils and slightly firm carrots. Garnish includes fresh parsley and dill sprigs, with a scattering of toasted pumpkin seeds for crunch. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing the natural beauty and vibrant colors of the sustainable ingredients to shine.
instructions: Prepare quick-pickled red onions: Thinly slice the red onion. In a jar, combine sliced red onion, 120ml apple cider vinegar, 120ml water, 10g sugar, and 5g salt. Stir well. Let sit for at least 30 minutes.
Cook lentils: Rinse green lentils. Place in a pot with 600ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender. Drain thoroughly.

Prepare carrots: Dice carrots into 1.5cm cubes. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Roast in an oven preheated to 200°C (390°F) for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Cook chicken: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove, cool slightly, then shred or dice into small pieces.
Prepare other vegetables: Dice the cucumber into 1cm cubes. Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Make vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together 80ml olive oil, 40ml lemon juice, Dijon mustard, 3g salt, and 2g black pepper. Stir in chopped parsley and dill.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine cooked lentils, roasted carrots, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and drained quick-pickled red onions. Add shredded chicken.
Dress and serve: Pour the vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and additional fresh herbs if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: To minimize waste, use carrot tops (if fresh and organic) finely chopped in the vinaigrette or as an additional garnish.
Lentil cooking water can be cooled and used to water plants.
This salad is excellent for meal prep; store dressing separately and add just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Carbonara
recipes.visual_description: The Chicken and Mushroom Carbonara is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, elegant portion. Al dente spaghetti, twirled neatly, forms the base. Interspersed throughout are golden-brown seared chicken breast chunks, roughly 2cm diced, and thinly sliced earthy cremini mushrooms. Crispy diced pancetta adds texture and visual contrast. The pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy, golden-yellow carbonara sauce, created from emulsified egg yolks, Pecorino Romano, and pasta water, without cream. Freshly cracked black pepper and finely chopped fresh parsley are generously sprinkled over the top, adding vibrant color. The dish is framed by moderate negative space on a simple wooden table, with a classic fork and spoon placed beside the plate, embodying a rustic yet refined Italian bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as carbonara sauce can thicken quickly upon cooling.
Offer additional grated Pecorino Romano cheese at the table for guests.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, dice pancetta or guanciale into 1 cm cubes. Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add diced pancetta. Render until crispy. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat in the pan.

Dice chicken breast into 2 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Add chicken to the pan with reserved fat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from the pan.
Thinly slice cremini mushrooms. Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until tender and browned, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a medium bowl, whisk together egg yolks, whole egg, grated Pecorino Romano, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, and plenty of black pepper. Mix well.
Drain cooked spaghetti, reserving 250 ml of pasta water. Add spaghetti to the pan with mushrooms and garlic. Add seared chicken and crispy pancetta back to the pan.

Remove the pan from heat. Immediately add the egg and cheese mixture to the pasta. Quickly toss everything together, adding reserved pasta water gradually, about 60-120 ml, until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms. Do not return to heat; this prevents eggs from scrambling.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley and extra black pepper.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The key to a creamy carbonara is to emulsify the egg mixture with hot pasta and a little pasta water off the heat, preventing the eggs from scrambling.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Carrot & Chickpea Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, minimalistic salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, featuring ample white space. Bright green, massaged kale forms a soft bed. Golden-brown roasted chickpeas, showing their textured skin, are scattered amongst thin, translucent rounds of quick-pickled carrots, adding a pale orange hue and visual interest. A creamy Miso-Tahini dressing is lightly drizzled, binding the elements. Toasted pumpkin and sunflower seeds, in earthy green and light brown, are sprinkled for textural contrast. The arrangement is natural and unforced, highlighting each ingredient's pure beauty. The setting features a light bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is neatly folded. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and an eco-conscious ambiance.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled, cut into thin rounds or half-moons

ingredients.name: Kale
ingredients.quantity: 200g, tough stems removed, torn into bite-sized pieces

instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Carrots: In a saucepan, combine 250ml water, white vinegar, 15g sugar, and 10g salt. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place carrot rounds in a heatproof jar. Pour hot brine over carrots. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight for best flavor.
Roast Chickpeas: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss rinsed chickpeas with 15ml olive oil and smoked paprika on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until crispy.
Prepare Kale: Place torn kale in a large bowl. Massage with hands for 1-2 minutes until softened.

Make Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, miso paste, lemon juice, 60ml water, and minced garlic (if using). Add a pinch of salt. Whisk until smooth and creamy. Adjust water for desired consistency.
Assemble Salad: Drain quick-pickled carrots. In a large serving bowl, combine massaged kale, roasted chickpeas, and drained carrots.
Dress and Serve: Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients. Sprinkle with toasted pumpkin and sunflower seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: To minimize waste, save any carrot peels for vegetable broth or compost.
Consider using the entire kale leaf, including tender ribs, by finely chopping them.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl, allowing the fluid risotto to spread naturally. Diced chicken pieces, approximately 2-3 cm, are visibly integrated, alongside finely diced red bell pepper (1 cm) and sliced brown mushrooms. A vibrant scattering of whole roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly burst, adorns the surface. Fresh basil leaves, torn, are generously sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of bright green. The colors are rich: golden-brown chicken, deep earthy mushrooms, bright red bell pepper and tomatoes, all against the creamy, pale yellow risotto. The texture is invitingly smooth and tender. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, creating a clean, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto is best enjoyed fresh.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly burst. Set aside.
Heat chicken broth in a saucepan; keep it hot over low heat.

Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.

Finely chop onion and mince garlic. Dice red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Slice mushrooms. Add remaining 10 ml olive oil and 15 g butter to the same skillet. Add onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the skillet. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add one ladleful (about 250 ml) of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir continuously until almost completely absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is al dente (creamy but still firm to the bite), stir in cooked chicken and roasted tomatoes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in remaining 15 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until creamy. Check seasoning; adjust with salt and pepper.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most into the risotto. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish with reserved fresh basil.
notes: The key to creamy risotto is to add hot broth gradually and stir constantly.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
traditional_techniques: Risottare (toasting rice and gradually adding liquid)
Mantecare (finishing risotto with butter and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pea & Ham Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of creamy risotto rests in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte, off-white finish. The risotto is fluid and naturally spread, not mounded, showcasing its soft, velvety texture. Vibrant green, whole shelled peas are evenly distributed, providing bright color contrast. Small, finely diced pieces of cured ham are scattered lightly over the surface and visible within the creamy rice, offering subtle rosy-red accents. The overall palette is natural and earthy, dominated by the soft cream of the rice and the fresh green of the peas. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside the bowl. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene from the side. The background is clean, out-of-focus, with a hint of a green plant, maintaining a minimalist aesthetic. A few fresh pea shoots or microgreens are delicately placed on top as a simple, natural garnish.

ingredients.name: Cured ham (prosciutto or serrano), finely diced

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium heat.
Add diced shallot. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Begin adding warm Fermented Pea Pod Broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously.
Wait for each ladleful to be nearly absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 15-18 minutes, until rice is al dente.
Stir in shelled green peas and finely diced cured ham during the last 3 minutes of cooking.
Remove from heat. Stir in plant-based butter and nutritional yeast. Stir vigorously until creamy.
Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with a little more broth if needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: To prepare Fermented Pea Pod Broth: Rinse pea pods thoroughly. Place them in a clean jar. Cover with filtered water and add 1 tablespoon of non-iodized salt per litre of water. Ensure pods are fully submerged (use a fermentation weight if available). Cover loosely or use an airlock lid. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until a pleasant tangy aroma develops. Strain liquid, discard solids. Store broth in the refrigerator for up to 1 week. This broth adds depth, umami, and contributes to zero-waste cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Tomato Skillet Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Cheesy Chicken and Tomato Skillet Rice is presented in a warm-toned, everyday ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features tender, 2-3cm chicken chunks thoroughly mixed with fluffy long-grain rice, diced tomatoes, and softened diced onions. Generous streaks of melted sharp cheddar cheese are visible throughout, with a light sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley on top for a touch of green. The rice has a moist, comforting consistency, showcasing natural colors of the ingredients: golden-brown chicken, red tomato, and creamy yellow cheese. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, with soft, natural lighting illuminating the dish. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin, emphasizing its homely, approachable character.
instructions: Dice chicken into 2-3 cm chunks. Dice onion. Mince garlic. Shred cheddar cheese.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot skillet. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the grains.
Pour in diced tomatoes with their juice and chicken broth. Stir well.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly.
Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Stir in 100 g of shredded cheddar cheese. Cover for 2 minutes to allow cheese to melt.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining shredded cheddar and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Conchiglie with Sausage, Ricotta, and Fontina
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Stuffed Conchiglie with Sausage, Ricotta, and Fontina is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Three to four golden-brown, cheesy stuffed shells are nestled in a vibrant red, simmering tomato sauce. The baked conchiglie appear tender, with some shells slightly open, revealing the creamy ricotta and crumbled Italian sausage filling. A generous sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the dish. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the top for garnish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard Italian flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its rich colors and textures in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook pasta shells according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add crumbled Italian sausage. Cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and optional red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooked sausage mixture, ricotta cheese, and half of the chopped fresh basil. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the bottom of a 23x33 cm (9x13 inch) baking dish.
Carefully stuff each cooked pasta shell with the sausage-ricotta mixture. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer in the baking dish.
Pour remaining tomato sauce over the stuffed shells. Sprinkle evenly with grated fontina cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and sauce is heated through.
Remove from oven. Garnish with remaining fresh basil. Serve immediately with Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Meatballs with Roasted Red Pepper Orecchiette
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a vibrant, inviting main course on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A generous portion of golden-hued orecchiette pasta is loosely tossed with a rich, velvety roasted red pepper sauce, which coats each piece. Nestled within the pasta are several perfectly seared, golden-brown turkey meatballs, their surfaces showing subtle browning from cooking. The deep red sauce provides a striking contrast against the pale pasta and meatballs. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered over the top, along with a dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese. The arrangement is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space. A simple linen napkin and traditional silver fork rest beside the plate, completing the authentic Italian casual dining setting under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
Offer extra Pecorino Romano cheese at the table for individual preference
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve red bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast 25-30 minutes until skins blister. Cool. Peel skins. Set aside.
Combine ground turkey, panko breadcrumbs, Parmesan, egg, milk, chopped parsley, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form mixture into 16-20 uniform spherical meatballs.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear meatballs until browned on all sides. Remove meatballs from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until translucent. This forms the soffritto base.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Blend roasted red peppers until smooth. Stir pureed peppers into the sauce. Simmer 10 minutes.
Return seared meatballs to the sauce. Ensure meatballs are submerged. Simmer gently 15-20 minutes, or until turkey meatballs reach an internal temperature of 75°C.
While meatballs simmer, boil orecchiette pasta in salted water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add drained pasta to the sauce with the meatballs. Toss gently to coat.
Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh basil leaves and freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese.
notes: Ensure turkey meatballs reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The soffritto base is crucial for developing deep flavor in the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Thai Basil Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A neat mound of fluffy jasmine rice occupies one side. Adjacent, a generous portion of spicy Thai basil chicken (Pad Krapow Gai) is artfully placed, featuring finely diced chicken pieces wok-fried to a light golden-brown, intermingled with vibrant green holy basil leaves, thinly sliced red bird's eye chilies, and minced garlic. The chicken has a glossy, rich brown sauce clinging to it, indicating proper caramelization and seasoning. Scattered around the chicken are bright red halved cherry tomatoes, adding a fresh, juicy contrast. A few fresh basil leaves garnish the top. The overall presentation is clean and balanced, showcasing the vibrant colors and varied textures. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate on a light wooden table surface, under natural, even lighting, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies and a squeeze of lime).

ingredients.name: Thai Bird's Eye Chilies, thinly sliced

instructions: Rinse jasmine rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package instructions. Keep warm.
Combine soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and water/stock in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves. This is the stir-fry sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken mince to the wok. Break up the chicken with a spatula. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Pour the stir-fry sauce over the chicken. Stir well to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Add holy basil leaves to the wok. Stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds until basil wilts. Remove from heat immediately.
Serve the spicy basil chicken directly alongside a portion of warm jasmine rice. Garnish with halved cherry tomatoes and a few fresh basil leaves.
notes: Holy basil (krapow) is traditional for this dish. If unavailable, Thai basil or sweet basil can be used as a substitute, though the flavor will be slightly different.
Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Homestyle Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Thick chunks of golden-brown seared chicken are nestled amongst tender, creamy potato slices, some with slightly crispy edges. A generous layer of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese forms a golden crust over the top, with some cheese visibly browned and caramelized. The chicken is cooked to a tender, juicy state, and the potatoes are soft but hold their shape. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the dish for a pop of green. The overall appearance is rustic, hearty, and comforting. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, with natural, warm kitchen lighting. A simple silver fork and a casually folded cloth napkin complete the homely setting. The portion is modest and inviting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes and slice into 5mm rounds.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced onion and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Push onion and garlic to one side. Add chicken chunks to the skillet. Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Once melted, stir in chicken broth, heavy cream, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Arrange half of the potato slices in an even layer in the skillet. Top with half of the seared chicken chunks. Sprinkle with one-third of the grated cheese.
Repeat layers with remaining potatoes, chicken, and another third of the cheese.
Pour the simmering cream sauce evenly over the layers.
Cover the skillet with a lid or foil. Bake for 30 minutes.

Remove lid/foil. Sprinkle remaining cheese over the top. Bake uncovered for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and cheese is golden and bubbly. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Let the bake rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sopa de Tortilla con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sopa de Tortilla con Pollo is presented in a deep, rustic Mexican ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, reddish-brown broth. Shredded chicken pieces are visible throughout the clear liquid. A generous cluster of golden, julienned fried corn tortilla strips is artfully arranged on top, some partially submerged, others crisp and upright. Accompanying the tortillas are several thick, rustic slices of vibrant green avocado and a scattering of crumbled white queso fresco. A delicate drizzle of pale Mexican crema provides a subtle contrast, and a fresh lime wedge rests on the rim of the bowl. A small sprig of fresh epazote is tucked into the side. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, beside a clean white cotton napkin and a modern spoon. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, with a softly blurred, casual bistro restaurant background, emphasizing the dish's comforting and authentic appeal. The entire bowl is clearly visible, with appropriate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with additional lime wedges for squeezing.
Offer small bowls of diced fresh jalapeños or pickled onions on the side.
Accompany with warm corn tortillas on the side for dipping or tearing into the soup.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve tomatoes. Quarter onion. Peel garlic. Place tomatoes, onion, and garlic on a baking sheet. Roast 20 minutes until lightly charred.

Wipe dried chiles clean. Remove stems and seeds. Toast chiles in a dry pan over medium heat 1 minute per side until fragrant. Be careful not to burn. Place toasted chiles in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let rehydrate 15 minutes.

Heat 15 ml oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 3 minutes per side until lightly browned. Add 500 ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 15-20 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken, set aside to cool. Reserve broth.

Drain rehydrated chiles. Combine roasted tomatoes, onion, garlic, and rehydrated chiles in a blender. Add 250 ml chicken broth. Blend until smooth. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.

Stack 4-5 corn tortillas. Cut into thin julienne strips. Repeat with remaining tortillas. Heat 45 ml oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry tortilla strips in batches until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt.
Shred cooked chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Heat 15 ml oil in the large pot over medium heat. Add the strained tomato-chile mixture. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it darkens and thickens. This is the base sauce.

Pour remaining 750 ml chicken broth into the pot. Add reserved chicken broth from cooking the chicken. Add epazote sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Add shredded chicken. Simmer 5 minutes to combine flavors.

Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with a generous handful of crispy tortilla strips, a few rustic avocado slices or cubes, crumbled queso fresco, and a drizzle of Mexican crema. Serve with a lime wedge on the side.
traditional_techniques: Roasting and charring vegetables for depth of flavor
Cooking down the blended sauce base (recaudo)

recipes.recipe_name: Жареная Курица с Хрустящим Картофелем и Розмарином
recipes.special_requests: надо все сформировать на русском языке
recipes.visual_description: На белой фарфоровой тарелке, расположенной на простом деревянном столе в стиле современного бистро, представлено одно золотисто-коричневое жареное куриное бедрышко с хрустящей кожей. Вокруг курицы аккуратно выложены крупные золотистые дольки или половинки жареного картофеля с румяной корочкой. Блюдо дополнено свежими веточками розмарина и тимьяна, добавляющими яркие зеленые акценты. Рядом с курицей лежит долька свежего лимона. Соус из формы аккуратно полит вокруг курицы и картофеля. Композиция сбалансирована, элементы расположены естественно, с умеренным негативным пространством. Присутствует хлопковая салфетка и классические столовые приборы. Освещение естественное, равномерное, подчеркивающее текстуры и цвета. Вся тарелка видна в кадре, фон минималистичный, создающий атмосферу непринужденной элегантности ресторана.

ingredients.name: Куриные бедрышки с кожей и костью

instructions: Разогрейте духовку до 200°C.
Вымойте и обсушите куриные бедрышки. Натрите солью и черным перцем.
Картофель тщательно вымойте. Крупный картофель разрежьте на четвертинки или клинья. Мелкий картофель оставьте целым.

В большой жаропрочной форме смешайте курицу, картофель, раздавленный чеснок, веточки розмарина и тимьяна. Полейте оливковым маслом. Перемешайте, чтобы все ингредиенты равномерно покрылись маслом и приправами.
Запекайте в разогретой духовке 40-50 минут, или пока курица не достигнет внутренней температуры 75°C, а картофель не станет золотистым и мягким внутри с хрустящей корочкой.
Выньте форму из духовки. Переложите курицу и картофель на тарелку для подачи. Накройте фольгой, дайте отдохнуть 5 минут.

Пока курица отдыхает, слейте из формы лишний жир, оставив немного сока. Добавьте куриный бульон. Доведите до кипения на плите, соскребая приставшие ко дну частицы. Варите 2-3 минуты до легкого загустения. Приправьте солью и перцем по вкусу. Выжмите немного лимонного сока.
Подавайте курицу и картофель, полив соусом из формы. Украсьте дольками лимона и свежими веточками розмарина.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty chicken and vegetable soup is presented in a clean, off-white ceramic bowl. The soup features clearly visible, evenly diced pieces of tender white chicken breast, bright orange carrot cubes, soft, pale yellow potato chunks, and vibrant red tomato pieces. These ingredients are suspended in a rich, reddish-orange broth, indicating a savory, tomato-infused base. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley or oregano garnishes the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures appear inviting and comforting. The bowl is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded cotton napkin and a plain metal spoon rest beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the steam rising gently from the hot soup. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, contemporary bistro setting without distraction, keeping the focus entirely on the appealing dish.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice carrots into 1 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Dice fresh tomatoes into 1.5 cm pieces.
Melt butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in tomato paste, diced fresh tomatoes, diced potatoes, dried oregano, and black pepper. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Season the soup with salt to taste.
Ladle the hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or oregano if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Beef and Root Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. Tender, dark brown beef chunks are nestled among vibrant orange carrot chunks, pale yellow potato chunks, and flecks of green celery. The rich, glossy, dark brown gravy coats all ingredients, creating a cohesive, appetizing appearance. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually placed beige cloth napkin. The setting evokes a warm, cozy home kitchen with natural, soft lighting and a slightly blurred, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels. In a large bowl, toss beef with flour, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot chunks, and celery slices to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add potato chunks, dried thyme, and bay leaves. Stir to combine.
Bring the stew to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaves before serving. Skim any excess fat from the surface if desired. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle hot stew into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure beef is cooked until very tender, easily pulled apart with a fork.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Roasted Chicken with Paprika Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, rustic white ceramic plate, showcasing a single generous portion. A golden-brown, crisply roasted chicken thigh, its skin slightly puckered and glistening, anchors the composition. Alongside the chicken are irregularly shaped, roasted potato chunks, their surfaces golden with hints of paprika, some edges slightly crisped. Interspersed among the potatoes are soft, deeply caramelized onion strands, their rich amber color providing a warm contrast. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and potatoes, adding a burst of color and freshness. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The background features a simple, light wooden table surface, a plain cotton napkin, and a sturdy, traditional fork and knife. Lighting is even and natural, enhancing the warmth of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Serve with a glass of dry Spanish white wine or a light red.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Russet), medium

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm chunks.
Peel onions. Halve, then slice thinly.
Peel and finely mince garlic.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the skillet. Add sliced onions. Sauté over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until softened and caramelized.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika to onions. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Add potato chunks to the skillet with the onion mixture. Stir to coat.
Nestle seared chicken thighs among the potatoes and onions in the skillet, skin-side up.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove from oven. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve directly from the skillet or transfer to serving plates.
notes: Adjust paprika quantity to personal preference for smokiness or heat.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs provide best flavor and moisture.
Ensure potatoes are cut uniformly for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Polish Żurek with Kielbasa, Egg, and Smoked Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl holds a rich, creamy Polish Żurek, a warm, opaque beige-brown from its rye sourdough base. Thick, seared kielbasa rounds and vibrant hard-boiled egg halves are partially submerged. A light sprinkle of melting, grated smoked cheese adds a subtle golden hue and glossy texture. Crispy, golden-brown rye croutons are scattered across the surface, with a generous flourish of fresh, chopped green dill or parsley. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table. A traditional wooden spoon rests beside it on a linen napkin. Soft, natural lighting creates a warm, authentic Eastern European bistro atmosphere. The entire bowl is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing a hearty single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional slices of fresh rye bread for dipping.
Traditionally enjoyed during Easter celebrations, but popular year-round.

ingredients.name: fresh white kielbasa, cut into 1.5 cm thick rounds
smoked bacon, diced into 1 cm pieces
smoked cheese (e.g., Oscypek or smoked Gouda), grated
rye bread, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
Fresh dill or flat-leaf parsley, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Spread rye bread cubes on a baking sheet. Toast for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add kielbasa rounds to the pot. Sear until browned on both sides. Remove kielbasa. Set aside with bacon.
Add vegetable oil or lard to the pot if needed. Add diced onion and carrots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken or vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing vegetables to tenderize.
Stir in Żur and dried marjoram. Bring back to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the soup to thicken slightly.

In a separate bowl, whisk sour cream until smooth. Ladle a small amount of hot soup into the sour cream, whisking constantly to temper it. Gradually add more soup until the sour cream mixture is warm.
Pour tempered sour cream mixture into the pot, stirring well. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Season soup with salt, black pepper, and horseradish if using. Adjust seasoning to taste.
To serve, ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Arrange seared kielbasa rounds and hard-boiled egg halves in each bowl.
Sprinkle with grated smoked cheese, crispy bacon, and toasted rye croutons. Garnish generously with fresh dill or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Corn and Black Bean Salad with Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: This vibrant Corn and Black Bean Salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Charred corn kernels, small diced Monterey Jack cheese, and glossy black beans are artfully scattered, creating a natural, inviting mound. Thinly sliced, bright pink pickled red onions are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color and a crisp texture. Fresh chopped cilantro provides a verdant contrast. The salad is lightly coated with a bright lime-based dressing, visible as a subtle sheen. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table. A small, unglazed clay bowl holds extra lime wedges. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige rests beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light highlights the fresh textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced, generous individual portion without overcrowding.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas or totopos (tortilla chips) for scooping.
Offer a side of fresh avocado slices or guacamole.
Pair with a refreshing agua fresca.
instructions: To pickle red onion: Combine white vinegar, water, sugar, and 2.5 g salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Char corn kernels in a dry cast-iron pan over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally until lightly browned and slightly tender. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine charred corn, rinsed black beans, diced Monterey Jack cheese, and chopped cilantro.
For the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, 30 ml of the pickled red onion liquid, remaining 2.5 g salt, and black pepper.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Add 60 g of the pickled red onions to the salad.
Gently toss to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Lemon Herb Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is cut into thick, even medallions, revealing its juicy interior, and is lightly golden from searing. A vibrant green cluster of roasted asparagus spears is neatly arranged alongside the chicken. A glossy, pale yellow lemon herb sauce, flecked with finely chopped fresh parsley and thyme, pools around the base of the chicken. The overall composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and fresh colors. The background is softly blurred, maintaining a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast asparagus for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic to skillet. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze with chicken broth. Scrape up browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in butter, juice from half a lemon, chopped parsley, and chopped thyme. Cook until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions.
Arrange chicken medallions and asparagus on plates. Spoon lemon herb sauce over chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot & Lentil Patties with Fermented Beet Relish and Pickled Stems
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of two round, rustic beetroot and lentil patties is centrally placed on a handcrafted, light beige ceramic plate. The patties exhibit a deep reddish-purple hue with a slightly crisp, browned exterior. Each patty is topped with a vibrant spoonful of fermented beet relish, a finely diced medley of bright red beetroot and dark purple shredded red cabbage. Alongside, pale pink, crisp quick-pickled beet stems are artfully arranged. A rich, deep green beet green pesto is drizzled gracefully over and around the patties, forming small pools on the plate's white space. The presentation emphasizes natural textures and colors, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural undyed linen napkin and simple, modern cutlery. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the dish's organic beauty against a clean, minimalist background with subtle plant elements.
instructions: Prepare Pickled Stems: Combine 200ml water, 100ml apple cider vinegar, 15g sugar, 5g salt, bay leaf, and peppercorns in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Add beet stems. Simmer for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool in the brine.

Prepare Fermented Beet Relish: In a bowl, combine diced beetroot, shredded red cabbage, 15ml apple cider vinegar, 3ml salt, and caraway seeds (if using). Mix well. Press down firmly. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for at least 2 hours, or overnight for deeper flavor.
Make Patties: Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan. Sauté diced onion until soft. Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and ground cumin. Cook for 1 minute. Remove from heat.

In a large bowl, combine cooked lentils, grated beetroot, oat flour, sautéed onion mixture, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined. Form the mixture into 8 patties (2 per serving).
Cook Patties: Heat the remaining 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through.
Make Beet Green Pesto: Blanch beet greens briefly in boiling water, then immediately transfer to ice water to stop cooking. Squeeze out excess water.
Combine blanched beet greens, walnuts or sunflower seeds, 1 clove garlic, 30ml olive oil, and lemon juice in a food processor. Process until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Assemble: Plate 2 patties per person. Top each patty with a spoonful of fermented beet relish. Arrange pickled beet stems artfully alongside the patties. Drizzle generously with beet green pesto.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing beetroots, their stems, and greens.
The dish is plant-forward and naturally low in calories.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Baked Chicken Thighs with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of crispy baked chicken thighs and roasted potatoes is presented on an everyday, slightly imperfect, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown chicken thighs, with visibly crisp skin, are placed naturally on one side of the plate. Around them, thick chunks of roasted potatoes, golden-brown with tender interiors, are casually arranged. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color. The dish is set on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple metal fork and knife placed casually beside the plate. A casually draped cloth napkin adds to the homely feel. Warm, cozy lighting from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a comforting and inviting atmosphere. The background subtly hints at a lived-in kitchen environment without distracting from the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm thick chunks or wedges.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs and seasoned potatoes in a single layer on a large baking tray. Do not overcrowd.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken skin is crispy and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons is nested in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a thick, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. A whole, bone-in braised chicken thigh rests centrally on the pasta, showing a rich, caramelized exterior. Small, tender cubes of carrot and celery, along with dark, wrinkled Kalamata olives, are distributed throughout the sauce. Freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vivid green garnish. The dish is set on a dark wood table with a folded linen napkin and a silver fork. Soft, natural light emphasizes the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Chianti wine
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano at the table
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden.
Flip chicken and brown the other side.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pan.
Sauté vegetables for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in wine. Deglaze the pan bottom.
Add tomatoes and olives. Stir well.
Return chicken to the pan. Cover.
Simmer 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Boil salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with sauce.
Place pasta in bowls. Top with one whole chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the wide pasta ribbons
Use high-quality San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Halloumi with Grilled Avocado and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mediterranean main course presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The composition features a generous portion of golden-brown seared halloumi planks alongside two perfectly grilled avocado halves, displaying distinct char marks. Nestled around these are brightly colored roasted vegetables: crimson red and golden yellow bell pepper strips, tender green zucchini rounds, and burst cherry tomatoes, interspersed with soft red onion quarters. Each ingredient retains its distinct shape and texture. A scattering of fresh green oregano leaves provides a fragrant garnish. The overall presentation is natural and inviting, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under even natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread.
Offer a side of tzatziki or hummus.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Cut zucchini into 1 cm thick rounds. Quarter red onion.
Toss bell peppers, zucchini, red onion, and cherry tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly charred.
While vegetables roast, slice halloumi into 1 cm thick planks.
Heat a grill pan or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Grill halloumi planks for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and tender. Set aside.
Halve avocados. Remove pits. Brush cut sides with remaining 15ml olive oil.
Place avocados cut-side down on the grill pan. Grill for 2-3 minutes until grill marks appear.
Squeeze juice from half a lemon over grilled avocado and halloumi.
Arrange roasted vegetables on plates. Place grilled halloumi planks and avocado halves beside vegetables.
Garnish with fresh oregano leaves and a lemon wedge.
notes: Use firm, ripe avocados for best grilling results.
Adjust lemon and seasoning to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The saffron-infused golden bomba rice forms a slightly mounded base, interspersed with vibrant red and green diced bell peppers and bright green peas. Substantial, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled atop and within the rice. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a fresh green contrast. The plating is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife on a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and diced tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze. Cook until wine is almost evaporated.
Stir in the bomba rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the grains.
Add chicken broth and saffron (steeped in 30 ml warm broth). Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Stir gently.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Stir in frozen peas. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Check seasoning and adjust.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use good quality smoked paprika and authentic saffron threads.

recipes.recipe_name: Dakgalbi (Spicy Korean Chicken Stir-fry)
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Dakgalbi is presented on a shallow, dark gray or black ceramic plate, mimicking a Korean hot plate. Diced chicken pieces, deeply coated in a glossy, rich red-orange gochujang sauce, are nestled amongst chunky, tender-crisp cabbage, thick rounds of golden-orange sweet potato, and translucent slices of onion. The chicken is visibly tender, not fanned, showing its natural diced shape. Bright green scallion pieces and dark green perilla leaves are scattered throughout, adding fresh contrast. The dish has a glistening, saucy texture. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a small white ceramic bowl of steaming white rice and a small dish of vibrant red kimchi. A set of metal chopsticks rests beside the plate. Warm, cozy light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Accompany with various banchan (side dishes) like kimchi
Eat directly from a communal pan or individual portions with metal chopsticks and a spoon
instructions: In a large bowl, combine gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, minced garlic, minced ginger, sugar or corn syrup, and sesame oil. Mix well to form the marinade.
Add chicken cubes to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat cooking oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add marinated chicken to the hot pan. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is mostly cooked through and browned.
Add sweet potato and onion to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sweet potato begins to soften.
Add cabbage to the pan. Continue to stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until cabbage is tender-crisp and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in scallions and perilla leaves (if using) during the last minute of cooking.
Serve immediately.
notes: Dakgalbi is traditionally cooked on a large cast-iron griddle in the center of the table.
Leftovers can be stir-fried with rice and seaweed for a delicious fried rice.
traditional_techniques: Marinating meat in a spicy, savory sauce
Stir-frying ingredients in a communal pan

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Fettuccine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Fettuccine is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown, seared chicken medallions, approximately 2-3 cm thick, are nestled among the creamy, al dente fettuccine. The pasta is lightly coiled, allowing its strands to be visible, coated generously with the rich, ivory-colored garlic parmesan sauce. A scattering of bright green, freshly chopped parsley leaves provides a vibrant contrast, along with a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese over the top. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space around the edges of the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and a traditional silver fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm thick medallions. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until sauce slightly thickens.
Meanwhile, cook fettuccine according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 60ml of pasta water.
Stir 100g Parmesan cheese into the sauce until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add cooked fettuccine and seared chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 15ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beer-Braised Pork Shoulder
recipes.visual_description: A hearty portion of deep brown, slow-braised pork shoulder sits centrally on a round white porcelain plate. The pork, cut into rustic 5 cm chunks, is incredibly tender, bathed in a rich, dark Belgian beer sauce. The sauce glistens, reflecting the light, and is studded with softened, caramelized onion slivers. Beside the pork, a smooth, creamy quenelle of golden mashed potatoes provides a contrasting texture and color. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley brightens the dish, adding a pop of green against the dark sauce and golden potatoes. The presentation is professional yet comforting, showcasing the natural textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table. A classic silver fork and knife are placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A white cotton napkin rests nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crispy Belgian frites
Offer pickled gherkins or pearl onions as an accompaniment
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge pork lightly in flour.
Heat half the butter in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving rendered fat.
Add remaining butter to the pot. Add sliced onions. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized, about 15-20 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour and cook for 2 minutes, creating a roux.
Gradually pour in the dark Belgian beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in beef broth, Dijon mustard, and brown sugar. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Return seared pork chunks to the pot. Ensure pork is mostly submerged in the liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender.
While pork braises, boil potatoes in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Mash potatoes with milk or cream and a knob of butter until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Once pork is tender, remove from oven. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Stir in cooked bacon lardons.
Taste and adjust seasoning of the braised pork and sauce. Serve hot with mashed potatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Rice & Seared Turkey Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a minimalist, natural composition on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. A generous mound of fluffy, slightly off-white fermented rice forms the base, its subtle texture visible. Resting beside the rice are two thick, golden-brown seared turkey chunks, their surfaces showing a crisp crust and tender interior, devoid of slicing. Vibrant quick-pickled vegetables – thin orange carrot batons, translucent white daikon slices, and bright red radish rounds – are artfully yet naturally scattered around the turkey and rice, adding pops of color and crisp texture. A light, clear vegetable scrap broth is drizzled sparingly over the components, adding a subtle sheen. The plating is clean, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, textured bamboo surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural lighting, creating an eco-conscious, serene ambiance. A single portion is presented.

ingredients.name: Lacto-fermentation starter (e.g., unpasteurized sauerkraut brine or water kefir grains)
Vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, onion ends, mushroom stems)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Rice: Cook 200g rice according to package directions. Cool rice completely to room temperature. Transfer cooled rice to a clean glass jar. Add 200ml cool water and 15ml lacto-fermentation starter. Stir gently. Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 12-24 hours, or until a slight tangy aroma develops. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate immediately after fermentation.

Prepare Quick-Pickled Vegetables: Wash and peel carrots and daikon. Slice carrots into thin batons. Slice daikon into thin rounds or half-moons. Thinly slice radishes. In a small saucepan, combine 200ml water, 100ml rice vinegar, 30g sugar, and 5g sea salt. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Cool pickling liquid completely. Place prepared vegetables in a clean jar. Pour cooled pickling liquid over vegetables. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or preferably overnight.

Prepare Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth: Combine 200g vegetable scraps and 500ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes. Strain broth, discarding solids. Return liquid to saucepan. Reduce over medium heat until lightly concentrated, about 10 minutes. Stir in 15ml soy sauce. Keep warm.

Cook Turkey: Pat turkey breast dry. Cut into 2cm thick chunks or medallions. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 5ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add turkey chunks. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from heat. Let turkey rest 5 minutes.

Assemble Dish: Divide fermented rice among four plates. Arrange seared turkey chunks beside the rice. Drain quick-pickled vegetables. Arrange them artistically around the turkey and rice. Drizzle a small amount of the warm vegetable broth over the components. Garnish with fresh dill or parsley sprigs.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable scraps for a flavorful broth.
The fermentation of rice and pickling of vegetables enhance flavor complexity and aid in preservation.
Adjust fermentation time for rice based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
Use seasonal vegetables available locally to maximize freshness and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Mascarpone Cream with Candied Hake Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mascarpone Cream with Candied Hake Crumble is presented in a simple, shallow ceramic bowl, white or light pastel in color, with natural, slight imperfections. The creamy, pale yellow mascarpone base fills about two-thirds of the bowl, its smooth, rich texture visible. A generous, uneven layer of golden-brown candied hake crumble is scattered over the top. The crumble pieces are small, irregular, and glisten slightly from the caramel coating, providing a textural contrast. A small, unbleached linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. The setting is simple and homely, with soft, warm light suggesting a cozy kitchen environment.
instructions: Prepare hake crumble: Poach hake fillets in simmering water for 5-7 minutes until cooked through. Drain well.
Cool hake. Flake finely with a fork, ensuring no bones or skin remain. Spread hake flakes thinly on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Dry hake: Bake in a preheated oven at 100°C for 60-90 minutes, or until completely dry and crispy. Stir occasionally.
Make hake caramel: In a small saucepan, combine 50g sugar and 30ml water. Heat gently until sugar dissolves, then increase heat and boil without stirring until it turns a light amber caramel.

Candy hake: Immediately add dried hake flakes to the caramel. Stir quickly to coat. Spread coated hake onto clean parchment paper. Let cool completely and harden. Break into small, irregular crumble pieces.
Prepare mascarpone cream: In a medium bowl, whisk egg yolks and 75g sugar until pale and thick.
Add mascarpone: Gently fold in mascarpone cheese and vanilla extract until smooth and well combined. Do not overmix.
Assemble: Divide mascarpone cream among 4 serving bowls or cups. Sprinkle generous amount of candied hake crumble over each. Serve immediately.
notes: The candied hake crumble offers a surprising sweet-savory crunch.
Ensure hake is completely dry before candying for best crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Relish and Herb Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A single, golden-brown seared chicken thigh, its skin slightly crisped, sits prominently. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy white rice, subtly flecked with green parsley, creates a clean contrast. A vibrant, rustic dollop of the ruby-red fermented tomato relish, showcasing flecks of orange carrot and green herb, is spooned artfully alongside the chicken, adding a burst of color and texture. Blanched spinach leaves, retaining their natural form, and slender carrot batons are thoughtfully arranged to complement the main components. The composition is minimalistic, with ample negative space. Natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and rich, natural colors of each ingredient. An undyed linen napkin rests nearby, completing the eco-conscious aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes
ingredients.quantity: 3 large (plus cores, seeds, skins for relish)

ingredients.name: For Fermented Tomato Relish: Tomato cores, seeds, skins
For Fermented Tomato Relish: Carrot peels
For Fermented Tomato Relish: Parsley stems
For Fermented Tomato Relish: Small piece of onion peel (optional)
For Fermented Tomato Relish: Sea salt

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Relish (minimum 24 hours in advance): Combine tomato cores, seeds, skins, carrot peels, parsley stems, and onion peel (if using) in a clean jar.

Dissolve 4g sea salt in 200ml water to create a 2% brine. Pour brine over vegetable scraps, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small clean stone to keep them under liquid.

Cover jar loosely or use an airlock lid. Let ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 1-3 days, until slightly tangy and bubbly. Once fermented, blend the contents of the jar into a coarse relish. Adjust seasoning. Store refrigerated.
Cook Rice: Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice and 500ml stock in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.
Prepare Vegetables: Dice 2 fresh tomatoes. Set aside. Cut carrots into 1cm batons.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add carrot batons. Sauté 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Add spinach and minced garlic to the pan. Cook 2-3 minutes until spinach wilts. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Cook Chicken: Pat chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken to hot pan. Sear 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

Assemble and Serve: Place a mound of herb rice on each plate. Place a whole seared chicken piece next to the rice. Spoon a generous amount of the fermented tomato relish beside the chicken. Arrange cooked carrots and spinach around the plate. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and diced fresh tomatoes.
notes: This recipe maximizes ingredient use, turning common kitchen scraps into a flavorful fermented relish.
Homemade vegetable or chicken stock from bones and vegetable trimmings further reduces waste.
Adjust the fermentation time for the relish based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain dinner plate holds a visually appealing, single-serving portion. A generous nest of golden tagliatelle, coated in a creamy, vibrant sun-dried tomato sauce, forms the base. Interspersed throughout the pasta are bright green wilted spinach leaves and rich red chopped sun-dried tomatoes, creating a balanced color palette. Resting beside the pasta is a perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, whole and golden-brown with a lightly crisped skin, showcasing its succulence. The dish is garnished with fresh, verdant basil leaves scattered over the pasta and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, set in a modern bistro style with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan at the table.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to skillet. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chopped sun-dried tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in heavy cream. Stir. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fresh spinach. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml pasta water.
Add drained tagliatelle to the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water.
Plate pasta in a nest. Place chicken breast on top or beside pasta.
Garnish with fresh chopped basil and additional Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Aromatic Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: Aromatic Chicken Biryani is plated as a generous, conical mound on a clean white ceramic plate with a slight rim. Golden-brown chicken chunks are partially visible amidst long, separate grains of basmati rice, some stained with saffron's warm orange hue, others pure white. Interspersed throughout are deep caramelized onion slivers and vibrant green flecks of fresh mint and roughly chopped coriander. The dish has a moist, fluffy texture with distinct rice grains. A small, round white bowl of cooling raita, garnished with a light sprinkle of red chili powder, sits beside the biryani. A fresh lemon wedge rests on the edge of the plate, ready to be squeezed. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting from the side, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and mint).
Offer a simple salad of sliced onions and cucumber.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon or by hand.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into 6-8 cm pieces
Whole spices (green cardamom, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, bay leaves)
Saffron strands, soaked in 50 ml warm milk

instructions: Wash basmati rice thoroughly. Soak in water for 30 minutes. Drain well.

Marinate chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, green chillies, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and half of the chopped mint and coriander. Add salt. Mix well. Set aside for at least 1 hour.

Heat ghee or oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. Fry thinly sliced onions over medium heat until deeply golden brown and crispy. Remove half of the fried onions (birista) and set aside for garnish.
Add whole spices to the remaining ghee/oil. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add marinated chicken to the pot. Sear chicken pieces for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Do not cook through.
In a separate large pot, bring plenty of salted water to a rolling boil. Add drained basmati rice. Cook for 5-7 minutes until rice is 70% cooked (still firm but not hard). Drain immediately.
Layer the half-cooked rice over the chicken in the heavy-bottomed pot. Spread evenly.
Sprinkle the reserved birista (fried onions), remaining fresh mint and coriander, and saffron milk over the rice layer.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid. For traditional 'dum' cooking, you can seal the edges with dough. Cook on low heat for 25-30 minutes. Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Turn off heat. Let the biryani rest, undisturbed, for 10-15 minutes.
Gently fluff the biryani with a fork, mixing the layers. Add lemon juice.
notes: Dum cooking is essential for melding the flavors and achieving tender chicken and perfectly cooked rice.
traditional_techniques: Dum Cooking (slow cooking in a sealed pot)

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The Chicken and Broccoli Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing its creamy, fluid consistency. The Arborio rice maintains its al dente texture, glistening with melted Parmesan and butter. Tender, golden-brown chicken cubes are nestled throughout the risotto, alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets. Fresh basil leaves, torn into irregular pieces, are scattered on top, providing a fragrant, contrasting green. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese finishes the dish. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp dry white wine
Accompany with a simple mixed green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar
instructions: Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, reaching 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is absorbed.

Add one ladle of hot chicken broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20-25 minutes.
While risotto cooks, steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp.
After 20 minutes, stir in cooked chicken and broccoli into the risotto.
Continue adding broth and stirring until risotto is creamy and rice is al dente. It should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Stir in torn fresh basil leaves. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken broth is hot throughout the risotto cooking process for best results.
The risotto should be stirred constantly for a creamy texture.
Use freshly grated Parmesan for superior flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Braised Beef & Fermented Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of hearty stew is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with an organic, earthy tone, such as cream or beige. The bowl sits on a light reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. The stew features rich, deep brown braised beef chunks (approximately 4-5 cm), tender and glistening. Interspersed are soft, muted orange and red bell pepper squares (2 cm), creamy potato cubes (3 cm), and translucent pieces of fermented onion, adding subtle color variation. A few fluffy, irregularly shaped sourdough discard dumplings are nestled among the ingredients. The textures are soft and inviting. A small sprig of fresh green parsley or thyme rests gently on top, providing a natural garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the bowl. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its natural textures. The background is clean and slightly blurred, with a hint of green from a nearby plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 4-5 cm chunks
Lacto-fermented bell peppers (mixed colors), cut into 2 cm squares
Potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm cubes
Bell pepper (fresh, mixed colors), cut into 2 cm squares

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
