Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep pan to 175°C. Fry chicken in batches for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Discard all but 15 ml oil from the wok. Add minced garlic, ginger, and sliced green chilies. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, vinegar, chili sauce, ketchup, sugar, and water/broth. Pour into the wok.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Stir in cornflour slurry to thicken. Cook for 1 minute until sauce is glossy.
Add fried chicken to the wok. Toss to coat evenly with the sauce.
Transfer to a serving plate. Garnish generously with diagonally sliced spring onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust green chili quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Saltimbocca with Prosciutto and Sage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Saltimbocca is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pan-seared chicken breast is a golden-brown, topped with crisped prosciutto and vibrant green sage leaves, adhering perfectly. A rich, glossy pan sauce, amber-brown with hints of lemon, is generously spooned over and around the chicken, pooling elegantly on the plate. The chicken, pounded to a uniform thickness, shows its tender, cooked interior where a small cut reveals it. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table. Silver flatware is neatly arranged beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin adds a touch of refinement. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting the textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered pasta or roasted asparagus.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound lightly with a mallet to an even 1 cm thickness.
Lay 2 slices of prosciutto over each chicken breast. Place 4 sage leaves evenly on top of the prosciutto. Secure prosciutto and sage with toothpicks if needed.
Lightly dredge the chicken, prosciutto-side down, in plain flour. Shake off excess.
Heat olive oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken, prosciutto-side down, in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes until prosciutto is crispy and golden.
Flip chicken over. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Keep warm.
Deglaze pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in remaining butter. Squeeze in lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer until slightly reduced, about 2 minutes.
Remove toothpicks from chicken. Place chicken on plates. Spoon sauce over.
notes: Ensure chicken is pounded to an even thickness for even cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing. Cook in batches if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Parmesan Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Parmesan Rigatoni is centrally plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thick medallions of pan-seared chicken breast, with a golden-brown crust, are nestled among al dente rigatoni pasta. The pasta is coated in a rich, velvety cream sauce, infused with bright green wilted spinach leaves. Specks of grated Parmesan cheese are visible throughout the sauce, which clings beautifully to the ridged pasta. A light scattering of vibrant fresh chopped parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness. The dish exhibits natural, appealing colors: the golden chicken, creamy white sauce, deep green spinach, and light tan pasta. The presentation is organized but not rigid, allowing for a natural flow of ingredients. There is ample negative space on the plate, highlighting the dish. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A folded, crisp white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from the side, creating subtle shadows that add depth without obscuring details. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan at the table.
instructions: Cook rigatoni according to package directions. Reserve 125 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Internal temperature 75°C. Remove chicken. Let rest 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce thickens.
Add cooked rigatoni and reserved pasta water to the sauce. Toss to coat.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions. Add to pasta. Toss gently.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency with more pasta water if needed.
traditional_techniques: Deglazing the pan for flavor base

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tangy Potato Puree and Jalapeno Relish
recipes.visual_description: The pan-seared chicken thigh, rendered golden and crispy, rests as a whole, un-sliced piece on an earth-toned ceramic plate. Beside it, a natural, creamy mound of off-white tangy potato puree provides a soft contrast. A vibrant, chunky relish, made from finely diced pickled jalapenos, red onion, and fresh green herbs, is spooned artfully over the chicken, adding pops of red and green. Tender-crisp blanched green beans, their bright green color prominent, are arranged neatly alongside. The minimalist composition utilizes ample negative space, highlighting the natural textures and colors of each ingredient. The setting features a light reclaimed wood table, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural light, creating an eco-conscious, clean, and unfussy presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to oven. Roast 15-20 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes.

While chicken roasts, boil potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain. Mash potatoes with butter, 20ml reserved jalapeno brine, and a pinch of salt. Adjust consistency with chicken stock if needed. Keep warm.
For relish: Finely dice pickled jalapenos and red onion. Mince garlic. Chop coriander and parsley. Combine all with remaining 30ml jalapeno brine and white wine vinegar. Stir well. Season to taste.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain.

To plate: Spoon a generous mound of tangy potato puree onto each plate. Place a pan-seared chicken thigh next to the puree. Spoon jalapeno relish over the chicken or alongside. Arrange blanched green beans artfully.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion, Mushroom, and Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl, showcasing a generous, artfully arranged mound of rigatoni pasta. Interspersed within the pasta are rich, deep brown strands of slowly caramelized onions, meaty sautéed mushroom slices, and vibrant, burst red cherry tomatoes. A few whole fresh basil leaves are scattered on top, providing a pop of green. The pasta has a light sheen from olive oil, with visible textures from the tender vegetables. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Slice onions thinly. Slice mushrooms. Halve cherry tomatoes. Mince garlic.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender.
While onions cook, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
In a separate pan, heat 30 ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Add minced garlic and halved cherry tomatoes to the mushroom pan. Cook for 3-5 minutes until tomatoes soften and burst slightly.
Add vegetable broth to the mushroom and tomato mixture. Bring to a simmer. Stir in caramelized onions.
Drain cooked pasta. Add pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to combine.
Remove from heat. Stir in nutritional yeast. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chop fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the pasta. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef short ribs is elegantly plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Rustic, fork-tender chunks of dark brown beef are piled generously atop a creamy, vibrant golden-yellow polenta base. The rich, deep red-brown braising sauce coats the beef, pooling slightly around the polenta. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh Italian parsley provides a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Traditional silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are neatly placed beside the plate, all under soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping.
A glass of robust red wine.
Finish with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
instructions: Pat beef short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear ribs until deeply browned on all sides. Remove ribs.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pot. Simmer 5 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared short ribs to the pot. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged. Cover.
Transfer to preheated oven at 160°C. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove ribs from pot. Discard herbs. Skim fat from sauce.
Shred beef from bones using two forks. Discard bones. Return shredded beef to sauce. Simmer sauce 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, prepare polenta: Bring water or broth to a boil in a separate pot. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, 20-30 minutes, until creamy and tender.
Stir butter and grated Parmesan into polenta. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle creamy polenta onto plates. Top with generous portions of braised beef and sauce.
Garnish with fresh chopped Italian parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Braising time can vary based on rib size and oven.
This dish can be made ahead; flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Gnocchi with Butternut Squash Sauce and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of potato gnocchi is presented in a clean, shallow white pasta bowl, occupying the center. The tender gnocchi are coated in a vibrant, creamy, warm orange butternut squash sauce, creating a rich, inviting hue. Scattered across the gnocchi are small, irregular chunks of fresh, milky white mozzarella, melting slightly from the warmth. A few whole, crisp, deep green sage leaves are artfully placed on top, providing a textural and color contrast. A light, even dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano covers the dish. The background features a simple, natural wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the bowl, and classic Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, maintaining a professional yet approachable restaurant style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a light green salad dressed simply with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel and deseed butternut squash. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Peel and roughly chop onion. Peel garlic cloves.
Toss squash, onion, and garlic with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
Transfer roasted vegetables to a blender. Add vegetable broth. Blend until smooth. Add more broth if needed for desired consistency.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi. Cook according to package directions, usually 2-3 minutes, until they float to the surface.
While gnocchi cooks, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add fresh sage leaves. Fry until crisp, about 1-2 minutes. Remove sage and set aside.
Pour butternut squash sauce into the skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer. Drain cooked gnocchi. Add gnocchi to the sauce. Toss gently to coat.
Cut fresh mozzarella into small, irregular chunks.
Serve gnocchi immediately in warm bowls. Top each serving with fresh mozzarella chunks, a few crispy sage leaves, and a generous grating of Parmigiano Reggiano.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (for the onion and garlic base, though roasted here)
Mantecare (finishing the pasta with sauce and cheese to create a creamy emulsion)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Tomato-Chili Sauce and Parmesan Crostini
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast centered on a vibrant, rustic roasted tomato-chili sauce. The sauce, rich in color with visible flecks of red chili and tender roasted tomato chunks, pools beneath the chicken. Three golden-crisp Parmesan crostini, generously topped with grated Parmesan, are artfully arranged beside the chicken. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and traditional Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and appealing colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side green salad.
Offer extra grated Parmesan at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp chili flakes. Spread on baking sheet. Roast 20 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to oven with tomatoes. Bake 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slice bread into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Brush both sides with remaining 15ml olive oil. Toast in a separate pan or oven until golden and crisp. Immediately grate 50g Parmesan over warm crostini.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add sliced garlic and remaining 1/2 tsp chili flakes to pan drippings. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.

Add roasted tomatoes and chicken broth to skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-5 minutes, mashing tomatoes slightly with a spoon, until sauce thickens. Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.

Spoon a generous amount of roasted tomato-chili sauce onto each white porcelain dinner plate. Place one pan-seared chicken breast on top of the sauce. Arrange 2-3 Parmesan crostini beside the chicken. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and a sprinkle of fresh grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Tagliata with Olive and Herb Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A bed of fresh, vibrant green arugula forms the base on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thick, irregular chunks of perfectly seared beef, displaying a deep brown crust and a rosy pink interior, are arranged centrally. A rich, dark purple-green olive tapenade, coarsely chopped, is spooned artfully beside the beef. A bright green gremolata, a mix of finely chopped parsley, basil, and lemon zest, is generously sprinkled over the beef and tapenade, adding fresh color and texture. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes are scattered for pops of color and sweetness. A light drizzle of golden-green extra virgin olive oil glistens over the entire dish, enhancing its visual appeal. The setting features a simple wooden table surface with a cotton napkin placed beside the plate, all bathed in natural, even overhead lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to scoop up the tapenade and pan juices.
instructions: Pat beef steak dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil.
Sear beef for 3-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached. Adjust time for thickness.
Remove beef from pan. Place on a cutting board and rest for 10 minutes.
Prepare olive tapenade: Finely chop black olives, green olives, capers, and 1 clove of garlic. Combine in a small bowl. Stir in 30 ml extra virgin olive oil and 15 ml red wine vinegar. Mix well.
Prepare gremolata: Finely chop parsley and basil leaves. Mince the remaining 1 clove of garlic. Zest half of the lemon. Combine all ingredients in a separate small bowl.
Slice rested beef against the grain into thick, irregular pieces, approximately 2 cm thick. Do not fan slices.
Arrange arugula on individual serving plates. Place the beef pieces on top of the arugula.
Spoon olive tapenade alongside the beef on each plate.
Generously sprinkle gremolata over the beef and tapenade.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Scatter them around the dish for garnish.
Drizzle the entire dish with a final touch of extra virgin olive oil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hyderabadi Chicken and Potato Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Hyderabadi Chicken and Potato Biryani is presented on a round, pristine white porcelain plate. The dish features a vibrant mix of fluffy, long-grain basmati rice, some grains stained golden with saffron, intertwined with tender, well-defined chunks of savory chicken and soft, roasted potato cubes. The chicken pieces are golden-brown from searing and slow cooking, nestled amongst the rice. Scattered throughout are emerald green flecks of fresh chopped coriander and mint, providing aromatic contrast. Crispy, golden-brown fried onion slivers are sprinkled generously over the top, adding texture and a rich aroma. The dish maintains a natural, slightly mounded shape. The plate rests on a simple, dark wooden table. Beside the plate, a small, white katori (bowl) holds a dollop of cooling raita, garnished with a single mint leaf. A metal serving spoon is placed to the side. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a subtle, blurred background of a modern bistro.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cooling Raita (yogurt dip)
Accompany with Mirchi ka Salan (chilli gravy) or Bagara Baingan (eggplant curry)
Offer plain yogurt or a fresh green salad
Serve with papadum or pickle on the side

ingredients.name: Saffron
ingredients.quantity: a pinch, soaked in 1/4 cup warm milk

instructions: Marinate chicken: Combine chicken pieces, potato cubes, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, slit green chillies, chopped mint, chopped coriander, bay leaves, green cardamom, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, cumin seeds, red chilli powder, biryani masala, turmeric powder, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice in a large bowl. Mix well. Marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the refrigerator.
Prepare fried onions: Heat 2 tbsp ghee or oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry thinly sliced onions until golden brown and crispy. Remove and set aside on paper towels.

Cook rice partially: Wash basmati rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Soak for 30 minutes. Drain. Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 1-inch cinnamon stick, and 1 tsp salt. Add soaked rice. Cook until 70% done (al dente, with a slight bite). Drain immediately.
Layer biryani: In a heavy-bottomed pot (dutch oven or biryani pot), spread half of the marinated chicken and potato mixture as the first layer.
Add rice layer: Gently spread half of the partially cooked rice over the chicken layer. Sprinkle some fried onions, chopped mint, and coriander.

Repeat layers: Add the remaining chicken and potato mixture. Top with the remaining rice. Sprinkle the remaining fried onions, mint, and coriander. Drizzle saffron milk over the top. Add remaining 2 tbsp ghee or oil.

Dum cook: Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Seal the edges with dough if possible. Cook on high heat for 5-7 minutes. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes. Turn off heat. Let rest for 10-15 minutes without opening the lid.
Serve: Gently mix the biryani from the bottom up to combine chicken, potato, and rice layers. Ensure chicken is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Soaking basmati rice prevents breakage and promotes longer grains.
Sealing the pot for 'dum' cooking is crucial for infusing flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Rice Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The golden-yellow broth is clear, with visible steam rising. Within the broth are hearty, irregular chunks of cooked chicken, approximately 2cm cubes. Soft, fluffy white rice grains are suspended throughout. Bright orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and translucent diced onions are interspersed, adding color and texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside it. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen at home.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh

instructions: Dice chicken into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Dice carrots, celery, and onion. Add to the same pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Add rice. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender. Stir occasionally.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Pork & Carrot Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Creamy Pork & Carrot Pasta is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pasta, likely penne or fusilli, is coated in a rich, creamy, light tan sauce. Visible throughout are browned chunks of ground pork, bright orange diced carrots, and finely diced onion pieces, all integrated. The dish has a comforting, rustic appearance, with pasta naturally tangled. A few specks of black pepper are visible. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showing subtle grain. A basic stainless steel fork is placed beside the plate. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen. Negative space around the plate ensures the dish is the focal point. Pork is presented as integrated pieces, not sliced.
instructions: Boil salted water in a large pot. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pan over medium-high heat. Add ground pork. Cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
Add diced onion and diced carrots to the skillet with the pork. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and soy sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Pour the sauce mixture into the skillet with the pork and vegetables. Add 150ml water or broth. Stir well to combine.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes, allowing the sauce to warm through. Do not boil.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet. Toss gently to coat the pasta evenly with the creamy sauce. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: This dish is perfect for a quick and satisfying weeknight meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Chicken and Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aloo Murgh is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. A mound of fluffy, steamed long-grain basmati rice occupies one side. Beside it, the curry features large 4cm chunks of moist chicken and 3cm cubes of tender potato. The sauce is a rich, deep orange-brown with visible textures of sautéed onions. Two bright green chilies, slit lengthwise, are nestled among the chicken pieces. Freshly chopped green coriander is scattered across the curry for contrast. The bowl rests on a rustic dark wood surface. A small side dish of pickled vegetables and a copper spoon accompany the meal. Natural light emphasizes the glossy sauce and soft textures of the rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lime wedges
Accompany with mango chutney
Traditional copper serving spoon
Serve with warm garlic naan
instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 20 minutes.
Boil 600ml water. Add soaked rice. Simmer 12 minutes until tender. Drain.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds.
Add diced onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and slit chilies. Cook for 1 minute.
Cut chicken into 4cm chunks. Add to pot. Sear until browned.
Add turmeric, garam masala, and 3cm potato cubes. Season with salt.
Pour in 200ml water. Cover with a tight lid. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with chopped coriander. Serve hot with rice.
notes: Ensure onions are well-browned for a deep sauce color
Use waxy potatoes so they do not break apart during the simmer
Soaking the basmati rice ensures long, separate grains

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh is centrally placed on a handcrafted, natural cream-colored ceramic plate. The plate's generous white space emphasizes the dish. Beneath the chicken, a smooth, pale orange root vegetable puree forms a soft, organic base. The chicken thigh features a deeply golden, crisp skin with visible texture, while the interior remains plump and juicy. A vibrant, chunky relish of bright red diced tomatoes, flecked with dark green basil and parsley, is generously spooned over the chicken, allowing some to cascade onto the puree. A few small, fresh basil leaves are scattered naturally on top for a subtle green accent. The composition is clean and unforced, highlighting natural ingredient colors and textures. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly placed nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, enhancing dimensionality.

ingredients.name: Pre-fermented garlic paste
ingredients.quantity: 30g or finely minced fermented garlic cloves

instructions: Prepare Root Vegetable Puree: Heat 15ml olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add chopped onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add chopped carrots and parsnips. Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook until vegetables are very tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain liquid, reserving if needed for consistency. Transfer cooked vegetables to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Make Fermented Tomato Relish: In a small bowl, combine diced tomatoes, fermented garlic paste, chopped basil, and chopped parsley. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil and apple cider vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Stir gently to combine. Let sit for 10 minutes for flavors to meld.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and very crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Rest Chicken: Remove chicken from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes before plating.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous dollop of root vegetable puree onto the center of each plate. Create a slight swirl or smooth mound. Place one whole, unsliced chicken thigh on top of the puree. Spoon a generous amount of the fermented tomato relish over and around the chicken. Garnish with a few small, fresh basil leaves or parsley sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Carrot and Black Rice Salad with Preserved Lemon
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, placed on a light reclaimed wood table. A bed of deep purple-black rice forms the base. Diced roasted carrots, red bell pepper, and zucchini are artfully scattered over the rice, showcasing their vibrant orange, red, and green hues. Finely diced preserved lemon peel pieces, a pale yellow, are sprinkled throughout, providing bright contrast. Fresh green parsley and mint leaves are generously interspersed, adding freshness and color. The components are loosely arranged, allowing each ingredient's texture and color to shine naturally. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. A rustic undyed linen napkin and a simple glass of water complete the eco-conscious setting under soft natural lighting.
instructions: Rinse black rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package instructions. Usually 1 part rice to 2 parts water. Simmer until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Dice carrots, red bell pepper, and zucchini into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender-crisp and lightly caramelized. Let cool.
Rinse preserved lemon thoroughly under cold water. Discard the pulp. Finely dice the preserved lemon peel.
Roughly chop fresh parsley and mint.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 45 ml olive oil, fresh lemon juice, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
In a large bowl, combine cooled black rice, roasted vegetables, diced preserved lemon, chopped parsley, and mint.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Toast pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant and lightly browned. Sprinkle over the salad before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken Ragu with Creamy Polenta and Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked chicken ragu with pappardelle and creamy polenta is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The rich, deep red-brown ragu, featuring tender, shredded chicken chunks, is nestled over a golden-yellow bed of creamy, flowing polenta. Al dente pappardelle pasta is tossed with the ragu, creating an inviting texture contrast. The dish is generously topped with freshly grated, pale yellow Parmesan cheese and bright green, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley, providing a vibrant pop of color and freshness. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by classic Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
Pair with a glass of robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery into small pieces for soffritto.
Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent, stirring occasionally. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is mostly reduced, about 3-4 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until chicken is very tender and easily shreddable with a fork. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme sprigs. Shred chicken into smaller pieces directly in the sauce using two forks. Stir well. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
While ragu finishes, prepare polenta. Bring 1 litre of water and a pinch of salt to a boil in a separate saucepan.

Slowly whisk in polenta, ensuring no lumps. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 25-30 minutes until creamy and thick. Add more hot water or broth if needed for desired consistency. Stir in 50g grated Parmesan cheese.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water. Add drained pasta to the ragu. Toss to coat, adding a little reserved pasta water if the sauce is too thick.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy polenta onto each plate. Ladle the chicken ragu with pappardelle over or alongside the polenta.
Garnish generously with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty chicken and vegetable rice soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a subtly imperfect rim, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-amber broth is rich with visible pieces: tender, shredded chicken, soft white rice grains, small diced red tomatoes, and vibrant green broccoli florets. The ingredients are naturally distributed, some overlapping, showcasing a comforting, home-cooked feel. A generous sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped green parsley brightens the top. A simple, slightly wrinkled cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. Warm, soft light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural colors and textures. The overall setting is a relaxed, lived-in family kitchen, emphasizing comfort and approachability. The entire bowl is visible, with ample negative space around it.
instructions: Rinse chicken breast. Place in a pot with 500 ml of chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Shred or dice into bite-sized pieces. Set aside.
Cook rice according to package instructions. Use water or broth. Set aside.
Dice the yellow onion. Mince the garlic cloves. Cut broccoli into small florets.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in remaining 1 L chicken broth and canned diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Add broccoli florets. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Stir in the cooked rice and shredded or diced chicken. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Macaroni with Italian Sausage and Three Cheeses
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Macaroni with Italian Sausage and Three Cheeses is presented in a white ceramic oval gratin dish. The dish boasts a golden-brown, bubbly top crust from melted mozzarella and toasted breadcrumbs. Tender elbow macaroni, coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce, is mixed with substantial, irregular chunks of browned Italian sausage. Creamy white ricotta and fresh green basil flecks are visible. Colors are warm reds, golden browns, creamy whites, and vibrant greens. Textures are crispy on top, tender and creamy inside. Garnish with torn fresh basil and grated Parmesan. It rests on a simple wooden table, with a white porcelain underplate, cotton napkin, and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting and a blurred modern bistro background complete the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil, chopped and whole leaves for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Pulse stale bread in a food processor to create coarse breadcrumbs. Set aside.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage. Break into irregular chunks. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon; set aside. Drain excess fat, leaving about 15ml in the skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in chopped fresh basil.
While sauce simmers, cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
In a large bowl, combine cooked macaroni, tomato sauce, cooked sausage, beaten eggs, ricotta cheese, and 75g of the grated Parmesan. Mix thoroughly.
Pour the macaroni mixture into the prepared baking dish. Spread evenly.
Top with shredded mozzarella cheese and the prepared breadcrumbs. Sprinkle with remaining 25g Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and bubbly. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure macaroni is cooked al dente before baking to prevent it from becoming mushy.
Adjust the spice level by using mild or spicy Italian sausage based on preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Quinoa Mediterranean Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Quinoa Mediterranean Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The cooked quinoa forms the base, flecked with finely diced red onion and yellow bell pepper, creating a mosaic of yellow and purple. Halved cherry tomatoes add bursts of red, while diced cucumber and halved Kalamata olives provide green and dark accents. Fresh chopped parsley is generously mixed throughout. The salad is casually arranged, allowing the natural textures and colors of the ingredients to shine. A simple lemon-herb vinaigrette lightly coats all components, giving a fresh sheen. The bowl sits on a beige linen placemat. A plain white ceramic plate with a small rim is next to it, ready for serving. A silver fork rests beside the plate. Warm, soft light from a nearby kitchen window illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural appeal of the homely dish. The overall presentation is unpretentious and inviting, typical of a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty bread.
instructions: Rinse quinoa under cold water.
Combine quinoa and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand covered 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Let cool completely.
Dice cucumber. Halve cherry tomatoes. Finely dice red onion. Dice yellow bell pepper. Halve pitted Kalamata olives. Chop fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, lemon juice, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooled quinoa, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, finely diced red onion, diced yellow bell pepper, halved Kalamata olives, and chopped parsley.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Add crumbled feta cheese. Toss lightly again.
Serve immediately or chill before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Clear Chicken Noodle & Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Japanese Clear Chicken Noodle & Rice Soup is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain donburi bowl. The clear, golden chicken broth forms the base. Cooked short-grain rice rests at the bottom, topped with neatly coiled, pale yellow egg noodles. Tender, thinly sliced chicken pieces, showing their cooked texture, are arranged gracefully over the noodles. Bright red, small-diced tomato cubes and vibrant green, thinly sliced scallions are scattered as garnishes, adding pops of color and freshness. The arrangement is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a simple ceramic chopstick rest. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's fresh ingredients and inviting warmth.
instructions: Rinse chicken breast under cold water. Pat dry. Set aside.
Peel and halve the onion. Smash garlic cloves. Slice ginger into thin rounds.
Place chicken, halved onion, smashed garlic, and ginger in a large pot. Add 1.5 L water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Skim any foam from the surface.
Remove chicken from the pot. Let it cool slightly. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Discard solids. Season broth with soy sauce, salt, and pepper to taste.
Shred or thinly slice the cooked chicken against the grain. Set aside.
Cook short-grain rice according to package instructions. Keep warm.
Cook egg noodles according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Dice the tomato into small, uniform cubes. Thinly slice green onions.
To serve, divide cooked rice among four individual donburi bowls. Add a portion of cooked egg noodles over the rice. Arrange shredded or sliced chicken on top.
Ladle hot, clear broth over the chicken, noodles, and rice. Garnish each bowl with diced tomato and sliced green onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta with Fermented Tomato Sauce and Crispy Sausage
recipes.visual_description: A mound of al dente rigatoni pasta, generously coated in a rich, reddish-orange fermented tomato sauce, sits centrally on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate. Scattered over the pasta are irregular, crispy browned chunks of Italian sausage, providing textural contrast. Bright green, whole basil leaves are artfully placed amongst the pasta, adding fresh color. The composition is clean and uncrowded, allowing ample white space on the plate's rim. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually draped to one side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the pasta's texture and the sauce's slight sheen. The background is minimalist, with a hint of a blurred green plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage. Cook, breaking it into small, irregular pieces, until well browned and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove sausage from pan. Drain excess fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add fermented or preserved diced tomatoes to the pan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.

Return cooked sausage chunks to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta and reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to combine, ensuring pasta is evenly coated. Cook for 2 minutes, allowing sauce to cling to pasta.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh basil leaves. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainable practices by using fermented tomatoes for preservation and utilizing sausage fat for flavor, minimizing waste. The focus is on natural ingredients and clean preparation.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato and Garden Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, bountiful Roasted Potato and Garden Vegetable Salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The dish is arranged casually, with components naturally overlapping. Diced roasted potatoes and butternut squash with lightly browned edges, vibrant red and yellow bell pepper pieces, and tender chicken chunks are prominent. Bright green peas and corn kernels add pops of color. Sautéed mushrooms and thinly sliced red onion are nestled among the roasted vegetables. Chopped red tomatoes and halved black olives are scattered throughout. A bed of mixed salad greens peeks from beneath, lightly coated in a simple vinaigrette. The salad is generously topped with crumbled white feta cheese and fresh green chopped parsley. The setting features warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a relaxed family dining area. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. The portion is hearty and homely, showcasing the diverse, colorful ingredients and emphasizing comfort food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Dice potatoes and butternut squash into 2 cm cubes. Dice bell peppers into 2 cm pieces.
Toss potatoes, squash, and bell peppers with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned. Stir halfway through.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove and rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
While chicken rests, add sliced red onion and quartered mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add frozen corn and green peas. Cook for 2 minutes. Drain well.
Chop tomatoes into 2 cm pieces. Halve pitted black olives.
For the dressing: Whisk together remaining 35 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, honey (or sugar), salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, squash, bell peppers, cooked corn, peas, sautéed mushrooms, and red onion.
Add chopped tomatoes, halved olives, and mixed salad greens to the bowl.
Add chicken chunks to the bowl. Pour dressing over the salad. Gently toss to combine.
Crumble feta cheese over the top. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Sausage Chowder
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty chowder fills a deep, classic white porcelain bowl. The creamy, off-white broth is generously laden with tender shredded chicken, round slices of browned sausage, bright yellow corn kernels, and soft 1.5 cm diced potatoes. Small pasta shapes, softened red bell pepper, and onion pieces are visible, alongside subtle 1 cm diced apple. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley adds a vibrant pop of color. A small cluster of golden-brown, rustic bread croutons rests on the surface, offering textural contrast. Colors are warm creamy whites, golden browns, yellows, reds, and fresh green. The bowl sits on a light, rustic wooden table with a folded white linen napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting warmth in a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 5ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden. Remove chicken. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest, then shred or dice into 1.5 cm pieces.
Slice sausage into 1 cm rounds. Add to the same pot. Cook until browned. Remove sausage.
Add remaining 10ml olive oil and butter to the pot. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring.
Add 1.5 cm diced potatoes, corn, and 1 cm diced apple. Return shredded chicken and cooked sausage to the pot.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
While soup simmers, cook pasta according to package directions in a separate pot of salted water until al dente. Drain.
Stir milk into the soup. Heat through, do not boil. Season with salt and pepper.
Toss bread cubes with a drizzle of olive oil. Toast in a pan or oven until golden and crisp to make croutons.
Stir cooked pasta into the soup. Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and toasted croutons.
notes: For a richer flavor, use heavy cream instead of milk.
Adjust thickness by adding more broth or milk as desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce and Roasted Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken with creamy mushroom sauce and roasted rosemary potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The golden-brown roasted potato wedges are neatly arranged on one side of the plate. A thick, seared chicken breast, cooked to a perfect golden hue, rests beside the potatoes. A rich, creamy mushroom sauce, studded with tender, earthy brown mushroom slices, is generously spooned over the chicken, cascading slightly onto the plate. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley adds a fresh contrast. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, with a silver fork and knife placed beside the plate, and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting and refined presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges or chunks. Toss with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 sprig rosemary (leaves removed and chopped), salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Flip halfway through.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 10g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven.
Bake chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside to rest, loosely tented with foil.
While chicken rests, finely dice shallots and mince garlic.
In the same skillet (or a clean one if preferred), melt remaining 20g butter over medium heat. Add shallots and sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and remaining rosemary sprig (whole or chopped) to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced or quartered mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Gruyere cheese. Simmer gently for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove rosemary sprig.
To serve, arrange roasted potatoes on a white porcelain plate. Place a whole or thick-cut chicken breast beside the potatoes. Spoon generous amount of creamy mushroom sauce over the chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Tomato and Mushroom
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised chicken is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, tender chicken thigh, not sliced, rests amidst a rich, deep red tomato and mushroom sauce. The sauce is thick with visible quartered brown mushrooms and softened diced onions. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley and basil leaves are scattered over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The chicken skin retains some crispness, contrasting with the tender braised meat. The overall presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a subtly blurred restaurant background.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for 3-4 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Sauté for 5 minutes until mushrooms are browned.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and dried oregano. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Tomatoes and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken skin is golden-brown with hints of browning, showcasing a tender, fall-off-the-bone texture. A rich, rustic tomato and olive sauce generously coats the chicken and pools around its base. The sauce is vibrant red, studded with softened diced onion, minced garlic, and dark, glossy whole pitted Kalamata olives. A sprinkling of bright green, freshly chopped parsley leaves provides a fresh counterpoint. A small sprig of fresh rosemary adds an aromatic touch. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware, under natural, even lighting. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Flip. Sear other side, 3 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, Kalamata olives, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer for 30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve individual chicken thighs with sauce, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Baked Chicken Thighs with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of crispy baked chicken and roasted broccoli on a round, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, skin-on chicken thighs, cooked whole, are placed on one side. Their skin is visibly crisp, meat tender. Adjacent are vibrant green broccoli florets, roasted to tender-crisp perfection with slight charring. A scoop of fluffy white rice completes the meal, arranged naturally beside the chicken and broccoli. The components touch organically. The plate rests on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded plain cloth napkin and everyday stainless steel cutlery are nearby. Soft, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style with additional side dishes.
Offer ketchup or hot sauce as condiments.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, toss chicken thighs with 30ml olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs skin-side up on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes.
While chicken roasts, toss broccoli florets with remaining 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper in the same bowl.
After 20 minutes, add broccoli to the baking sheet with the chicken.
Continue roasting for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is crispy. Broccoli should be tender-crisp.
Serve immediately with cooked white rice.
notes: Check chicken temperature with a meat thermometer for safety.
Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Cherry-Chocolate Soup
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl holds a generous portion of the hearty beef and cherry-chocolate soup. The soup is a rich, dark brown, thick and comforting. Tender, irregularly shaped beef chunks are visible, alongside softened, dark red cherry halves and finely diced carrots, celery, and onion. A delicate swirl of pale cream floats on the surface. Bright green chopped fresh parsley is scattered across the top, adding a fresh visual accent. The bowl sits on a well-used, dark wooden dining table, showing minor imperfections. A simple ceramic spoon rests on a casually folded linen napkin. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting casts soft shadows. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a comfortable, lived-in family kitchen with a salt and pepper shaker. The scene exudes warmth and comfort.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to pot. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape bottom of pot to release browned bits. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Return beef to pot. Add beef broth, bay leaf, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Add pitted cherries and chopped dark chocolate to pot. Stir until chocolate melts and cherries soften, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
Stir in 100ml heavy cream. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Swirl a little extra cream on top. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: The red wine is optional. If omitted, use additional beef broth.
For a thicker soup, you can mash some of the vegetables or blend a portion of the soup before adding beef back.
Ensure cherries are pitted. Fresh or frozen work equally well.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Parmesan Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Parmesan Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The risotto, a creamy, free-flowing mound of tender brown rice, is infused with a subtle orange hue from tomatoes and speckled with vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes. Its texture is rich and moist, not dry or stiff. Beside the risotto, a thick, pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown exterior, rests as a whole piece, showcasing its juicy interior. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a few torn fresh green basil leaves, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a rustic wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures, creating an approachable yet refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: A glass of crisp white wine
Crusty artisan bread

ingredients.name: Fresh basil, leaves torn or chopped

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil and half the butter. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add brown rice to skillet. Toast 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.

Add hot chicken broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until most liquid is absorbed before adding next ladleful. Continue for 35-45 minutes, or until rice is tender with a slight bite (al dente).
While risotto cooks, halve the cherry tomatoes. Add to risotto during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Once rice is tender, remove from heat. Stir in remaining butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Risotto should be creamy and free-flowing.
Let chicken rest 5 minutes before serving.
Ladle risotto onto plates. Place whole chicken breast beside risotto. Garnish with fresh basil and extra Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Baked Chicken Thighs with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of crispy baked chicken and roasted broccoli on a round, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, skin-on chicken thighs, cooked whole, are placed on one side. Their skin is visibly crisp, meat tender. Adjacent are vibrant green broccoli florets, roasted to tender-crisp perfection with slight charring. A scoop of fluffy white rice completes the meal, arranged naturally beside the chicken and broccoli. The components touch organically. The plate rests on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded plain cloth napkin and everyday stainless steel cutlery are nearby. Soft, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style with additional side dishes.
Offer ketchup or hot sauce as condiments.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, toss chicken thighs with 30ml olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs skin-side up on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes.
While chicken roasts, toss broccoli florets with remaining 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper in the same bowl.
After 20 minutes, add broccoli to the baking sheet with the chicken.
Continue roasting for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is crispy. Broccoli should be tender-crisp.
Serve immediately with cooked white rice.

Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Mushroom Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Chicken and Mushroom Rice is served in a round, shallow, everyday ceramic bowl. The rice is fluffy and golden-brown, studded with browned chicken chunks, earthy sliced mushrooms, and softened onion. Chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing rustic appeal. A few vibrant green chopped parsley leaves are sprinkled over the top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually placed beside it. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures casts soft shadows. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere, perhaps a blurred edge of another simple ceramic dish. No distracting elements. A comfortable, generous single serving.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in uncooked rice. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and hot sauce. Stir well. Bring mixture to a boil.
Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove skillet from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Pork with Tomato, Fermented Brown Rice, and Pickled Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial portion of slow-braised pork shoulder rests centrally on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, showcasing its rich, deep brown crust and tender, glistening interior. The pork, presented as a whole, un-sliced chunk, is generously coated in a rustic, vibrant red-orange tomato braising sauce, speckled with soft, diced carrot and onion. Alongside, a generous mound of earthy brown rice, its grains distinct and slightly al dente, provides textural contrast. A small, artfully placed cluster of thinly sliced, bright pink pickled red onions sits delicately on the rice, offering a sharp visual and flavor counterpoint. The plate is set on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the inherent beauty of each ingredient against a clean, minimalist background with subtle green plant accents, ensuring the food remains the focal point.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (onion ends, carrot peels, celery leaves)
Fermented vegetable broth
ingredients.quantity: 500ml (e.g., brine from homemade pickles or stock made from fermented vegetable scraps)

instructions: Thinly slice 1 red onion. In a small saucepan, combine 100ml apple cider vinegar, 100ml water, 10g sugar, 5g sea salt, and 5g black peppercorns. Bring to a simmer until salt and sugar dissolve. Pour hot liquid over sliced onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate.

Pat pork shoulder chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork.

Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced carrot, celery, and the remaining 1 diced red onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add diced tomatoes, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs. Stir well.

Return seared pork to the pot. Add enough water or vegetable scrap broth to mostly cover the pork. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Simmer 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Turn pork every hour.

Rinse brown rice thoroughly. In a medium saucepan, combine 300g brown rice with 600ml fermented vegetable broth. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 40-45 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Remove pork from pot. Skim any excess fat from braising liquid. Remove bay leaves and thyme stems. If sauce is too thin, reduce over medium-high heat until slightly thickened. Taste and adjust seasoning. Return pork to sauce.
Place a mound of fermented brown rice on each plate. Arrange one pork chunk next to the rice. Spoon braising sauce over the pork and rice. Garnish with a small cluster of pickled red onions.
notes: This recipe emphasizes using all parts of ingredients. Pork bones and vegetable scraps can be used to make a flavorful broth for the braise or rice. The pickled onions offer a vibrant, fermented element and can be made in advance. This dish celebrates clean, simple flavors and eco-conscious cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Chickpea Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Bell Pepper and Chickpea Pasta Salad is casually presented on an everyday white ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The dish features a colorful mix of al dente fusilli pasta, vibrant diced red and yellow bell peppers, crisp diced cucumber, bright red halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, earthy chickpeas, dark halved Kalamata olives, and creamy crumbled feta. Fresh chopped parsley is scattered throughout, adding a pop of green. A simple vinaigrette coats all components, enhancing their natural sheen. The ingredients are loosely arranged, with some overlapping, creating a natural, inviting appearance. A plain silver fork rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting, casting soft shadows. A casually placed plain linen napkin sits nearby. The overall presentation is homely and unpretentious, reflecting a comforting, family-style meal.
instructions: Cook fusilli pasta according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain pasta. Rinse with cold water to cool. Drain well.

In a large bowl, combine diced red bell pepper, diced yellow bell pepper, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, rinsed chickpeas, halved Kalamata olives, and crumbled feta cheese.
Add cooled pasta to the vegetable mixture.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Pour dressing over pasta and vegetable mixture. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve immediately or chill for later.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber and Grilled Beef Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai Cucumber and Grilled Beef Salad is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Thinly sliced grilled beef, cooked to a tender medium, is casually interspersed among generous portions of thinly sliced cucumbers, quartered cherry tomatoes, and fine slivers of red onion. Fresh green cilantro and mint leaves are generously scattered throughout, adding color and texture. A clear, spicy lime dressing pools slightly at the bottom, glistening on the fresh ingredients. The dish features a medley of natural greens, reds, and the rich brown of the beef, with the beef slices laid naturally, not fanned. The setting includes a simple, everyday ceramic plate, a pair of wooden chopsticks resting beside the bowl, and a small, unpretentious side dish of sticky rice. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene, evoking a relaxed family meal atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of warm sticky rice or jasmine rice.
Offer extra chili flakes or lime wedges on the side for individual adjustment.

ingredients.name: Lettuce leaves (e.g., romaine or butter lettuce)

instructions: Pat beef dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat a grill pan or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Grill beef for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached (internal temperature 60-65°C). Rest beef for 5 minutes.
While beef rests, prepare dressing. Mince garlic. In a small bowl, combine fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, minced garlic, and chili flakes. Whisk until sugar dissolves.
Thinly slice cucumber. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion. Roughly chop cilantro and tear mint leaves.
Thinly slice rested beef against the grain.
In a large bowl, combine sliced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, cilantro, mint, and beef slices. Pour dressing over ingredients.
Gently toss to combine. Arrange lettuce leaves on serving plates. Spoon salad mixture over lettuce.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Potato Medley
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken and potato medley is presented on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate. Two bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, deeply golden-brown and crispy, are nestled amongst chunky, rustic potato wedges. The potatoes are roasted to a tender interior with a crisp, golden exterior, showcasing their natural imperfections. Scattered among the chicken and potatoes are softened, caramelized onion slices and roasted garlic cloves. A few fresh sprigs of rosemary are casually placed on top, adding a touch of green. The dish is arranged naturally, components touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a comforting, home-cooked meal. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, natural overhead light. A simple cloth napkin and standard metal cutlery are casually placed beside the plate. The overall scene is homely and inviting, without any pretense or overly styled elements, emphasizing hearty satisfaction.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges or chunks. Slice onion into thick pieces.
