In a large mixing bowl, combine potato wedges, onion slices, minced garlic, olive oil, rosemary sprigs, and thyme leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken thighs and seasoned potato mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet or roasting pan. Ensure chicken skin is facing up.
Roast for 40-50 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden and crispy. Potatoes should be tender and browned.
Check chicken internal temperature. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve warm directly from the pan or on individual plates.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Chasseur
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic Chicken Chasseur rests on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Large, golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks are nestled amidst vibrant sautéed red and yellow bell pepper strips, tender sliced button mushrooms, and diced onions, all coated in a rich, glossy tomato-based sauce. The sauce, a deep reddish-brown, pools slightly around the ingredients, showing flecks of herbs. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The chicken exhibits a tender, moist texture. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin to the left and a silver fork and knife to the right. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's textures. The background suggests a modern bistro with soft, muted tones, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French bread for dipping
Serve with steamed rice or simple potato gratin
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 5 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and sliced bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and brown slightly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.

Return seared chicken to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender. Internal temperature of chicken should reach 75°C.
Remove thyme sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley just before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Gaeng Hung Lay (Northern Thai Pork Curry)
recipes.visual_description: The Gaeng Hung Lay is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, reddish-brown hue. Tender, slow-braised pork shoulder chunks, each about 4-5cm, are nestled within the thick, glossy curry sauce. The pork, fork-tender, reveals subtle marbling. The sauce, glistening with rendered pork fat, is studded with whole roasted peanuts and thinly sliced pickled garlic cloves. A mound of fluffy white jasmine rice is served alongside in a separate, smaller white porcelain bowl. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, vibrant green coriander leaves, providing a fresh contrast. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and traditional Thai spoon and fork. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its warmth and depth without overcrowding the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with jasmine rice
Fresh vegetables on the side
Pickled mustard greens
instructions: Prepare curry paste: Combine soaked dried chilies, shallots, garlic, fresh ginger, galangal, lemongrass, coriander root, shrimp paste, white peppercorns, roasted cumin seeds, roasted coriander seeds, cardamom seeds, nutmeg, turmeric powder, and Thai curry powder in a mortar and pestle. Pound until a fine, aromatic paste forms. Alternatively, use a food processor.
Brown pork: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add pork shoulder chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot and set aside.
Cook curry: Reduce heat to medium. Add curry paste to the pot. Stir-fry paste for 5-7 minutes until very fragrant and oil separates. Return browned pork to the pot. Stir to coat pork with paste.

Braise curry: Add palm sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste. Stir well. Pour in water or stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Finish curry: Add roasted peanuts and sliced pickled garlic (if using) to the curry. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Cook rice: While curry simmers, rinse jasmine rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package instructions, typically 1 part rice to 1.5 parts water. Fluff with a fork when done.
Serve: Ladle Gaeng Hung Lay into deep serving bowls. Serve immediately with a separate bowl of fluffy jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken Fettuccine
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single individual portion. A generous mound of al dente fettuccine, coated in a creamy, pale ivory sauce, forms the base. Nestled within and around the pasta are succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks, each about 2.5 cm in size, showing a slight char from searing. Vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color and texture. The sauce has a smooth, rich consistency, lightly clinging to the pasta strands. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a fresh, aromatic garnish on top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Add fresh spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add cooked chicken chunks to the sauce. Stir to combine.
Add drained fettuccine to the pan with the sauce and chicken. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.
Do not overcook pasta; it should be al dente.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Vegetable Primavera Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Roasted Vegetable Primavera Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. The al dente pasta forms a gentle mound, artfully intertwined with vibrant, roasted vegetables. Visible elements include tender-crisp broccoli florets, caramelized carrot rounds, soft roughly chopped onion pieces, and burst halved cherry tomatoes, showcasing deep greens, bright reds, and golden browns. Each ingredient retains its distinct shape and texture. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the pasta, with fresh green basil leaves scattered over the top for color. The arrangement is organic, leaving ample negative space. A folded white cotton napkin and simple silver flatware rest beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
Offer additional grated Parmesan at the table.
Pair with a light white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
On a large baking sheet, toss broccoli florets, carrot slices, and chopped onion with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized. Add halved cherry tomatoes for the last 10 minutes of roasting.
While vegetables roast, cook pasta according to package directions in a large pot of salted water until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water before draining.
In a large skillet or pot, heat remaining 30ml olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add roasted vegetables to the skillet. Stir gently.
Add cooked pasta, vegetable broth, and reserved pasta water to the skillet. Toss to combine, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped basil.
notes: Roasting vegetables enhances their sweetness and adds depth of flavor.
Reserving pasta water helps create a cohesive sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage & Creamy Caper Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Cabbage & Creamy Caper Salad is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl, in a muted, earthy tone like cream or light grey. Shredded fermented white cabbage and vibrant orange carrots form the base, artfully mounded. Thinly sliced red onion rings are interspersed throughout, adding a touch of deep purple. Toasted sunflower seeds provide a contrasting texture and a warm, golden hue. The creamy, off-white caper dressing, flecked with dark caper pieces and fresh green dill, lightly coats the vegetables, binding the elements. The entire dish sits on a light reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by a natural beige undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh textures and natural colors, emphasizing a clean, sustainable aesthetic. The composition is minimalistic, with ample negative space around the bowl, and a hint of a green plant in the soft background.
instructions: Ferment Cabbage: Shred white cabbage and carrots. Combine with 20g sea salt and 5g black peppercorns. Massage mixture until liquid releases. Pack tightly into a 1-liter clean glass jar. Pour filtered water over vegetables until submerged. Ensure no air pockets. Seal jar with an airlock lid or tightly sealed lid, burping daily if using a regular lid. Ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Dressing: In a medium bowl, whisk together 100ml oat milk, 30g chopped capers, 15ml organic ketchup, 15ml fresh lemon juice, and 2g freshly ground black pepper. Slowly drizzle in 45ml extra virgin olive oil while continuously whisking until dressing is smooth and emulsified. Stir in 10g fresh dill, chopped.

Assemble Salad: Drain 400g fermented cabbage and carrots. Place in a large mixing bowl. Add 50g thinly sliced red onion and 40g toasted sunflower seeds. Pour prepared dressing over. Toss gently to evenly coat all ingredients. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Cucumber Soy Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Potato and Cucumber Soy Salad is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl, typical of Japanese home dining. Boiled potato chunks, approximately 2 cm cubes, form the base, their soft texture contrasting with the crisp, thinly sliced cucumber rounds and juicy, diced red tomatoes. Finely sliced red onion pieces are subtly mixed throughout. A light, glossy soy-based dressing evenly coats all components, enhancing their natural colors—creamy white potatoes, vibrant green cucumber, and deep red tomatoes. The arrangement is casual and abundant, with ingredients naturally overlapping. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, with a plain cloth napkin casually placed.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside steamed white rice.
Pairs well with grilled fish or a simple miso soup.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Place potato cubes in a pot. Cover with cold water. Add 2 grams of salt.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until fork-tender.
Drain potatoes well. Let cool slightly.
While potatoes cook, prepare other vegetables. Slice cucumber into thin rounds.
Dice tomatoes into 1.5 cm pieces.
Thinly slice red onion. Soak onion in cold water for 5 minutes to reduce pungency. Drain well.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, 3 grams of salt, and black pepper for the dressing.
In a large bowl, gently combine the cooled potatoes, sliced cucumber, diced tomatoes, and sliced red onion.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Gently toss to coat all ingredients.
Serve immediately or chill for 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds if desired.
notes: Soaking red onion in cold water reduces its sharp pungency.
Adjust sweetness or tanginess of dressing to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Mushroom Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked whole, displays a rich golden-brown crust. A luscious, creamy mushroom sauce, light beige in color with visible sliced cremini mushrooms, is generously spooned over and around the chicken, pooling gracefully on the plate. The sauce has a smooth, rich texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a color contrast and fresh garnish on top of the chicken and sauce. The composition is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware, a fork and knife, are placed beside the plate. A folded white cotton napkin is neatly positioned. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish. The background suggests a modern bistro setting, subtly out of focus.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced shallots to the same skillet. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Simmer for 2 minutes until wine is mostly reduced.
Stir in chicken broth and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, reducing liquid slightly.
Pour in heavy cream. Continue to simmer gently for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens to desired consistency. Remove thyme sprigs.
Stir in butter until melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet with the sauce. Spoon sauce over chicken to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Tenderloin with Cherry-Dark Chocolate Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared pork tenderloin is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork is cut into thick medallions, displaying a beautiful golden-brown sear on the exterior and tender, slightly pink interior. They are arranged naturally, not fanned. A rich, glossy cherry-dark chocolate reduction generously coats the pork, featuring vibrant halves of fresh cherries. Beside the pork, a creamy, free-flowing mound of golden polenta sits. A fresh sprig of green thyme provides a subtle color contrast. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard flatware placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation typical of a modern bistro.
instructions: Pat pork tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Cut into 2 cm thick medallions.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pork to a plate. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add shallots to skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine and balsamic vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock and half of the fresh cherries. Simmer 5 minutes. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Return pork medallions to skillet. Turn to coat in sauce. Add remaining fresh cherries. Simmer 2 minutes until pork is heated through and cooked to internal temperature of 63°C (145°F).
Stir in butter until melted and glossy. Remove from heat.

For polenta: Bring water or milk to a boil in a saucepan. Whisk in polenta slowly. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, 15-20 minutes until creamy and tender. Stir in Parmesan cheese, salt, and pepper.
Serve pork medallions immediately with cherry-dark chocolate reduction. Serve alongside creamy polenta. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken with Orecchiette and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, inviting main course presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of golden saffron-infused rice, fluffy and fragrant, forms the base. Nestled atop the rice are two succulent, whole chicken thighs, seared to a rich golden-brown and glistening with a creamy, herb-flecked Tuscan sauce. The sauce, a light orange hue from sun-dried tomatoes, generously coats plump orecchiette pasta, which is interspersed with wilted dark green spinach. Alongside the chicken, perfectly roasted broccoli florets display vibrant green hues with delicate charred edges, adding textural contrast. A light sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness. The dish is arranged naturally, allowing each component to be clearly visible, creating a balanced and appealing composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping the sauce

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes
ingredients.quantity: 60g, packed in oil, drained and sliced

instructions: Prepare Saffron Rice: Rinse rice. In a saucepan, melt 10g butter. Add rice. Toast 1 minute. Add 400ml water, saffron, pinch salt. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Cook 15-18 minutes until water absorbed. Let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with fork.
Roast Broccoli: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Cook Pasta: Bring large pot of salted water to boil. Add orecchiette. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Reserve 125ml pasta water.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken. Set aside.

Make Sauce: Reduce heat to medium. Add 5g butter to skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in sliced sun-dried tomatoes.

Pour in chicken broth. Bring to simmer. Scrape up browned bits. Stir in heavy cream. Bring to gentle simmer. Return chicken to skillet. Simmer 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly and chicken is heated through.
Stir in fresh spinach until wilted. Stir in cooked orecchiette and reserved pasta water. Add grated Parmesan. Toss to coat pasta and chicken.
Serve: Divide saffron rice among 4 plates. Top each with creamy Tuscan chicken and orecchiette. Arrange roasted broccoli florets beside chicken. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Turkey and Beer Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a hearty, rustic appeal, served in a clean, wide-rimmed white porcelain dinner bowl. Fluffy long-grain rice, infused with a rich reddish-brown hue from smoked paprika, forms the base. Evenly distributed browned ground turkey provides substantial texture. Visible elements include soft diced onion, minced red chili, and bright green flecks of fresh coriander. The dish has a cohesive, moist texture, not dry or soupy, mounded naturally in the bowl. Garnished generously with vibrant green chopped fresh coriander. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded light grey cotton napkin beside the bowl. A modern silver spoon rests within the dish. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish as the main subject. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Prepare ingredients: Dice 1 large onion. Mince 4 cloves garlic and 1-2 red chilies (deseeded). Chop 20g fresh coriander.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add 500g ground turkey. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Drain excess fat. Remove turkey and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 10g smoked paprika, 5g ground cumin, and 3g dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in 250ml beer. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in 750ml beef stock and 300g long-grain rice. Season with 5g salt and 2g black pepper.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid.
Return cooked turkey to the pot. Gently fluff rice with a fork to combine.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Serve hot. Garnish generously with chopped fresh coriander.
notes: For an extra creamy touch, a dollop of sour cream or Greek yogurt can be added as a garnish just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single, generous individual portion on an everyday round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Whole roasted chicken thighs, their skin golden-brown and crispy, are nestled among tender, fluffy 3 cm potato chunks. Some potato edges are slightly caramelized. Thick wedges of soft, sweet roasted onion and smashed garlic cloves are interspersed throughout. A few fresh rosemary sprigs and scattered leaves provide a vibrant green contrast. Natural pan juices lightly pool around the ingredients, adding a glossy sheen. The arrangement is organic and casual, as if plated directly from the roasting pan in a home kitchen. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, lived-in atmosphere. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate, with a casually folded cloth napkin nearby.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Cut onion into thick wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, onion, and smashed garlic. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, 0.5 teaspoon black pepper, and leaves from 1 sprig fresh rosemary. Toss to coat.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon black pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan. Pour chicken broth into the pan. Add the remaining rosemary sprig.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and potatoes are tender. Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Do not overcrowd the roasting pan to ensure even cooking and crispiness.
Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey Garlic Chicken with Roasted Broccoli and Carrot Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Honey Garlic Chicken with Roasted Broccoli and Carrot Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pan-seared chicken pieces, cooked to a golden-brown, are arranged centrally, coated in a glossy, dark amber honey-garlic glaze. The chicken is presented as whole, irregular chunks, not sliced. Alongside, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets are clustered, showing slight charring on their edges. A neat mound of fluffy white Jasmine rice, speckled with small, bright orange diced carrots, sits slightly off-center. A light scattering of toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green onion batons garnishes the chicken, adding subtle contrast and freshness. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's distinct components. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks resting on a small ceramic chopstick rest. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a clean, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with chopsticks and a small rice bowl
A side of kimchi or pickled daikon could accompany for added flavor contrast
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, and 60ml water/broth. Stir in cornstarch until dissolved. Set aside.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken thighs. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Keep warm.
While chicken cooks, wash rice thoroughly. Dice carrots into small cubes.

In a medium saucepan, combine washed rice, diced carrots, and 600ml water/broth. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with remaining 15ml vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast broccoli for 15-20 minutes, or until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Pour the prepared sauce into the pan used for chicken. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Return chicken to the pan, coating evenly with the sauce.
Fluff the cooked rice with a fork.
Serve chicken pieces with a side of carrot rice and roasted broccoli. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple-Potato Rosti and Thyme Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with crisp skin, is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a whole, plump piece, unsliced. Beside it, a circular apple-potato rosti, roughly 10 cm in diameter, displays a beautifully golden, slightly rustic, crisp exterior with hints of shredded potato and apple texture. A rich, glossy brown thyme jus is spooned artistically over a portion of the chicken and pools around the base. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the chicken. The color palette is warm with the golden chicken and rosti, contrasting with the deep brown jus. Moderate negative space surrounds the components. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Firm, tart apples (e.g., Granny Smith or Honeycrisp)

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Grate potatoes and apples using a coarse grater. Place grated potato and apple in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze out excess moisture firmly. Discard liquid.
Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

In a large non-stick pan, heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter over medium heat. Add grated potato and apple. Season with salt and pepper. Cook, pressing down with a spatula, until golden brown and crisp on the bottom, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and cook other side until golden and tender, about 6-8 minutes. Form into 4 individual rostis. Keep warm.

In a separate large oven-safe pan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crisp. Flip chicken. Add 2 thyme sprigs and 20g butter to the pan. Baste chicken with melted butter.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.

While chicken rests, return pan to stovetop over medium heat. Add diced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. Deglaze pan with chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Add remaining 4 thyme sprigs. Reduce liquid by half, about 5-7 minutes. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve into a small saucepan. Discard solids and thyme.
Whisk in remaining 20g butter into the jus until melted and glossy. Season jus with salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, place one apple-potato rosti on each plate. Place one chicken breast beside the rosti. Spoon thyme jus generously over and around the chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Chili Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Hearty Beef and Potato Chili Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with earthy tones. The rich, reddish-brown broth, thickened slightly with flour, holds substantial chunks of seared beef (diced), tender diced potatoes, vibrant diced red and green bell peppers, and bits of stewed tomato. The soup has a hearty, slightly chunky texture. A small amount of fresh, finely chopped parsley is sprinkled over the top, adding a touch of green color. The bowl sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. Alongside the bowl, a thick slice of crusty, rustic bread is casually placed. The scene is lit with warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear diced beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in diced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 3 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add diced potatoes, canned diced tomatoes, beef stock, chili powder, Dijon mustard, and hot sauce (if using).
Bring soup to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 60-75 minutes. Cook until beef is tender and potatoes are cooked through. Ensure beef reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Corn Risotto, Crispy Potatoes, and Basil Orzo Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Corn Risotto, Crispy Potatoes, and Basil Orzo Salad. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The pan-seared chicken breast, with its golden-brown crust, is positioned prominently on one side of the plate. Beside it, a free-flowing mound of creamy, pale yellow corn risotto is ladled, showcasing visible sweet corn kernels and a smooth, fluid texture. Several crispy roasted potato chunks, irregularly shaped and golden-brown with slightly charred edges, are artfully arranged nearby, adding textural contrast. A vibrant green basil orzo salad, featuring al dente orzo pasta interspersed with bright red halved cherry tomatoes and flecks of fresh, roughly chopped basil, provides a fresh, colorful counterpoint. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate, with standard modern flatware. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., baby potatoes, Yukon Gold)
ingredients.quantity: 500g, scrubbed and quartered or cut into 2-3cm chunks

ingredients.name: White wine vinegar or lemon juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato chunks with 30ml olive oil, 5g salt, and 2g pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-40 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and crispy.

Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add orzo and cook according to package directions until al dente (approx. 8-10 minutes). Drain well and rinse with cold water to stop cooking and prevent sticking.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Arborio rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent. Pour in white wine (if using) and cook until fully absorbed, stirring frequently.

Add hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in corn kernels during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Once rice is al dente, remove from heat. Stir in Parmesan cheese and butter until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.

While risotto finishes, pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest for 5 minutes.

In a bowl, combine cooked orzo, halved cherry tomatoes, and chopped basil. Dress with 30ml extra virgin olive oil, 15ml white wine vinegar or lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently to combine.

Ladle a generous portion of creamy corn risotto onto each plate. Place one pan-seared chicken breast beside the risotto. Arrange a portion of crispy roasted potatoes and a scoop of basil orzo salad on the plate. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Rice & Roasted Chicken Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with earthy, natural tones (e.g., beige or light grey). A generous, gently mounded portion of fluffy, off-white fermented rice forms the base on one side of the bowl. Adjacent to the rice, a whole, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, with visibly crispy skin and tender meat, is placed as the focal point. The chicken is not sliced. Beside the chicken, vibrant orange pickled carrot ribbons are artfully arranged in a loose, natural curl, adding a pop of color and texture. A rich, dark brown onion jus is drizzled elegantly over the chicken and around the base of the rice, creating a subtle sheen. The plating emphasizes clean lines, ample white space, and the inherent beauty of each ingredient. No excessive garnishes; perhaps a single delicate sprig of fresh thyme or a small, tender carrot green is placed lightly near the chicken. The scene is set on a light-colored, natural wood or stone surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing textures and colors. The background is minimalist and clean, with subtle hints of natural elements like a blurred plant or simple wall, ensuring the food remains the central subject.
instructions: Day 1: Prepare Fermented Rice. Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice, 600ml water, and 12g sea salt in a clean jar. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days. Small bubbles will appear.

Day 3: Prepare Pickled Carrots. Wash carrots. Peel two carrots into thin ribbons using a vegetable peeler. Bring 100ml white wine vinegar, 100ml water, and 10g sugar to a boil. Pour over carrot ribbons. Let cool. Refrigerate.

Prepare Onion Jus. Reserve chicken bones and trimmings after butchering (if applicable). Roughly chop one large onion. Smash 3 garlic cloves. In a saucepan, add 10ml olive oil. Sauté chopped onion, smashed garlic, and chicken bones/trimmings until lightly browned. Add 400ml chicken stock. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain, discarding solids. Reduce liquid over medium heat until thickened to a jus consistency. Season with salt and pepper.

Prepare Roasted Chicken. Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Finely slice remaining large onion. Smash remaining 3 garlic cloves. In an oven-safe pan, toss sliced onion, smashed garlic, and thyme sprigs with 20ml olive oil. Place chicken thighs skin-side up over the onion mixture.
Roast chicken for 30-35 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is crispy. Let rest 5 minutes.

Cook Fermented Rice. Drain fermented rice. Rinse lightly under cold water. Cook rice according to package directions using fresh water (or chicken stock for extra flavor), ensuring it is tender and fluffy.

Assemble bowls. Place a mound of cooked fermented rice in each bowl. Arrange one roasted chicken thigh alongside. Neatly place pickled carrot ribbons next to the chicken. Drizzle onion jus over the chicken and around the plate. Serve immediately.
notes: Fermentation time for rice can vary based on ambient temperature. Adjust as needed until a pleasant tang is achieved.
For zero-waste, utilize chicken bones and vegetable scraps (onion skins, carrot peels) for the chicken stock used in the jus.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Corn Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Cheesy Chicken and Corn Bake is presented on an everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The dish features chunky, seared chicken cubes interspersed with bright yellow sweetcorn kernels, all enrobed in a creamy, rich cheddar cheese sauce. The top layer of cheese is melted and golden brown, showing a slight bubbling texture. The components are naturally arranged, touching and overlapping in a casual, asymmetrical manner, filling the plate without overcrowding. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of natural color. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, cozy lighting suggesting a relaxed family dining area. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed nearby, and basic flatware is arranged for a homely, lived-in atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the comfort food in its natural, appetizing state.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add a little oil.
Sear chicken cubes until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add butter to the skillet. Melt butter over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, whisking until sauce thickens.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in 150g of grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
Stir in the seared chicken cubes and drained sweetcorn.
Pour mixture into a 20x30 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet.
Sprinkle remaining 50g of grated cheddar cheese over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbling and cheese is golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Tuscan Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The penne pasta is generously coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce, interspersed with succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks, each about 3-4 cm. The sauce has visible specks of finely diced onion and garlic, with the occasional pop of vibrant red cherry tomatoes. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered throughout, adding color and freshness. A generous dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese rests atop the dish. The texture is invitingly rustic, with the tender pasta and hearty chicken. The plate sits on a warm, natural wooden table, accompanied by a simple white cotton napkin and a silver fork, under soft, even natural lighting. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
While sauce simmers, cook penne rigate pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked pasta and halved cherry tomatoes to the sauce. Toss well to coat all ingredients. If needed, add reserved pasta water to reach desired consistency.
Stir in fresh basil leaves.
Serve immediately, topped with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Rustico al Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh rests centrally on a rustic, cream-colored ceramic plate. The chicken, cooked until fall-off-the-bone tender, is generously coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce, thickened naturally from the crushed tomatoes. The sauce pools around the chicken, revealing small, soft chunks of tomato and finely diced onion. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are torn and scattered casually over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The chicken skin, where visible, shows a hint of its initial golden-brown sear. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple, everyday fork and knife rest beside the plate. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting appeal of the dish. A piece of crusty Italian bread, perfect for soaking up the savory sauce, sits next to the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the savory tomato sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Can be served over pasta or polenta for a heartier meal.
instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. This takes about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Stir to combine. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken pieces to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce. If not, add a little more broth.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Taste the sauce and adjust salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with torn fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: This dish often tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.
Adjust the amount of chicken broth to achieve your preferred sauce consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rosemary Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a rustic white ceramic plate. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is the focal point. Around it are scattered golden-brown potato wedges, some with slightly charred edges, alongside soft, caramelized chunks of roasted onion and tender, smashed garlic cloves. Fresh rosemary sprigs and a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley add color and aroma. A roasted lemon wedge sits beside the chicken. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The overall impression is warm and hearty. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic European flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, warm light illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pair with a glass of dry Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs and drumsticks)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Roughly chop the onion. Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
Slice half of the lemon into thin rounds. Juice the other half.
In a large roasting pan, combine chicken, potato wedges, chopped onion, smashed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and lemon slices. Drizzle with olive oil. Toss everything to coat evenly.
Roast for 30 minutes. Turn chicken and potatoes.
Pour white wine and chicken broth into the pan. Stir gently.
Continue roasting for another 25-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden brown. Baste occasionally with pan juices.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with fresh lemon juice. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for safety.
For extra crispness, increase oven temperature to 220°C (425°F) for the last 10 minutes, monitoring closely.
traditional_techniques: Seasoning with fresh herbs and lemon

recipes.recipe_name: Kimchi Chicken & Udon Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Kimchi Chicken & Udon Stir-fry is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, leaving ample negative space. A bed of thick, white Udon noodles forms the base, loosely coiled. Irregularly shaped, golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 3 cm, are nestled among the noodles. Bright orange julienned carrots and translucent julienned onions are interspersed throughout. Vibrant red-orange kimchi pieces are prominently featured, providing a burst of color and texture. The dish has a natural, unfussy composition. A scattering of thinly sliced green scallions provides a fresh, natural garnish. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface. Adjacent to the main plate, a small, matching ceramic bowl holds a modest portion of extra kimchi. Undyed linen napkins in a natural beige tone are neatly folded. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural plant foliage blurred softly, emphasizing the eco-conscious and sustainable aesthetic. Traditional dark wood chopsticks rest beside the plate, completing the authentic Korean dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional kimchi on the side.
Offer a small bowl of clear, light broth as an accompaniment.
Accompany with other traditional Korean banchan (small side dishes) such as pickled radishes or seasoned spinach.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Mince garlic. Julienne onion. Julienne carrot into thin strips.
Heat rapeseed oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add onion and carrot to the wok. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Add minced garlic. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add kimchi to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Combine soy sauce, sesame oil, gochujang, rice vinegar, and chicken stock in a small bowl. Mix well.
Add Udon noodles to the wok. Pour in the sauce mixture. Toss to coat.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing noodles to heat through and absorb flavors.
Slice scallions thinly for garnish.
Serve immediately, garnished with sliced scallions.
notes: To enhance sustainability, use chicken bones to make homemade chicken stock. Freeze excess for future use.
Regrow scallions by placing the white root ends in a shallow glass of water.
Adjust gochujang quantity to control spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Vegetable Stew with Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of hearty beef and vegetable stew is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl. The stew is rich and thick, featuring tender, dark brown beef chunks (3-4 cm cubes) nestled among vibrant orange carrot and creamy yellow potato chunks (2-3 cm pieces). Small pasta, like ditalini, is visibly mixed throughout the savory, reddish-brown tomato-based broth. Finely chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled on top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin rests beside the bowl. A slice of crusty, artisanal bread with a golden-brown crust is placed nearby. Warm, inviting lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen. The focus is on the comforting, natural appearance of the food.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm cubes
Carrots, peeled, cut into 2 cm chunks
Potatoes, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef in batches until seared on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in carrots and potatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return browned beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Skim any fat from the surface if desired. Adjust seasoning.
Add pasta directly to the stew. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or according to package directions, until al dente.
Remove bay leaves before serving. Serve hot with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Creamy Mushroom and Mustard Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables is artfully arranged: thick potato wedges, tender butternut squash cubes, caramelized red onion wedges, bright bell pepper strips, and burst cherry tomatoes. Each vegetable shows distinct roasted edges. A rich, creamy mushroom and mustard sauce, studded with bright green peas, yellow corn kernels, and dark olive slices, is generously spooned over the chicken and vegetables, creating an inviting flow. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Mixed salad greens
Fresh bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, butternut squash cubes, red onion wedges, bell pepper strips, cherry tomatoes, and smashed garlic. Drizzle with 45ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up among the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip chicken. Continue roasting for 20-30 minutes more, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
While chicken roasts, prepare the sauce. Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the saucepan. Sauté until browned and their liquid has evaporated, about 7-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thickened.
Stir in Dijon mustard, soy sauce, and a pinch of sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add frozen green peas and corn kernels. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until heated through. Stir in sliced black olives. Keep warm.
Once chicken and vegetables are roasted, remove from oven.
To serve, place a roasted chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange a generous portion of roasted vegetables beside it. Spoon creamy mushroom and mustard sauce over chicken and vegetables.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately with a side of mixed salad greens tossed in vinaigrette.

recipes.recipe_name: French Braised Chicken with Olives and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: This dish is plated in a clean, professional restaurant style on a round white porcelain dinner plate. A single braised chicken thigh, golden-brown from searing and glistening with rich sauce, is positioned slightly off-center. The chicken is whole, not sliced. It rests on a generous bed of rustic, savory tomato-olive sauce. The sauce is a deep reddish-orange, studded with dark, plump Kalamata olives and flecks of vibrant green herbs. The chicken skin is crisp on top, contrasting with the tender, moist meat beneath. A light scattering of fresh, chopped bright green parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space around the central elements. The colors are natural and appealing: golden-brown chicken, rich red sauce, dark purple-black olives, and fresh green herbs. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimal, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction. A traditional European-style fork and knife are placed to the side of the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with simple boiled potatoes or rice to absorb the rich sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crisp (5-7 minutes). Flip and sear other side (3-4 minutes). Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent (5-7 minutes).
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce.
Add pitted olives.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F).
Remove from oven. Discard thyme sprigs, rosemary sprig, and bay leaf.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning if needed.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The sauce can be made ahead and gently reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice with Cucumber Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spanish Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a rustic wooden table. Golden-brown chicken chunks are nestled into the vibrant, reddish-orange rice. The rice is studded with diced red and yellow bell peppers and diced onion, showcasing a rich paprika hue. A spoonful of bright green cucumber salsa, made with finely diced cucumber and fresh parsley, rests atop the chicken and rice. A lemon wedge sits beside the dish. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, with a simple, folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. A traditional Spanish ceramic serving bowl (cazuela) with a pattern is visible in the background, adding cultural depth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Cook chicken to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to skillet. Add diced onion and diced bell peppers (red and yellow). Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked rice and diced tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Pour in chicken broth. Stir gently to combine.
Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly. Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

While rice cooks, prepare cucumber salsa. Dice cucumber into small cubes. In a small bowl, combine diced cucumber, half of the chopped fresh parsley, and juice from half a lemon. Season with salt to taste.
Once rice is cooked, remove skillet from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Stir in remaining fresh parsley.
Serve Spanish chicken and rice hot. Top each portion with a spoonful of fresh cucumber salsa. Garnish with a lemon wedge.
notes: For extra flavor, consider adding a pinch of saffron threads to the chicken broth when cooking the rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Ma Yi Shang Shu (Ants Climbing a Tree)
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Ma Yi Shang Shu is presented in a deep, traditional ceramic rice bowl, resting on a sturdy, well-used wooden dining table. The bowl is filled with finely crumbled ground pork generously coating translucent, tangled bean thread noodles. The pork is cooked to a rich, reddish-brown hue, interspersed with vibrant green scallion pieces and dark red dried chili segments. The noodles are glossy and plump, having absorbed the savory, spicy sauce. A small, separate bowl of fluffy white steamed rice sits immediately beside the main dish. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests casually on the table, ready for use. The scene is bathed in warm, natural light, creating an inviting, homely kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of simple pickled vegetables.
instructions: Soak bean thread noodles in hot water for 10 minutes. Drain. Cut into shorter segments.
Mince garlic and ginger. Chop scallions, separating white and green parts.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat.
Add Sichuan peppercorns. Fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Remove and discard peppercorns.
Add ground pork to the pan. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned and crumbled. Drain excess fat.
Push pork to one side. Add minced garlic, ginger, and white scallion parts. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add doubanjiang and dried red chilies. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until oil turns red and fragrant.
Stir pork back into the mixture. Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine. Mix well.
Add drained noodles and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until noodles absorb most of the liquid.
Stir in sesame oil. Garnish with green scallion parts.
Serve immediately.
notes: The dish's name, 'Ants Climbing a Tree,' refers to the appearance of the minced pork clinging to the bean thread noodles.
traditional_techniques: Use of doubanjiang for authentic Sichuan flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato and Tomato Salad with Crispy Bread
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, rustic white ceramic plate, featuring a mounded portion of vibrant salad. Golden-brown, tender roasted potato wedges are interspersed throughout. Bright red and yellow burst cherry tomatoes add pops of color and juicy texture. Irregularly torn, golden crispy bread chunks are scattered, providing satisfying crunch. Thinly sliced red onion, vibrant green cucumber chunks, and red bell pepper pieces contribute fresh notes. Dark Kalamata olives and crumbles of white feta cheese are visible. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, and chopped parsley are generously mixed in and garnish the top. A light sheen from the olive oil dressing coats the ingredients. The presentation is natural and abundant, showcasing fresh textures and colors. The plate sits on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting, with soft, natural light. Standard flatware is beside the plate. The background is minimal, focusing on the inviting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional crusty bread on the side for soaking up juices.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm wedges. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, 2 g salt, 1 g black pepper, and 2 g dried oregano on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden-brown.

While potatoes roast, halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper. Add to the baking tray with potatoes during the last 10 minutes of roasting, or roast separately for 10-12 minutes until slightly burst.
Tear rustic bread into irregular 2-3 cm pieces. Toss with 20 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper. Spread on a separate baking tray. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Thinly slice red onion. Cut cucumber and red bell pepper into 2 cm chunks.

Prepare vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 85 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, remaining 3 g dried oregano, 3 g salt, and 2 g black pepper until emulsified.
In a large serving bowl, combine roasted potatoes, roasted tomatoes, crispy bread, sliced red onion, cucumber chunks, bell pepper chunks, and pitted Kalamata olives.
Pour vinaigrette over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat everything evenly.
Roughly tear basil leaves. Chop parsley. Fold most of the fresh basil and parsley into the salad. Crumble feta cheese over the top.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil and parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Mushroom Risotto with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, free-flowing Italian Pork and Mushroom Risotto is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The rich, al dente Arborio rice, infused with savory broth and Parmesan, forms the base. Succulent, golden-brown seared pork chunks are nestled into the risotto, alongside earthy, sautéed cremini mushrooms. Vibrant red, roasted cherry tomatoes are artfully scattered throughout the dish, providing pops of color and sweetness. The risotto's creamy texture contrasts with the tender pork and soft mushrooms. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped Italian parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan cheese complete the presentation. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by traditional silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting warmth and texture. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a perfectly portioned individual serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Cut pork tenderloin into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove pork from pan and set aside.
Slice mushrooms. Add remaining 10 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms and set aside with pork.
Dice onion and mince garlic. Add butter to the pan. Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains become translucent. This is tostato.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Begin adding hot broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait for broth to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next ladleful. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in cooked pork and sautéed mushrooms during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in remaining butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This is mantecatura. Stir vigorously until creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Gently fold in most of the roasted cherry tomatoes. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with remaining roasted tomatoes and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 70°C (158°F) for safe consumption.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Turkey Bolognese with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous mound of al dente tagliatelle, coated in a rich, deeply simmered turkey bolognese sauce, rests centrally on a rustic ceramic plate. The sauce, a warm reddish-brown, is thick with finely diced carrots, celery, and onion, interspersed with savory chunks of browned ground turkey. A few whole basil leaves or chopped fresh parsley are scattered over the top for a pop of green. The pasta strands are intertwined with the hearty sauce, creating a comforting, inviting texture. Grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish, adding a touch of creamy white contrast. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Adjacent are simple, slightly imperfect ceramic bowls holding extra grated Parmesan. A linen napkin is casually folded beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. A few rustic Italian-style bread slices are visible on a small cutting board in the background, along with a simple glass of water.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground turkey. Cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften, stirring occasionally.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits. Cook until wine has mostly evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken or vegetable broth, dried oregano, bay leaf, salt, and black pepper. Stir well to combine.
Bring the sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover partially and simmer for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sauce should thicken and flavors deepen.
Cook tagliatelle pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 125ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Remove the bay leaf from the bolognese sauce. Add the cooked tagliatelle directly to the sauce in the pot. Toss to coat the pasta evenly. If sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh parsley or basil and extra grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Simmering the sauce for a longer period (up to 2 hours) will deepen the flavors further if time permits.
For a richer sauce, a splash of whole milk or cream can be stirred in during the last 10 minutes of simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork with Five Spice and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A deep, clean white ceramic bowl holds a generous portion of fluffy white jasmine rice. Nestled atop the rice are two large, dark, glistening chunks of braised pork shoulder, tender and rich with a deep amber hue. A glossy, dark brown braising liquid pools generously around the pork and rice. Vibrant green blanched bok choy halves are neatly arranged beside the pork. A halved hard-boiled egg, revealing its creamy yellow yolk, rests nearby. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, bright green coriander leaves. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a white porcelain bowl. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. A small ceramic dipping bowl with chili-vinegar sauce and a pair of chopsticks with a spoon on a rest complete the culturally authentic yet refined presentation. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chili-vinegar dipping sauce (Prik Nam Som).
Traditionally eaten with a spoon and fork, not chopsticks, in Thailand.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5-6 cm chunks. Pat dry.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks on all sides until browned. Remove pork.
Add crushed garlic, ginger slices, and coriander roots to the pot. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, five-spice powder, star anise, and cinnamon stick.
Pour in water or pork stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until pork is fork-tender.
Add rehydrated shiitake mushrooms to the pot during the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Cook jasmine rice according to package directions.
Blanch bok choy in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain.
Halve hard-boiled eggs.
Taste braising liquid. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve braised pork and sauce over jasmine rice. Arrange blanched bok choy and halved hard-boiled egg on the side. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Cerdo
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, orange-hued rice known as Arroz con Cerdo, served on a clean white porcelain plate. Large, golden-brown seared pork chunks are distributed throughout the fluffy medium-grain rice. Visible pieces of translucent diced onions, minced garlic, green olives, and small capers add textural variety. The rice is garnished with fresh, bright green chopped cilantro. A side of thick-cut fried sweet plantains rests beside the rice. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table and a neutral cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the moist texture of the meat and individual grains. The entire plate is visible, showing a balanced restaurant portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fried sweet plantains (amarillos)
Accompany with thick slices of fresh avocado
Serve with a side of crispy tostones
instructions: Season pork chunks with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork chunks on all sides until golden. Remove pork from pot.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until translucent.
Stir in tomato sauce, sazón, green olives, and capers.
Return pork to the pot. Add rice and stir to coat grains.
Pour in water. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a caldero for the most authentic rice texture.
Do not stir the rice while simmering to allow a crust (pegao) to form at the bottom.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Savory Chocolate Cheese Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, positioned centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked whole, sits atop a rich, dark reddish-brown savory chocolate cheese sauce. The sauce, smooth and glossy, pools gracefully around the base of the chicken, showing subtle specks of melted cheese curd. A few small, distinct pieces of fresh cheese curd are delicately placed on top of the sauce near the chicken, providing textural contrast. Bright green chopped cilantro is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce. Alongside, vibrant green steamed asparagus spears, cut into batons, provide a balanced vegetable element. The overall presentation is clean and refined, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a light grey cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred background of a casual restaurant atmosphere. The portion is a single serving.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion to skillet. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cocoa powder, cumin, and chili powder. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Add cheese curd. Stir until cheese curd is mostly melted and sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Simmer 2-3 minutes to heat through.
Steam asparagus batons until tender-crisp. Arrange beside chicken.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Hearty Chicken Stew
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, hearty chicken stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Generous chunks of tender, braised chicken are nestled among substantial potato wedges and thick-cut carrot rounds. A scattering of bright green peas adds a pop of color. The rich, savory gravy coats all ingredients, appearing thick and inviting. The stew has a natural, slightly loose consistency, filling the bowl amply. The chicken is in irregular, large chunks. The potatoes are cut into robust wedges, and carrots are in thick, organic rounds. The bowl sits on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. A sturdy, everyday metal fork rests nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, suggesting a cozy, relaxed family meal. The background is gently blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks.
Peel potatoes and cut into 3 cm wedges. Peel carrots and cut into 2 cm thick rounds. Dice onion. Slice celery into 1 cm pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot oil. Brown chicken on all sides. Cook until no longer pink. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion and sliced celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Stir until smooth and thickened.
Return chicken to the pot. Add potato wedges, carrot rounds, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Stir to combine.
Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Cheddar Potato & Tomato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown Creamy Cheddar Potato & Tomato Gratin is presented in an individual oval ceramic gratin dish, set on a simple wooden table surface. The top crust is a rich golden-brown, bubbling with melted cheddar cheese, revealing tender, thinly sliced potatoes layered beneath. Interspersed within the layers are sweet, caramelized diced onions and vibrant red roasted tomato halves, offering bursts of color. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped chives provides a contrasting green accent. The dish is centered on the table, flanked by a simple white porcelain side plate and sturdy, polished silver flatware. A folded natural cotton napkin rests beside the gratin. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its comforting textures and inviting warmth in a clean, modern bistro setting. The entire dish is visible, showcasing its generous single portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot as a main course.
Pair with a simple green salad with vinaigrette.
Serve alongside roasted chicken or beef for a complete meal.
